bugs.fix: Added support to download files from more directories.

bugs.title: Packet loss caused by failure of internal hardware bus
bugs.symptoms: All or 50% of from-network packets arriving at a front panel port are dropped in hardware prior to delivery to tenant(s) running on the CPU. Packet loss is caused by CRC errors on an internal bus connecting two hardware components leading to eventual failure of the bus.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs randomly, but most commonly seen soon after bootup when packets first start to be handled by fastL4 hardware acceleration, hardware per-virtual server syn cookie protection, or AFM hardware protection.
bugs.impact: Total loss of from-network to CPU packets on r5900, r5800, and r5600 appliances, and either total loss or loss of 50% of from-network to CPU packets on r10900, r10800, and r10600 appliances. r4800, r4600, r2800, and r2600 appliances are unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the appliance and disable fastL4 acceleration, per-virtual syn cookie hardware protection, and AFM hardware protection before re-enabling ingress traffic.
bugs.fix: This issue has been corrected.

bugs.title: Nic-manager core file
bugs.symptoms: During a power down sequence the l2-agent may generate a core file. The system comes back up without any issue.
bugs.conditions: System power loss.
bugs.impact: Core file is generated.
bugs.fix: A fix has been added to detect and prevent creating an l2-agent core file during a power down.

bugs.title: Control plane starvation on a fully loaded rSeries system
bugs.symptoms: When an rSeries appliance is running to maximum capacity, and CPU load is 100%, the control plane does not get enough cycles to perform operations.
bugs.conditions: When an rSeries appliance is running to maximum capacity.
bugs.impact: The control plane does not get enough cycles to perform operations.
bugs.workaround: echo 2048 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/kubepods/cpu.shares
bugs.fix: cpu.shares is set to 2048 on boot to boost its CPU shares.

bugs.title: Tcpdump capture of packets with interface-based filtering fails on r5000 and r10000 appliances
bugs.symptoms: On r5000 and r10000, running a tcpdump as follows: appliance-1# system diagnostics tcpdump -nni 1.0 to filter packets traversing interface 1.0 only, will fail. The error seen will be "errbuf ERROR:Interface configuration failed. Please retry tcpdump: pcap_loop: Interface configuration failed. Please retry." and the client will terminate. Retrying the client will not help, contrary to the message.
bugs.conditions: Tcpdump capture is started on an r5000 and r10000 device and the option to filter packets based on an interface ("-i" option) is chosen.
bugs.impact: Tcpdump cannot work in the interface filtering mode. It will operate in the other modes; only the interface filtering option causes it to be unable to start.
bugs.workaround: 1) Start a tcpdump capture with no interface filter "system diagnostics tcpdump" or "system diagnostics tcpdump -nni 0.0" Packets will be captured from all interfaces, and further (non-interface) filters can be used to narrow down capture For example: "system diagnostics tcpdump host 1.1.1.1 and port 80" or "system diagnostics tcpdump vlan 200" 2) Restart the tcpdump container. This would make the -i option available again.

bugs.title: When configured for SNMP, the system does not properly report a sysObjectID for the F5OS system
bugs.symptoms: F5OS systems may not be detected by SolarWinds or other management systems due to the wrong sysObjectID configuration in SNMP.
bugs.conditions: SNMP
bugs.impact: F5OS systems may not be detected by SolarWinds or other management systems due to the wrong sysObjectID configuration in SNMP.
bugs.fix: The sysObjectIDs are correct now.

bugs.title: Delay in tenant deployment with tenant image corruption error
bugs.symptoms: The system posts an intermediate error message: Tenant image corrupted - Update the tenant config with proper image. This error auto-recovers within 20 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Observed intermittently while bringing up the tenant.
bugs.impact: There is a delay in tenant deployment with an intermediate error on the CLI console.

bugs.title: Diagnostics ihealth upload qkview-file does not auto-complete with available qkview file names
bugs.symptoms: The ConfD command system diagnostics ihealth upload qkview-file is not tab-expandable, and you are not presented with the list of available qkview files.
bugs.conditions: Running "system diagnostics ihealth upload qkview-file <TAB>" to see the list of available qkview files.
bugs.impact: The available qkview files are not presented using tab autocomplete.
bugs.workaround: Run "system diagnostics qkview list" to obtain the list of available qkview files, and then manually type the desired qkview file name in when using the "system diagnostics ihealth upload qkview-file" command.
bugs.fix: Pressing <TAB> after system diagnostics ihealth upload qkview-file will produce a list of available files. Entering part of the name and <TAB> will auto-complete selecting a valid and available qkview file name.

bugs.title: Allow for encrypted key with passphrase
bugs.symptoms: Currently all OpenSSL keys are of type unencrypted which means that no passphrase is needed to use them. Although the keys are encrypted in ConfD, there is an insecure element in that the keys reside on the filesystem in the clear.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: There is no support for encrypted keys with a passphrase.
bugs.fix: With this new option added, keys with a passphrase are supported.

bugs.title: Tenants fail to come up after a live upgrade from pre-1.1.0 version to 1.1.0 on the r4xxx appliances
bugs.symptoms: When a live upgrade is attempted from a pre-1.1.0 release to a 1.1.0 release on the r4xxx series of appliances, the tenants will not come up after the live upgrade. The symptoms that will be seen are: ICE driver may not load ( "lsmod | grep -i ice" will not show a line with 'ice' ), no VFs will be created, tenant deployment will fail.
bugs.conditions: -- An F5OS upgrade is performed on an r4xxx series appliance to version 1.1.0 -- The appliance was running pre-1.1.0 software -- A license is installed -- Tenants are attempted to be deployed
bugs.impact: Tenant deployment fails after live upgrade as the ICE driver is not loaded.
bugs.workaround: After the live upgrade, check that the tenant is failing to deploy. Check that "lsmod | grep -i ice" does not show a line with 'ice' reboot the system Now rerun lsmod again. This should show the ice module line.
bugs.fix: Fixed in all versions after 1.1.0.

bugs.title: MIBs directory content is not accessible
bugs.symptoms: Directory contents are not accessible from ConfD API.
bugs.conditions: When file list ConfD API is used on MIBs directory, it is showing an invalid path.
bugs.impact: Will not be able to see directory content from ConfD API.
bugs.fix: The MIBs directory content is now accessible as expected.

bugs.title: On upgrading, the correct webUI changes are not reflected
bugs.symptoms: On upgrading from one F5OS-A version to another, the appropriate webUI changes are not reflected, and the older changes still persist.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from one F5OS-A version to another.
bugs.impact: Appropriate changes with respect to the version are not reflected on the webUI.
bugs.workaround: Refreshing the containers is a known workaround using /usr/libexec/platform-deployment stop and /usr/libexec/platform-deployment start.
bugs.fix: The fix is to clean up stale volumes so that new volumes are mounted after system reboot. A --remove-orphans flag was added to docker-compose down to remove volumes which were created in the previous run of docker-compose. Also, appliance_orchestration_manager was called to stop separately, as it was using a volume called config_vlogsev, which was also being used by other containers, because it is not a part of the platform.yml file. Also docker-compose down has been added before starting service in the beginning of the platform-deployment service to handle the scenario of upgrading from broken ISO to fix ISO.

bugs.title: Request for a webUI option to clear/reset the STP mode configuration
bugs.symptoms: On the webUI STP Configuration screen, the user does not have an option to clear STP mode once they have selected an STP mode.
bugs.conditions: User should have selected an STP mode.
bugs.impact: Once the STP mode is selected, the user does not have an option on the webUI to clear the selection.
bugs.fix: Added a new disabled option in STP mode selection. Selecting it will clear the previous STP mode selection.

bugs.title: Large tar/gz/iso file download via the restconf API fails.
bugs.symptoms: Downloading large tar/gz/iso files using the restconf API results in a corrupted file.
bugs.conditions: Large tar/gz/iso file download via the restconf API.
bugs.impact: Download fails, the downloaded file is corrupted.
bugs.fix: Fixed the code to download large tar/gz/iso files.

bugs.title: F5OS with an AFM license provisioned may provide incorrect AFM stats to a BIG-IP tenant
bugs.symptoms: This is an intermittent problem where the affected BIG-IP tenant may receive incorrect statistics from the F5OS platform. This can cause the BIG-IP tenant to drop DNS traffic that should not be dropped. Typically, the BIG-IP tenant will have periods of time where it receives the correct stats, and periods where it receives incorrect stats.
bugs.conditions: All of the below must be true: -- Two or more BIG-IP tenants are deployed either on the same node in a partition or on the same appliance. -- An AFM license is installed on the F5OS platform. -- At least one tenant is receiving malformed DNS traffic.
bugs.impact: Clients that send DNS traffic to the affected BIG-IP tenant will not receive DNS responses when they should.
bugs.workaround: When AFM is provisioned for the system, deploying tenants on different nodes on a chassis based system or one tenant per appliance avoids the issue.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP tenants receive the correct platform statistics regardless of the node in which they are deployed.

bugs.title: Enhance the LACP LAG data shown under the interface to take into account lacp state of the LACP LAG member
bugs.symptoms: The data shown under the /interfaces/interface oper-state and lag-speed does not take into account the lacp state for LACP LAGs. Prior to this change, the oper-status and speed were computed only based on port oper-data. This was the original design, with the assumption that the user will collect data from lacp state and aggregate the two outputs.
bugs.conditions: Configuration of LACP LAGs.
bugs.impact: User has to collect output from two different sources to get accuracy on LACP LAG speed and oper status.
bugs.fix: After the fix, the LACP LAG data shown under the interfaces/interface takes into account both oper-status and lacp_state when computing the speed and LAG oper-status.

bugs.title: Unable to fetch appliance fan speed using SNMP
bugs.symptoms: Unable to get appliance fan RPMs using SNMP (for example, snmpget/snmpwalk).
bugs.conditions: Appliance with management IP and allowlist configuration.
bugs.impact: User cannot fetch fan RPMs using SNMP; an SNMP walk will fail.
bugs.workaround: Fan speed can be fetched using CLI.
bugs.fix: Support to fetch fan details is added to the appliance code in 1.3.0, and data can now be fetched using SNMP.

bugs.title: CLI commands are not logged in audit.log
bugs.symptoms: CLI commands from ConfD are not getting logged in audit.log.
bugs.conditions: Execute commands using the ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: CLI commands which are required for security compliance audit will not get logged in audiit.log file.

bugs.title: Host Logs in F5OS-A not being rotated
bugs.symptoms: Log files under /var/log in host-os were able to grow in GBs.
bugs.conditions: Log files under /var/log not added in logrotate.
bugs.impact: Size of log files will grow in GBs, which will consume a significant amount of hard disk space.
bugs.fix: Host Logs in F5OS-A are now being rotated as expected.

bugs.title: K3s cluster is unhealthy when the system date or time is changed
bugs.symptoms: When the system date is changed, some of the k3s cluster certificates becomes invalid, and pods enter into an unknown/non-operational state. Once the system date and time are made current, most pods will be recovered. Some of the virt-controller/virt-operator/virt-api kubevirt pods are in a failed state but tenant functionality is not affected.
bugs.conditions: System date and time is changed back and forth.
bugs.impact: Some of the k3s pods go into a failed/non-operational state.
bugs.workaround: Re-spinning the certificates will restore the pods. Delete the pods to trigger a re-spin of certificates that are in a terminating or crashed state. The orchestration manager will start the pod with a new certificate. Command to delete the pod: #kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n <name-space>
bugs.fix: Only change the system date and time when necessary.

bugs.title: Downgrade from F5OS-A 1.3.0 or later to any release before F5OS-A 1.3.0 with tenants having more than one service can cause redirects
bugs.symptoms: From F5OS-A 1.3.0 or later releases have new DAG capability to enable "dag-adjust" and "ipv6-prefix-length" settings in combination with BIG-IP tenant version 15.1.8 and later. If we downgrade F5OS-A 1.3.0 or later to older releases before F5OS-A 1.3.0 and have a BIG-IP tenant software version 15.1.8 or later, the platform creates duplicate service entries. Due to a mismatch in the DAG profile in the platform and tenant, there will be packet redirects.
bugs.conditions: Downgrading F5OS-A 1.3.0 or later to any older release before F5OS-1.3.0 with BIG-IP tenant software version 15.1.8 or later.
bugs.impact: Performance degrade due to packet redirects.
bugs.workaround: Workaround steps: 1. Backup the tenant's configuration that experienced this issue -> https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13132 2. Copy the configuration off the tenant to some other host 3. Take note of the affected tenant's partition configuration -> show running-config tenants tenant <name> 4. Delete the affected tenant in the partition 5. Recreate the tenant with the same configuration noted in step #3 6. Copy the tenant config backup taken in step #1 back to the tenant and reload the configuration

bugs.title: System controller is not responding when the disk is out of space
bugs.symptoms: System becomes unresponsive when the disk runs out of space. This could happen when multiple qkview logs are generated and stored on the disk.
bugs.conditions: When the disk runs out of space, some of the applications either stop or restart. If the application restarts, it does so improperly.
bugs.impact: The controller on which the disk has run out of space will not come up properly. A controller restart is required.
bugs.workaround: Clean up the unwanted files from the disk and trigger the controller reboot with the below options. Recovery options 1. Restarting all containers from the affected controller using "systemctl restart platform-services-deployment.service" 2. Use the CLI of another controller and reboot the standby controller using the API "system reboot controllers controller standby" command

bugs.title: Duplicate service-instance entries in chassis partition
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances, when viewing the partition service-instance entries, duplicate entries will exist for system level daemons like LACPD, L2FwdSvc, and SwRbcaster. The issue occurs rarely, and the user should only notice a cosmetic difference.
bugs.conditions: Adding blades to and removing blades from a partition may trigger the issue.
bugs.impact: Display is not correct.
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the affected partition.
bugs.fix: Duplicate service-instance entries will be removed in cases of a blade rebooting and a blade being added to a partition.

bugs.title: Logrotate parameters do not get updated by software upgrade
bugs.symptoms: If the parameters (frequency/size) for log file rotation are updated in a new software release, they are not updated on the target system during upgrade. The result is that the size of retained log messages depends on the upgrade history, not on the software version.
bugs.conditions: System that is live upgraded from any version to any other version prior to F5OS-C 1.5.0.
bugs.impact: When logfiles are collected by qkview, differing amounts of data may be gathered, perhaps omitting information that was intended to be collected.
bugs.fix: The system updates the logrotate parameters during software install, so that the setting correspond to the software version, not the upgrade history.

bugs.title: PSU status undeterminable under "show system events" output
bugs.symptoms: The "show system events" log messages are not clearly communicating PSU status.
bugs.conditions: The "show system events" command in ConfD always shows "Presence detected" when we assert and de-assert the power supply.
bugs.impact: User might not be able to conclude whether PSU is present and removed.
bugs.fix: User is now able to see "Absent" when PSU is physically removed and "Presence detected" when PSU is connected.

bugs.title: System import functionality is unstable if PXE install source is not imported
bugs.symptoms: If a VELOS controller or rSeries appliance is PXE installed with a given ISO, and that ISO is not imported manually on the controller after the installation, future imports may fail or be left in an inconsistent state.
bugs.conditions: 1. PXE install VELOS system controller or rSeries appliance 2. Fail to manually import ISO used for PXE install 3. Import other software
bugs.impact: Confusing import and upgrade failures under conditions that seem like they shouldn't produce issues.
bugs.workaround: After PXE installing a VELOS controller, make sure to manually import the ISO used for PXE install before importing any other platform software components.
bugs.fix: Better handling for cases where the ISO that is used for PXE install of VELOS controllers is not imported after the install.

bugs.title: 10G/25G/40G burst support in rSeries appliance
bugs.symptoms: When a burst of traffic at 100Gb/s is sent to a 10G/25G/40G port, the burst size supported by the rSeries appliance depends on the buffer size. Once the buffer is full, packets are dropped.
bugs.conditions: -- Use of 10G/25G/40G ports. -- A 100Gb/s burst of traffic occurs.
bugs.impact: This results in loss of egress packets.
bugs.fix: Improved the burst capability on rSeries appliances when 10G/25G/40G ports are used.

bugs.title: File download API changes to support file download from the webUI
bugs.symptoms: Header information is not effective to download files from the webUI.
bugs.conditions: X-Auth token is required to download from the webUI.
bugs.impact: Downloading files from the webUI fails.

bugs.title: Null bytes or non-ascii characters are present in velos.log
bugs.symptoms: Null bytes are created in the log files.
bugs.conditions: Abrupt restarts may cause this issue.
bugs.impact: Grep considers the log file as a binary file.
bugs.workaround: Use ‘-a’ option in grep command.

bugs.title: Status LED color always stays amber
bugs.symptoms: The status LED is always amber.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during normal operation when the status LED should be green.
bugs.impact: Status LED may not change to green when system is operational.
bugs.fix: Added a diagnostic task that periodically monitors and sets status LED color to green.

bugs.title: LOP Controller RX error: unknown
bugs.symptoms: Within the platform.log file, one can see a large number of error messages with the text including "LOP Controller RX error: unknown".
bugs.conditions: When the LOP firmware is upgraded to a recent version, new messages around the PSU PMBus have been added. When the application software is rolled back to an older version, the HAL layer no longer recognizes those messages and reports an unknown message error.
bugs.impact: The issue does not impact the operation of the product.
bugs.workaround: Updating to a more recent version of the rSeries ISO will prevent the message from showing up in the platform.log file.
bugs.fix: Update to a more recent version of the rSeries ISO.

bugs.title: Error log "Failed to execute iptable cmd: ," getting generated when trying to add same port to allow list
bugs.symptoms: When an allowed IP for the same port is added more than once, this log is generated.
bugs.conditions: Add allowed IP for the same port more than once.
bugs.impact: No impact on functionality. The function to remove the default rule, which is failing, is being called every time.
bugs.fix: The log is no longer generated.

bugs.title: Currently allowed-ip profile name is in string format. There is no restriction while configuring profile name.
bugs.symptoms: Able to create allowed IP profile name with any character (accepting all symbols and characters).
bugs.conditions: rSeries appliance
bugs.impact: allowed-ip profile name can be created with any symbols and characters.
bugs.fix: Added code to restrict allow list profile name to alphanumeric characters and special characters such as "-", "." and "_".

bugs.title: Ambiguous error message when user configures duplicate IP port combination
bugs.symptoms: A duplicate IP/port combination is not allowed in allowlist configuration. Allowlist is mainly used to allow traffic from specific source addresses. The error message is generic and does not describe the problem.
bugs.conditions: An error is displayed when the user tries to configure the same IP and port as part of two different allowlist profiles.
bugs.impact: The error message is not descriptive, and the user might not be able to identify the issue immediately.
bugs.fix: A descriptive error message is displayed on the screen, informing the user about a duplicate IP and port.

bugs.title: K3s cluster goes to unhealthy state when system is rebooted after changing hostname.
bugs.symptoms: When the system hostname is changed and the system is rebooted, all or some of the following symptoms may be encountered: -- System-related pods in K3s are stuck in a failure state. -- The K3s cluster shows more than one node. -- OMD continuously cores.
bugs.conditions: The system is rebooted after the hostname is configured in confd.
bugs.impact: -- K3s cluster goes into an unhealthy state. -- Tenant functionality is impacted.
bugs.fix: Changing the hostname via confd does not change the system hostname. Configured hostname is reflected only in the bash and confd prompts. When no hostname is configured, the bash prompt uses a default PS1 prompt.

bugs.title: WebUI does not inform users that file transfer status may take some time to return depending on various factors like network speed
bugs.symptoms: The webUI does not inform users that file transfer status may take some time to return depending on various factors like network speed, which could lead to some confusion.
bugs.conditions: Occasional delay in fetching file transfer status due to network speed and other factors.
bugs.impact: Missing clarity on file transfer success/failure.
bugs.workaround: If the user is not able to see the file transfer status immediately they will be able to see it automatically within 15 seconds, as there is continuous polling for the API.
bugs.fix: Informative text on the file import/export displays to align user expectations.

bugs.title: Removing multiple images simultaneously from the webUI causes an error
bugs.symptoms: The image removal action handler takes the input and processes it one item at a time. From the CLI/RESTCONF interface, the user can provide one image at a time. But the webUI allows the user to select multiple images and click Delete to remove them in a single click. This was creating a backend handler issue that caused the image agent to crash.
bugs.conditions: When multiple images are selected and processed for removal from the webUI.
bugs.impact: In this situation, all subsequent image removal requests cause an error: "Error: application communication failure".
bugs.workaround: The issue is fixed in F5OS-A 1.2.0. To avoid this situation in other releases of F5OS-A, the user must select one image at a time for deletion from the webUI. Restarting the image agent service recovers the system from this state.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed by improving the image removal process.

bugs.title: Tcpdump on F5OS does not capture packets of certain sizes
bugs.symptoms: When using tcpdump on the F5OS host, packets of certain sizes may not be captured via tcpdump.
bugs.conditions: Tcpdump packets less than 1501 bytes and greater than 1483 bytes as well as several other ranges are affected by this issue.
bugs.impact: Tcpdumps may be incomplete.
bugs.fix: Packets of certain sizes are no longer dropped.

bugs.title: FPGA bit files are not updated to the latest version after a live upgrade
bugs.symptoms: FPGA bit files are not updated to the latest version after a live upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Live upgrade to an ISO file.
bugs.impact: Unexpected behavior with tenant and traffic.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands from the bash prompt: 1. /bin/systemctl stop appliance_orchestration_manager_container.service 2. /bin/systemctl stop platform-services-deployment.service 3. reboot Once the system is rebooted, the correct bit files will be installed.
bugs.fix: Cleaned up the stale/old container volumes before bringing up the new containers.

bugs.title: Occasional issue observed when tenant deployed on r2xxx/r4xxx series
bugs.symptoms: The r2xxx/r4xxx appliance interface drivers are not created in time and lead to tenant deployment failure after the PXE boot, live upgrade, reboot, and port profile change.
bugs.conditions: Live upgrade from any version to v1.1.1 and PXE and on reboot and on port profile change.
bugs.impact: Occasionally tenant deployment fails to come up.

bugs.title: Database config restore failed on rSeries appliance
bugs.symptoms: System database config-restore will fail when there is mismatch in the system images between when the backup is taken and the current images present on the system.
bugs.conditions: The current system images that are present on the system (show system image) do not match the list of images that are stored in the backup file.
bugs.impact: Config restore fails.
bugs.workaround: Edit the configuration backup file and delete the <image> stanza, from: <image xmlns="http://f5.com/yang/system/image"> to </image>
bugs.fix: Configuration restore on rSeries appliances now works regardless of differences in the set of available system software images.

bugs.title: Management interface is not accessible if core system daemons are not running
bugs.symptoms: If the system management daemon (confd) is not able to run when the system starts up, the system will not configure its management IP address and will not have network connectivity.
bugs.conditions: rSeries appliance
bugs.impact: Management connectivity is lost, and the only way to access the system is via serial console.
bugs.workaround: An administrator can configure an IP address and default route for an rSeries appliance when logged in from the serial console using the "ip" command. For instance, the following commands temporarily assign a management IP address of 198.51.100.100 to the appliance, and create a default route via a gateway of 198.51.100.254. ip addr add 198.51.100.100/24 dev mgmt0-system ip route add default via 198.51.100.254
bugs.fix: Configure IP workaround.

bugs.title: After an appliance upgrade from 1.0.1 to 1.1.1, a tenant in Provisioned state may show inconsistent CLI status
bugs.symptoms: After an appliance upgrade from 1.0.1 to 1.1.1, if the running-state of a tenant is configured in the Provisioned state, the operational status of the tenant may oscillate between "Ready to deploy" and "Allocating resources to the tenant is in progress" state in the partition CLI status.
bugs.conditions: A race condition exists after an appliance upgrade from 1.0.1 to 1.1.1, that may display an inaccurate tenant operational state when the tenant is configured as Provisioned.
bugs.impact: The tenant state constantly changes.
bugs.workaround: Configure the running-state of the tenant to Deployed.

bugs.title: Customer security policy requires disabling basic authentication
bugs.symptoms: F5OS by default enables basic authentication, meaning it allows users to perform create/modify/delete Restconf operations using basic authentication.
bugs.conditions: This is observed when the user tries to perform Restconf operations(except initial login) on F5OS using a username/password (basic authentication).
bugs.impact: This basic authentication violates some of the customer security policies.

bugs.title: rSeries Appliance inoperable after powering down from Linux while configured for Appliance mode
bugs.symptoms: If the rSeries device is powered down from Linux (for example, using 'halt -p', 'poweroff', or 'shutdown -h now') while in Appliance mode, the device becomes permanently disabled. In this state, nothing external can be done to power on the Linux host, for example, cycling power, accessing the LCD Power on option, or pressing the Power button. Trying to access the AOM menu from the serial console reports the following message: AOM Command Menu - disabled for security purposes.
bugs.conditions: -- Appliance mode is enabled (this is the state the 'appliance-setup-wizard' sets when it runs to completion). -- The host is powered down (for example, using 'halt -p', 'poweroff', or 'shutdown -h now')
bugs.impact: The AOM command menu is not available to power on the host. A power cycle of the appliance does not power on the host. The disabled appliance must be replaced.
bugs.workaround: ***Important!*** If the BIG-IP rSeries appliance is configured for Appliance mode, do not power off the device using commands such as 'halt -p', 'poweroff', or 'shutdown -h now'. Instead, run 'halt' and then remove power from the system (for example, unplug, remove power brick, remove power from rack). Note: If you have already encountered this issue, contact F5 Support :: https://www.f5.com/services/support to request an RMA. For more information, refer to K12882: Overview of the F5 RMA process :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K12882 .
bugs.fix: Appliance mode no longer disables the AOM menu, allowing access to power on the host command with console access to the appliance.

bugs.title: Downgrade to 1.0.1 failed with tenant configuration
bugs.symptoms: When an appliance system has tenants configured already, attempting to downgrade to version 1.0.1 fails, and the appliance will not become operational.
bugs.conditions: During the downgrade process, the system goes for a reboot and attempts to come up in 1.0.1 release. During this bring-up process, the tenant configuration validation fails, which causes the system to fail to become operational.
bugs.impact: Downgrade to 1.0.1 is not possible if tenants are already configured.
bugs.workaround: Remove all tenants and then perform the downgrade to 1.0.1.

bugs.title: System goes into inoperative state when downgraded from 1.1.1 to 1.0.1 without moving the tenant to configured state
bugs.symptoms: The system goes into an inoperative state when it is downgraded from F5OS-A version 1.1.1 to 1.0.1 without first moving the tenant to a configured state
bugs.conditions: When downgraded from 1.1.1 to 1.0.1 without moving the tenant to the configured state
bugs.impact: System becomes inoperative.
bugs.workaround: 1. rm /var/F5/system/confd/*.cdb 2. reboot Note: This removes all the system configuration

bugs.title: ConfD encryption key can lock up the TPM module
bugs.symptoms: Due to an error that happens rarely in the HAL layer, the encryption key mechanism can misinterpret such an error as a valid identifier for the system. This causes the TPM to lock up, using that identifier, but then the actual identifier no longer unlocks the TPM.
bugs.conditions: This happens rarely but when it does, the system-manager cannot read the encryption keys and will not start ConfD. This will manifest itself as unable to start up the configuration by attempting to become admin.
bugs.impact: The system is unusable. Installing a new ISO does not help. The TPM must be cleared to become unlocked. Once the TPM is cleared, a new key is generated so existing encryptions need to be re-encrypted. This is will require that the ConfD system database be reset to default.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to do the following: # docker exec system_platform-mgr tpm2_takeownership -c # docker restart system_manager # su admin # config # (config) system database reset-to-default proceed yes # exit; exit # docker restart system_api_svc_gateway
bugs.fix: The incorrect identifier is now ignored and the lockup is avoided. Note that the fix does not unlock a locked system. The workaround will have to be applied first.

bugs.title: Common name for setup-wizard tool across platforms
bugs.symptoms: The setup-wizard tool command is named differently in F5OS-A and F5OS-C, which can be confusing for administrators of both systems.
bugs.conditions: 'appliance-setup-wizard' is used to run tool in F5OS-A bash prompt whereas 'velos-setup-wizard' is used in F5OS-C.
bugs.impact: Increases complexity and creates confusion in running the tool on device.
bugs.fix: 'setup-wizard' is made as a common command name to run the tool on both F5OS-A and F5OS-C

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenants created before F5OS-C 1.5.1 or F5OS-A 1.3.0 may be allocated a smaller disk than required
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP tenant disk space is fully used by creating multiple software volumes within the tenant, it will generate disk errors.
bugs.conditions: - A tenant originally deployed from an “ALL-F5OS” tenant image (i.e., BIGIP-15.1.6.1-0.0.10.ALL-F5OS.qcow2.zip.bundle) originally created from one of the following: -- 14.1.5 or above in the 14.1.x branch of code -- 15.1.6.1 or above in the 15.1.x branch of code - The tenant is configured to use 76G of disk space (the default)
bugs.impact: Software installs within the tenant may fail.
bugs.workaround: Beginning in F5OS-A 1.3.0, the system detects the minimum size of a disk created from a tenant image file, and enforces that minimum on newly-created tenants. If a customer has a tenant affected by this issue and upgrades their system to F5OS-A 1.3.0 or later, set the tenant to "configured", and then deploy the tenant again. If the disk size is not right, the system will show the minimum size, then adjust the tenant disk size to what is advised by the system or larger. From 1.4.0, user does not need to adjust the size unless the user needs a bigger size. The right/minimum size will be auto-allocated when the state is changed.
bugs.fix: The tenant disk size will be detected and auto-allocated.
bugs.behavior: There are two behaviors. 1.3.x: If the disk size is smaller than it has to be, it warns the user and doesn't start the tenant until the user specifies the right/minimum size. 1.4.0: It auto increases the size to the right/minimum size if the user didn't specify the disk size.

bugs.title: No options to control system power via LCD menu
bugs.symptoms: The front-panel LCD on rSeries appliances does not provide a way to control system power to the host operating system.
bugs.conditions: One of the following rSeries appliances: - r2000 / r4000 - r5000 / r10000
bugs.impact: The system LCD panel provides no way to power on/off the device.
bugs.workaround: The system power can be controlled via the AOM.
bugs.fix: The system LCD now provides a Power On control in the System menu.
bugs.behavior: In the older release, the system power can be controlled via the AOM. In the current release, it is being addressed. The system LCD now provides a Power On control in the System menu.

bugs.title: Bash history does not include timestamps for commands
bugs.symptoms: Bash 'history' does not include timestamps.
bugs.conditions: User is logged into a bash shell and runs the 'history' command.
bugs.impact: It is unclear when bash commands in 'history' were run.
bugs.fix: Bash history now includes timestamps for commands.

bugs.title: Port-profile changes when tenants are in the deployed state
bugs.symptoms: Port-profile changes are not being blocked when tenant(s) are in the deployed state.
bugs.conditions: Tenants in the deployed state
bugs.impact: Tenants may not come up after the system reboots.
bugs.workaround: The tenant running state for any tenant in the deployed state must be moved to provisioned and back to deployed. Then the tenant will come up and function properly.

bugs.title: Occational issue with tenant deployment after live upgrade on R2xx/R4xx series
bugs.symptoms: Interface drivers are not created, leading to tenant deployment failure after a live upgrade
bugs.conditions: Live upgrade from version 1.1.0 to version 1.1.1
bugs.impact: Tenant deployment fails occasionally
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the device solves the issue

bugs.title: Tagged LLDP PDUs (VLAN ID 1) are sent on appliance devices.
bugs.symptoms: VLAN ID 1 is seen in LLDP PDU coming from appliances.
bugs.conditions: LLDP is enabled and RXTX is configured to send and receive LLDP PDU.
bugs.impact: Tagged VLAN ID 1 is coming in LLDP PDU.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue by adding required VLAN at F5OS.

bugs.title: Occasionally Selinux modules are getting corrupted when the system reboots
bugs.symptoms: In rSeries appliances, if Selinux modules are corrupted -> Virt-handler pod crashes continuously. -> Tenant will be in pending state. -> Semodule file size is 0 in dir "/etc/selinux/targeted/active/modules/400/"
bugs.conditions: If interruption happens during Selinux modules building on system bootup, the interruption can be an abrupt power off.
bugs.impact: -> Virt-handler pod is crashing continuously. -> Tenant functionality is impacted.
bugs.fix: Identify and remove the corrupted Selinux files and rebuild them while the system is booting up.

bugs.title: Add or improve the reporting status of imported images
bugs.symptoms: There are no correct error messages or status is shown in the log files and in the CLI, when the non-compatible images, corrupted images, or zero-sized images are copied to the imported directories. It is difficult to determine the exact problem, as they had to examine the import directory and mount status of the ISO file being copied.
bugs.conditions: Coping zero-length, file name having special characters, corrupted or incompatible ISO files to the import directory /var/import/staging.
bugs.impact: No status is displayed in the CLI and in the log files.
bugs.fix: The log files will display the exact error messages. System events will show the cause of the error and SNMP traps are generated in the event of the error.

bugs.title: Backup and restore fails when port-profile is mismatched
bugs.symptoms: Because there will be some configuration changes between two different port-profiles, database backup and restore between two appliances with different port-profiles will fail.
bugs.conditions: Make sure both source and target appliances have the same port-profile configurations before performing a database restore.
bugs.impact: A database restore will fail when port-profile configuration is mismatched.
bugs.workaround: The target appliance where the restore is being performed should have the same port-profile as the backup database.
bugs.fix: Fix is that the target appliance where we are performing restore should have same port-profile as backup database.

bugs.title: Changing the root password in appliance mode is unlocking root account
bugs.symptoms: If the password of root is changed in appliance mode, it disables appliance mode.
bugs.conditions: Appliance mode is enabled. Root password is changed using set-password API.
bugs.impact: Appliance mode is disabled.
bugs.workaround: Toggle appliance mode to enable it again.
bugs.fix: Appliance mode is not disabled and displays a message: "Info: The password has changed but appliance mode is enabled that blocks root login."

bugs.title: appliance-orch-manager coredump
bugs.symptoms: appliance-orch-manager(omd) polls node, events and system pods status and update the status into ConfD. During K3S response processing, OMD failed to handle a few exceptions. Because of that, OMD coredump is observed.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently OMD core dumps if K3S response is not as expected.
bugs.impact: Intermittent OMD core dumps.
bugs.fix: If OMD core dumps, systemd will bring up the process automatically. No action is expected from user. However, if any OMD core dumps are observed, contact F5 support.

bugs.title: Inconsistencies with time zones displayed in controller and log files
bugs.symptoms: System logs on F5OS systems are logged in a mix of the user's configured time zone (when available: controller/appliance) and UTC, depending on which log file you look at.
bugs.conditions: If user has a time zone configured that is different from UTC, the logs may show different times for log messages.
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting and tracing issues can be difficult, as the time zones used in different logs do not match.
bugs.fix: Fixed all controller, partition, and blade docker images to be cognizant of the relevant configured time zone for either the chassis or the partition. When a partition is created, it defaults to the configured chassis time zone, but is independently configurable thereafter.

bugs.title: F5OS HAL lock up if the LCD module is not responding.
bugs.symptoms: There are rare cases where the LCD module is present, enabled, and its network link is up; however, it does not respond to requests made by the HAL. Ultimately this causes a the HAL services to become unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: There are rare cases where the LCD does not respond to requests from the HAL services. When this happens, the HAL service can get locked up.
bugs.impact: When this rare event occurs, the HAL becomes unresponsive for other devices in the system, like the AOM for example.
bugs.workaround: If this occurs, a restart of the HAL services or a reset of the system is required to clear the condition.

bugs.symptoms: When user tries to configure more than 3 DNS server entries in F5OS-A using command "system dns servers server" or from webUI, no error message is displayed. System allows only 3 DNS servers, but user will be allowed to configure more than 3.
bugs.conditions: Configure DNS server in F5OS-A using ConfD CLI or webUI.
bugs.impact: No impact. Even though user configures more than 3, system will take only 3 entries.

bugs.title: Failed upload entries displayed under CLI file transfer-operations
bugs.symptoms: Old, failed uploads continue to display in the file transfer-operations list for an unknown period of time both in CLI and GUI.
bugs.conditions: If the image upload operation fails for some unknown reason, then the failed entries are listed under both the transfer-status list and the transfer-operations list. The list under transfer-status is cleared every 24 hours, but the list under transfer-operations remains.
bugs.impact: - As old, failed uploads continue to display in the list for an unknown period of time, the list under transfer-operations is more cluttered. - There is no functional impact.
bugs.fix: All operation entries are cleared if their transfer time exceeds 24 hrs making the file transfer-operations list clutter free.

bugs.title: Data Mover lock-up causes major application traffic impact and tenant deploy failures
bugs.symptoms: Major impact to BIG-IP tenant virtual server traffic. PoolMember health monitors fluctuate up and down, or remain down. LACP LAGs may go down. Depending on which Data Mover (DM) is impacted, a subset of the BIG-IP tenant TMMs will no longer transmit packets. The LACP daemon will be unable to transmit its PDUs. /var/F5/partition<n>/log/velos.log contains messages like these at the time the problem started: blade-1(p1) dma-agent[10]: priority="Alert" version=1.0 msgid=0x4201000000000129 msg="Health monitor detected DM Tx Action Completion ring hung." ATSE=0 DM=2 OQS=3. blade-1(p1) dma-agent[10]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x4201000000000135 msg="Health monitor DM register dump requested.". blade-1(p1) dma-agent[10]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x4201000000000137 msg="Health monitor DM register dump complete." FILE="agent-dump-1666310215.txt". In the BIG-IP tenant, the tmctl sep_stats table shows high counts for tx_send_drops2 or tx_send_drops3 (over 10,000). In the output below, all of the TMMs with SEP devices on DM 2 are impacted, unable to transmit packets. # tmctl sep_stats --select=iface,dm,sep,atse_socket,tx_send_drops2,tx_send_drops3 iface dm sep atse_socket tx_send_drops2 tx_send_drops3 ------ -- --- ----------- -------------- -------------- 1/0.1 2 0 0 1180470 <-- 80068 <-- 1/0.10 2 9 0 0 33046 <-- 1/0.11 0 10 0 0 0 1/0.2 0 1 0 0 0 1/0.3 1 2 0 0 0 1/0.4 2 3 0 0 33714 <-- 1/0.5 0 4 0 0 0 1/0.6 1 5 0 0 0 1/0.7 2 6 0 0 32980 <-- 1/0.8 0 7 0 0 0 1/0.9 1 8 0 0 0 In the F5OS Partition CLI, the following command will show a high count of tx-action-ring-full drops. In the output below, DM 2 on blade-1 is impacted: default-1# show dma-states dma-state state dm-packets dm-packet * 2-3 tx-action-ring-full TX ACTION NAME DM QOS RING FULL -------------------------------- blade-1 0 2 0 0 3 0 1 2 0 1 3 0 2 2 65890377811 <-- 2 3 328664822594 <-- merged 0 2 0 0 3 0 1 2 0 1 3 0 2 2 65890377811 <-- 2 3 328664822594 <-- After encountering this, subsequent attempts to deploy a tenant may fail until the blade is recovered, since the locked-up Data Mover is unable to free the memory it is holding for the impacted tenants.
bugs.conditions: Although the exact conditions are unknown, the problem is more likely to occur when standard virtual servers are configured to mirror traffic to the peer BIG-IP. While L7 connection mirroring increases the risk, it is not a necessary condition.
bugs.impact: Significant or total loss of application traffic for BIG-IP tenant instances running on the affected blade. This impact could also affect tenant instances on other blades if the LACP LAGs are marked down. Subsequent attempts to launch a new tenant or to stop and then start an existing one may fail.
bugs.workaround: To recover a device, determine which blade is affected by looking at the start the following dma-agent log message in /var/F5/partition<n>/log/velos.log: blade-1(p1) dma-agent[10]: priority="Alert" version=1.0 msgid=0x4201000000000129 msg="Health monitor detected DM Tx Action Completion ring hung." ATSE=0 DM=2 OQS=3. ^^^^^^^ Then, reboot the blade. This will shut down all tenant instances on the blade. Once the blade boots up, the tenants should run and pass traffic normally. If the blade cannot be rebooted immediately, it may be possible to mitigate the problem for a multi-slot tenant by disabling the impacted slot to steer traffic to the remaining slots that are still healthy: # An example of disabling BIG-IP tenant slot 1 tmsh modify sys cluster default members { 1 { disabled } } Reducing the use of connection mirroring, especially for standard virtual servers, should reduce the likelihood of encountering this issue.
bugs.fix: No fix exists yet.

bugs.title: Mount command added to QKView collection
bugs.symptoms: Mount command was not provided in QKView diagnostics file.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: Mount data is currently collected, but may be missing data provided by the mount command.
bugs.workaround: Run mount command on system and copy results from device.
bugs.fix: Mount command will be executed in QKView.

bugs.title: Not able to set severity from CLI/webUI for some services.
bugs.symptoms: Not able to set severity for following services from CLI/webUI in F5OS-A. R5R10: - Utils-agent, partition-common(system-common), tcam-manager R2R4: - Utils-agent, partition-common.
bugs.conditions: Try to change severity for following services: R5R10: Utils-agent, partition-common(system-common), tcam-manager R2R4: Utils-agent, partition-common.
bugs.impact: Not able to change severity as these services are not listed in ConfD CLI as well as webUI.
bugs.fix: Severity can now be set from CLI/webUI for all services.

bugs.title: VELOS shows in the wording for "show services service " table on rSeries
bugs.symptoms: When the user runs "show services service" on rSeries: appliance-1# show services service Possible completions: 9 Service id is unique and generated by Network Manager displaylevel Depth to show | Output modifiers <cr> Possible match completions: ipv6-prefix-length Networking mask used by disaggregator algorithms tenant_name Tenant name associated with each Service tier1_dag_profile sDAG on VELOS <-- tier2_dag_profile eDAG on VELOS <-- You can see "VELOS" in the description; this text is incorrect. It should either say "rSeries" or no platform at all.
bugs.conditions: Run "show service service".
bugs.impact: No functional impact.

bugs.title: "cdb_exists failed" error logged in platform.log during boot up
bugs.symptoms: This occurs unconditionally upon every reboot. It doesn't have any functional impact.
bugs.conditions: Upon every reboot.
bugs.impact: No impact.
bugs.fix: Boot or reboot the device and check platform.log. The issue should no longer occur.

bugs.title: Copied ISO file does not have the immutable bit set after F5OS USB install
bugs.symptoms: When performing a USB install, F5OS creates the ISO file used for installation under /var/import/staging. Under certain conditions, this newly created ISO file is missing the immutable bit, allowing the file to be potentially modified or deleted while it is in use.
bugs.conditions: Perform a USB install of F5OS.
bugs.impact: New ISO file is missing the immutable bit (should show up as an 'i' in the chattr output). [root@appliance-1 ~]# lsattr /var/import/staging/ -------------e-- /var/import/staging/F5OS-A-1.1.0-7645.R5R10.iso This results in risk of the ISO file being deleted or modified while in use.
bugs.workaround: If the imported ISO file is still present in /var/import/staging, set the immutable bit on it, for example: chattr +i /var/import/staging/R5R10.1.1.1-9159.iso If the imported ISO file is missing, that is, because it was deleted or renamed: 1. Put a copy of the ISO file on the rSeries appliance named precisely the same as the original file was, for example: Copy the ISO file to the rSeries appliance, but name it "R5R10.1.1.1-9159.iso" and put it in /var/import/staging/ 2. Set the immutable bit on the file: chattr +i /var/import/staging/R5R10.1.1.1-9159.iso 3. Reboot the device.

bugs.title: WS-2021-0200 - DoS in YAML from versions v2.2.0 to v2.2.2
bugs.symptoms: YAML in versions v2.2.0 to v2.2.2 is vulnerable to a denial of service attack.
bugs.workaround: There is currently no workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: YAML v2.2.0 - v2.2.2 has been removed and upgraded to YAML v3.0.0 in F5OS-A v1.3.0 or later, which resolves WS-2021-0200.

bugs.title: LDAP config tried to configure blank bind password
bugs.symptoms: When using the CLI or older webUI, it was possible to enter an "empty" password. This would cause nslcd to be incorrectly configured.
bugs.conditions: LDAP configured. Blank LDAP bind password entered: system aaa authentication ldap bindpw ""
bugs.impact: A blank password was highly unlikely to be the intended result and would fail to work correctly when configuring authentication or talking to the LDAP server.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly set the bind password to unset: no system aaa authentication ldap bindpw
bugs.fix: Fixed authentication so any form of "empty" password results in the password being unset.

bugs.title: Improve user readability during file upload on partition or controller
bugs.symptoms: When the user starts uploading a tenant image file, the file transfer status in the image import status table displays after a few seconds rather than immediately.
bugs.conditions: On the tenant images screen, when the user has started a file upload from his local machine.
bugs.impact: User is notified of file upload status after some time, which might lead the user to think that file upload has not started until he sees the status.
bugs.fix: A new banner was added at the top of the page saying "File upload is initializing, the transfer status will appear momentarily.", which appears as soon as the user starts the file upload. After a few seconds the message on the banner will change to "File upload in progress, please do not refresh the page.", informing user that refreshing the page will cancel the upload process.

bugs.title: Live upgrade to F5OS-A-1.3.0 will not work if STP is not configured correctly.
bugs.symptoms: System database compatibility checks will fail with STP misconfigurations.
bugs.conditions: Live upgrades to F5OS-A-1.3.0 will not work if STP is not configured correctly.
bugs.impact: System database compatibility checks will fail.
bugs.workaround: STP cannot be enabled on individual LAG members. To perform a live upgrade to F5OS-A-1.3.0, the user must correct the STP configurations by removing the STP from the interface which is assigned to aggregation-id.

bugs.title: Continuous Diagnostic Controller Event Queue errors are printed in platform.log
bugs.symptoms: Flooding of logs continuously in platform.log.
bugs.conditions: Whenever the watchdog timer is closed, this issue occurs.
bugs.impact: Event Queue is getting flooded.
bugs.fix: Provided watchdog timer fix to avoid the event log flooding.

bugs.title: Uploading qkview to iHealth may fail on long iHealth user names
bugs.symptoms: When an iHealth username/email is entered into the configuration for the iHealth upload feature, if it is sufficiently long (over 16 characters), there may be an authentication error when attempting to upload.
bugs.conditions: iHealth username/email exceeds 16 characters.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload to iHealth.f5.com via F5OS-A or F5OS-C webUI.
bugs.workaround: Use the file export feature to download the qkview file from the device to a PC, and then use the PC to upload the qkview file to iHealth.f5.com.
bugs.fix: Feature has been fixed in F5OS-C 1.6.0 and F5OS-A 1.3.0.

bugs.title: Diagnostic Controller Panic messages getting logged in platform.log at startup
bugs.symptoms: On startup, receiving the Info messages from LOP for all bits and some of them are not relevant to system type. This is causing panic logs from diagnostic agent service.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only during startup.
bugs.impact: No functionality impact.
bugs.fix: Diagnostic agent will not panic and log any panic messages during the system startup.

bugs.title: webUI session timeout popup referring to browser time instead of server time
bugs.symptoms: If the browser time is not in parity with the server time then the session timeout popup is showing up early (before the token expires) or sometimes not showing up even when the token actually expires.
bugs.conditions: When the user browser and the server times are not in sync.
bugs.impact: The user sees incorrect session timeout popup or does not see session timeout popup when the token actually expires.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed and verified that the timer for the popup is set correctly.

bugs.title: USB information not available in QKView
bugs.symptoms: USB information was not available in QKView.
bugs.impact: SEs do not have sufficient data to diagnose USB issues.
bugs.workaround: Execute the lsusb command and record results.
bugs.fix: The lsusb command is now executed as part of QKView collection.

bugs.title: ldapsearch not available to use on F5OS devices
bugs.symptoms: ldapsearch is a crucial utility for troubleshooting LDAP remote authentication. However, it wasn't available on any F5OS devices, and therefore, couldn't be utilized.
bugs.conditions: The utility could not be found searching on the base OS using the command: "find / -name '*ldapsearch*'" It also could not be found within the name-service-ldap container, using the command: "docker exec -it name-service-ldap ldapsearch"
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting is made more difficult.
bugs.fix: ldapsearch has now been installed and can be accessed using the name-service-ldap container. To do this, you can run the command: "docker exec -it name-service-ldap bash".

bugs.title: F5OS config-restore with an incorrect primary-key does not produce a warning
bugs.symptoms: 'system database config-restore' does not verify that the backup file is encrypted with the same database primary-key that is currently active on the device.
bugs.conditions: Restoring a config-backup on a device with a different primary-key than when the backup was produced.
bugs.impact: System will not operate properly because it will not be able to decode encrypted secrets that control certificates, private keys, and other items. Tenants will not operate properly.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that a new config-backup is created after executing the "system aaa authentication primary-key set" command.
bugs.fix: Config-restore fails is the database primary key does not match the config backup file, and reports the primary-key hash. Reset the primary-key to match the backup file in order to restore the backup file.

bugs.title: AAA server group name and type are not displayed on ConfD
bugs.symptoms: When a server group is created on an appliance, "show system aaa server-groups" does not display the name and type of the server group.
bugs.conditions: When a AAA server group is created (LDAP/RADIUS/TACACS).
bugs.impact: appliance-1# show system aaa server-groups NAME NAME TYPE ------------------------ ldap-group - - ----> Name and type are not displayed
bugs.fix: Published the name and type of the server group created.

bugs.title: Reading data from wrong socket leads to LACPD restart.
bugs.symptoms: Reading an update from the ConfD subscription socket leads to LACPD container restart.
bugs.conditions: Reading an update from the ConfD subscription socket.
bugs.impact: This issue leads to LACPD container restart.
bugs.fix: Read data from read socket, not from subscription socket.

bugs.title: Updating LDAP configuration on Auth Settings screen on the webUI fails to preserve the existing bind password
bugs.symptoms: When the LDAP configuration on Auth Settings is updated via webUI, the unchanged/existing bind password is replaced by an empty string, resulting in LDAP authentication failure.
bugs.conditions: Modify existing LDAP configuration on Auth Settings screen.
bugs.impact: Bind password is not preserved.
bugs.workaround: One of the following: -- Use the F5OS CLI to modify authentication settings, rather than using the webUI. -- When editing authentication settings in the webUI, always re-enter the bind password.
bugs.fix: Updating LDAP configuration preserves existing/unchanged bind password, will not result in LDAP authentication failure.

bugs.title: Blank LDAP tls_key causes error
bugs.symptoms: When using the CLI or older webUI, it was possible to enter an "empty" tls_key. This would cause nslcd to be incorrectly configured.
bugs.conditions: LDAP configured. Blank LDAP tls_key entered: system aaa authentication ldap tls_key ""
bugs.impact: A blank tls_key would fail to work correctly when configuring authentication or talking to the LDAP server.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly set the bind password to unset: no system aaa authentication ldap tls_key
bugs.fix: Fixed authentication so any form of "empty" tls_key results in the tls_key being unset.

bugs.title: Ability to configure LDAP chase-referrals option
bugs.symptoms: By default, our LDAP implementation was set to chase LDAP referrals. This could be expensive and make lookups very slow in large organizations with multiple layers of LDAP servers.
bugs.conditions: LDAP enabled in very large LDAP organizations with multiple levels of servers.
bugs.impact: The default of chasing referrals in the above conditions could result in slow LDAP lookups and timeouts.
bugs.fix: A chase referrals option was added to LDAP configuration. The default is still enabled, but now it can be easily disabled: system aaa authentication ldap chase-referrals false

bugs.title: Increased interval for boot device selector hot-key 'b' acceptance after the BIOS banner
bugs.symptoms: Users may miss the boot selector hot-key 'b' at the BIOS banner because of the short interval, with the banner displayed, before boot proceeds.
bugs.conditions: Reboot of the appliance.
bugs.impact: Reboot required to catch the interval where the hot-key is accepted.
bugs.workaround: Repeatedly pressing the 'b' hotkey during BIOS POST codes will not negatively affect the BIOS POST and should fall within the 3 second interval after the banner is displayed.
bugs.fix: 'b' hot-key accept interval, after the BIOS banner is displayed, has been increased to 5 seconds.

bugs.title: telemetry.db grew to 50G and caused error "database disk image is malformed"
bugs.symptoms: As we received multiple RAS events continuously while monitoring, the telemetry.db size grew to 50G.
bugs.conditions: If the hardware is in issue state, we can see more events getting generated, which will increase the telemetry.db size.
bugs.impact: File system will not be accessible as telemetry.db is consuming more space.
bugs.workaround: Delete the telemetry.db file and restart the platform-monitor service.
bugs.fix: This fix truncates the telemetry.db to a size of 500 MB or less.

bugs.title: LDAP authentication mishandling
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances when LDAP authentication is configured, a remote user may not be authorized correctly when logging into the command line.
bugs.conditions: An improperly configured user profile. LDAP configured on F5OS.
bugs.impact: Authorization does not occur as expected.
bugs.fix: LDAP authorization works as expected.
bugs.workaround: Restrict access to the management port to trusted users.

bugs.title: Remotely authenticated user who is a member of multiple roles that include invalid roles is not allowed to log in
bugs.symptoms: Users on systems have a role assigned to them. This role is one of a predefined set which includes the admin role. A remote user with multiple roles, some of which are not in this predefined set, is configured on a remote authentication server (LDAP, tacplus or RADIUS). Such a user was treated different based on mode of access (GUI or ssh) and the remote authentication method. Sometimes the user can log in, sometimes not.
bugs.conditions: A user has to configured on a remote authentication server (LDAP, tacplus or RADIUS) with multiple group IDs, some of which are not assigned to any role in our system. That remote authentication method has to be configured as an authentication method on our system. User supplies the correct password and tries to log in. The user may or may not be allowed into the system, depending on method of access and remote authentication method.
bugs.impact: When a remote user has multiple roles which include invalid roles, the behavior of the system was inconsistent.
bugs.workaround: Removing the invalid group ID from the remote server will fix the issue.
bugs.fix: When a remote user belongs to multiple roles, some of which are invalid ones, only the valid roles are considered for authorization. Also, this is consistently done across methods of access (GUI, ssh, etc.) and across all remote authentication methods (LDAP, tacplus, RADIUS, etc.).

bugs.title: Network Manager crashes while processing an L2 Listener Request on R2x00 or R4x00
bugs.symptoms: Network Manager crashes and a core file will be generated asynchronously.
bugs.conditions: When an L2 Listener Request is received on the platform, which is not expected to be received in the case of R2x00 or R4x00 platforms.
bugs.impact: Network Manager crashes generating a core file.
bugs.fix: Network Manager no longer crashes.

bugs.title: RJ45 interface links once at 1G
bugs.symptoms: The RJ45 interfaces on F5 r2000 and r4000 platforms link at 1G only once. If the link goes down, the interfaces cannot reestablish a link at 1G.
bugs.conditions: When an RJ45 interface that is 10G/1G capable is connected to a 1G port on F5 r2000 and r4000 platforms.
bugs.impact: The RJ45 interface won't achieve a link.
bugs.workaround: To clear the no-link condition, reboot or power cycle the platform. The RJ45 link will then come up at 1G, but only once.
bugs.fix: The RJ45 interfaces on F5 r2000 and r4000 platforms are now able to re-establish a 1G link.

bugs.title: F5OS config restore fails if .iso or components vary between two devices.
bugs.symptoms: If the .iso or components in the backup file do not match the ones in the restore file, the restore operation fails with admin access denied error: Error: Database config-restore failed.
bugs.conditions: Take a config backup from one device and restore it on another device on where .iso or components vary.
bugs.impact: Configuration restore fails.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that .iso and components match when performing backup and restore between devices.

bugs.title: LDAP user with admin and operator role gets only operator permissions
bugs.symptoms: An LDAP user configured with groups for both admin and operator roles only receives operator permissions.
bugs.conditions: LDAP user configured with gidNumber assignments for both admin and operator roles.
bugs.impact: A user with this config would be assigned only operator permissions.
bugs.workaround: Only configure the gidNumber for the desired role in LDAP for the user. Do not configure multiple roles for the same user.
bugs.fix: There was an error in the NACM rules for ConfD config. The role logic has been fixed.

bugs.title: Utils-agent "Failed to delete inactive download sessions" error on startup
bugs.symptoms: After booting a device, an error message of "Failed to download inactive download session" is observed in the error logs.
bugs.conditions: Immediately after booting.
bugs.impact: Error logs are observed after booting.
bugs.fix: The log is fixed in the utils-agent to log the data only if the data is not deleted properly.

bugs.title: An iptables CLI error
bugs.symptoms: An iptables command error: [root@appliance(appliance.chassis.local) ~]# iptables -L Another app is currently holding the xtables lock. Perhaps you want to use the -w option?
bugs.conditions: When a parallel iptables query is happening, this error displays.
bugs.impact: The iptables can get disturbed. User may not be able to view the iptables.
bugs.workaround: During iptables listing, it uses DNS and reverse DNS lookup if "-n" option is not used, which will make iptables hold the lock for longer durations.
bugs.fix: Added "-n" option in all places where iptables listing is happening.

bugs.title: Error when trying to perform FIPS HSM initialization through API on F5OS-A
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS-A, if you try to perform a FIPS initialization of the HSM through the restconf API, a 502 error appears due to a timeout.
bugs.conditions: F5OS-A 1.4.0 on FIPS platforms using API endpoints for FIPS HSM initialization.
bugs.impact: FIPS initialization fails through restconf.
bugs.workaround: Use ConfD CLI for FIPS initialization.

bugs.title: Monitoring agent service is missing telemetry inputs after its restart
bugs.symptoms: When diagnostic event queue is getting flooded due to watch dog closure issue, we are seeing failure in telemetry input reload.
bugs.conditions: Only seen when the diagnostic event log gets flooded due to watch dog closure issue and followed by monitoring service restart.
bugs.impact: Diagnostic agent service will not get any latest measurements.
bugs.fix: Monitoring agent service is reloading all telemetry inputs after its restart.

bugs.title: Blank server error popup appears over unauthorized popup for operator user
bugs.symptoms: When an operator user performs any operation that makes a REST call that is unauthorized for the operator role, a blank server error popup appears behind the unauthorized popup.
bugs.conditions: When the logged in user is in an operator role and performs an unauthorized action.
bugs.impact: A blank server error popup is seen behind an unauthorized popup, which is unnecessary.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Tested that only the unauthorized popup is visible when the operator user performs any unauthorized action.

bugs.title: Tenants are stuck in Pending state with status 0/1 nodes available after upgrading to F5OS-A 1.2.0
bugs.symptoms: The system is unable to start tenants, and the tenant reports a status of "Insufficient f5.com/qat".
bugs.conditions: Might occur after an F5OS-A software upgrade or after reinstalling K3s.
bugs.impact: Tenants will not start and are unusable.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, perform one of these actions: 1. Reboot the rSeries appliance. or 2. Restart the qat-plugin process by logging into the appliance as root, and running "pkill qat-plugin".
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the qat-plugin process that prevented the system from starting tenants.

bugs.title: NSLCD does not restart if it dies or exits
bugs.symptoms: If the NSLCD process is terminated for any reason, the process is not restarted.
bugs.conditions: LDAP authentication is enabled and the NSLCD process is terminated or unexpectedly exits.
bugs.impact: LDAP authentication will be unavailable.
bugs.workaround: The process can be restarted by manually restarting the container using the command docker restart name-service-ldap.
bugs.fix: The NSLCD process will now restart if it is terminated.

bugs.title: Help text for LDAP TLS certificate check has been clarified
bugs.symptoms: The help text for LDAP tls_reqcert was not clear. This has been rectified. appliance(config)# system aaa authentication ldap tls_reqcert Possible completions: allow Session proceeds with or without server certificate, including a bad one. demand Session terminates immediately if a bad or no certificate is provided. hard This keyword is equivalent and semantically the same as demand. never The client will not request or check any server certificate. try Equivalent to allow, but the session is terminated if a bad certificate is provided.
bugs.impact: Help text was confusing.
bugs.fix: Help text has been improved.

bugs.title: LDAPS server group and StartTLS should be mutually exclusive
bugs.symptoms: If an LDAPS server group is specified with LDAP settings that specify StartTLS, LDAP authentication will not function.
bugs.conditions: LDAPS server group configured with LDAP settings specifying StartTLS.
bugs.impact: LDAP authentication will not function.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure an LDAP server group as type "LDAP over SSL" and also set the LDAP "TLS" setting to "StartTLS". Set the LDAP server group to "LDAP over TCP" if the LDAP "TLS" setting is "StartTLS".

bugs.title: Enabling LDAP may produce a log message with the usage help for the kill command
bugs.symptoms: If the nslcd process is being restarted but was not previously running, this message could be issued.
bugs.conditions: The nslcd process is being restarted because of a configuration change but was not previously running.
bugs.impact: Alarming log messages. Potential failure to restart nslcd, resulting in failures in remote authentication.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the name-service-ldap container is likely to resolve the issue.
bugs.fix: The nslcd run/start script was rewritten to make it more robust, while reducing the chance for unnecessarily alarming log messages.

bugs.title: Convey warning to user when user tries to change root user password with appliance mode enabled
bugs.symptoms: There are no issues in functionality. This is to show extra information whenever the user tries to change the root user password on Users screen on the webUI, and the appliance mode is enabled. The CLI shows a message, and webUI will also show the same message in the form of popup.
bugs.conditions: Whenever the user tries to change the root user password on the Users screen on the webUI while appliance mode is enabled, a warning popup shows up with the same information.
bugs.impact: This does not impact the functionality.
bugs.fix: Enable appliance mode and change the root user password on the Users screen, a popup shows up with the information "The password has changed but appliance mode is enabled that blocks root login."

bugs.title: System is not configured to use user-specified NTP servers by default
bugs.symptoms: The default configuration of a VELOS system is for external NTP to be disabled. This means that even if user-specified NTP servers are configured, they will not be used until the overall NTP feature is enabled. Additionally, the overall NTP enablement value is not reflected in the output of 'show running-config system ntp' in controller ConfD.
bugs.conditions: System is running with default NTP configuration and user configures an external NTP server.
bugs.impact: Behavior is confusing or concerning to users who do not realize that they need to enable NTP for their configuration to take effect.
bugs.workaround: To work around the issue, users must enable external NTP: syscon-1-active(config)# system ntp config enabled syscon-1-active(config)# commit Commit complete.
bugs.fix: System is configured to use user-specified NTP servers by default, and reports NTP enablement value in running config.

bugs.title: Potential mis-forwarding of packets caused by stale internal hardware acceleration configuration
bugs.symptoms: Because configuration entries added to the internal ePVA hardware acceleration tables may become stuck, packets arriving from front panel ports may be handled by stale entries resulting in unexpected forwarding behavior. The stale entries may also prevent TMM from offloading new connections to ePVA.
bugs.conditions: The most likely cause for entries to become stuck is either a reboot of tenant or restart of TMM while it has active connections offloaded to ePVA without also rebooting the entire appliance.
bugs.impact: Packets may be forwarded to unexpected destinations, and/or new connections are unable to be offloaded to ePVA.
bugs.workaround: Don't reboot or restart TMM without also rebooting the entire appliance.
bugs.fix: Packets are behaving as expected.

bugs.title: iHealth accepts QKView files to upload without any file extension
bugs.symptoms: QKView files without any extension failed to upload into iHealth.
bugs.conditions: If the QKView files are generated without any extension.
bugs.impact: iHealth report invalid file extension.
bugs.workaround: Generate QKView files with extension.
bugs.fix: Allow to upload QKView files to iHealth without any extension.

bugs.title: nslcd start/run script may fail or log alarming messages
bugs.symptoms: The script that watches and restarts the nslcd process could sometimes fail to do so, and would sometimes log messages that appeared alarming.
bugs.conditions: Changing authentication settings that affect nslcd.
bugs.impact: The messages were benign, but the occasional failure to restart nslcd on config change could cause authentication changes to fail to propagate to the running process.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the name-service-ldap container is likely to solve the issue.
bugs.fix: The nslcd start/run script was rewritten to minimize alarming log messages and reliably start and restart the process when expected.

bugs.title: Configuring auth server-group and server requires duplicate name/address values
bugs.symptoms: When configuring a server-group from the CLI, users were forced to enter the config name and/or the config address multiple times to successfully configure the server-group.
bugs.conditions: User is attempting to configure an auth server-group using the CLI.
bugs.impact: Configuration was unnecessarily complex and error prone.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly enter the config name or config address to complete the configuration of the server-group.
bugs.fix: Server-group only requires the config name and/or config address to be entered once to successfully configure the object.

bugs.title: CLI "show interfaces summary" command doesn't provide a summary
bugs.symptoms: The "show interfaces" command is quite cluttered when displaying the state of both physical and virtual (aggregate) interfaces, making it difficult to get a high-level summary of all interfaces. The "show interfaces interface full" command displays a confusing subset of interface states, when the intent of "full" was to display all state fields, including the duplicate "name" column.
bugs.conditions: The administrator attempts to use the "show interfaces" command to diagnose networking problems.
bugs.impact: Difficult to diagnose interface configuration/connectivity problems.
bugs.fix: The new "summary" option for "show interfaces" displays a brief subset of the most important interface state information. appliance-1# show interfaces interface state summary OPER NAME TYPE MTU ENABLED STATUS --------------------------------------------- 1.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 2.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 3.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 4.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 5.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 6.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 7.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP 8.0 ethernetCsmacd 9600 true UP mgmt ethernetCsmacd - true UP

bugs.title: "Allow IP" rule name does not have any length limit
bugs.symptoms: Allowed IP profile name does not have any length restrictions. A user is able to create a profile name with long strings.
bugs.conditions: When trying to create the allowed-ip rule and give the profile name more than 50 characters.
bugs.impact: confd need to store a rule name of any length in cdb.

bugs.title: DMA-Agent system logs preserved through system reboots
bugs.symptoms: The dma-agent log file is deleted and recreated every time the system is rebooted, this makes investigating dma-agent related issues difficult if the system had restarted since the problem occurred.
bugs.conditions: Accessing dma-agent system logs.
bugs.impact: Difficult in investigating or debugging dma-agent system logs.
bugs.workaround: Do not reboot the system in which dma-agent logs need to be investigated.

bugs.title: config-restore will cause a reboot if the portgroup configuration changes
bugs.symptoms: If config-restore causes the portgroup configuration to change, the system will reboot automatically, but no warning prompt is given.
bugs.conditions: Restoring a saved configuration with a different portgroup configuration than the current configuration.
bugs.impact: System reboots unexpectedly.
bugs.fix: System provide a warning prompt notifying of a reboot prior to it happening.

bugs.title: Qkview collects redundant log files
bugs.symptoms: Qkview collects most log files as part of its main collection, but some containers have been specified to collect log files specific to the operation of that container.
bugs.conditions: Execute system diagnostics qkview capture
bugs.impact: Redundant log files collected use extra storage space and bandwidth for transmission.
bugs.fix: Redundant log files have been scrubbed from container collection.

bugs.title: F5OS will not import system images copied with WinSCP
bugs.symptoms: F5OS will not import system images copied into /var/import/staging/ using WinSCP. The file will be present on the filesystem, but the system will not process and validate them. On older software versions (prior to F5OS-C 1.3.0 and F5OS-A 1.1.0), the image will remain stuck in an "In Queue" state.
bugs.conditions: Importing F5OS system images (F5OS-C controller and chassis partition images and F5OS-A system images) to /var/import/staging/.
bugs.impact: The images cannot be used for F5OS software installs.
