bugs.symptoms: When requesting a self-signed-cert, if the key-type is encrypted, then a passphrase is required. However, if no parameters are supplied, the key-type is then requested as a mandatory parameter, but won't ask for passphrase if encrypted type is selected.
bugs.conditions: No parameters passed to the config: system aaa tls create-self-signed-cert.
bugs.impact: An error indicates that the passphrase wasn't supplied, but it never was asked for in these conditions.
bugs.workaround: Specify key-type as a parameter and then if encrypted, the passphrase will be requested.
bugs.fix: The key-type is no longer a mandatory field and simply defaults to RSA. There is no conflict with not passing any parameters.

bugs.title: OCSP server state data and actual configured data is different in ConfD CLI
bugs.symptoms: The OCSP server data shown from non-config mode in the ConfD CLI is different from actual configured data.
bugs.conditions: - Showing state data related to OCSP server from ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: Inability to check the actual OCSP server value from non-config mode.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to run 'show running-config' from non-config mode.
bugs.fix: When the user sets new values for the OCSP server configuration, the state data is updated as well so that the user can see the actual values from non-config mode.

bugs.title: The error message is not correct when enabling client-cert (Client Certificate Authentication) before setting verify-client (Client Certificate Verification) to true
bugs.symptoms: An error on the ConfD CLI occurs when the user tries to enable Client Certificate Authentication before setting Client Certificate Verification to true. The error message given by this condition is not correct.
bugs.conditions: - User trying to enable Client Certificate Authentication when Client Certificate Verification is set to false.
bugs.impact: Due to the incorrect error message, the user is not able to enable Client Certificate Authentication.
bugs.fix: Provide a proper error message when user tries to enable Client Certificate Authentication before setting Client Certificate Verification to true.

bugs.title: Hashed/encrypted passwords are getting logged
bugs.symptoms: When the audit log entries are created with database changes, the updated values of password hashes and encrypted passwords are exposed. These values are potentially sensitive and should be masked.
bugs.conditions: Updating user passwords, server passwords, and other values that are stored as either hashes or encrypted in the configuration database.
bugs.impact: Potentially exposes sensitive information, though the encrypted fields use AES128-CFB, and the one-way hashes use SHA512, and cannot easily be converted back to plaintext form.
bugs.workaround: Secure the viewing of logs to trusted users. See the following page for more information: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K58243048
bugs.fix: These fields are now always masked during audit logging.

bugs.title: Repeated disabling and enabling of link partner interface might result in datapath corruption
bugs.symptoms: Packets received on an interface are corrupted or lost after a link partner interface is repeatedly disabled and then enabled within relatively short windows of time.
bugs.conditions: A link partner interface is repeatedly disabled and then enabled within relatively short windows of time.
bugs.impact: Dataplane services on the given interface will be inoperable.
bugs.workaround: The product must be rebooted to recover.
bugs.fix: An FPGA firmware fix was implemented to add an additional clock to an internal component that served to isolate noise between the MAC and itself.

bugs.title: Tenants are stuck in Pending state with status 0/1 nodes available after upgrading to F5OS-A 1.2.0
bugs.symptoms: The system is unable to start tenants, and the tenant reports a status of "Insufficient f5.com/qat".
bugs.conditions: Might occur after an F5OS-A software upgrade or after reinstalling K3s.
bugs.impact: Tenants will not start and are unusable.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, perform one of these actions: 1. Reboot the rSeries appliance. or 2. Restart the qat-plugin process by logging into the appliance as root, and running "pkill qat-plugin".
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the qat-plugin process that prevented the system from starting tenants.

bugs.title: Diagnostic agent stops displaying firmware update status banner even though firmware update is not complete
bugs.symptoms: The firmware update status banner is not showing in the webUI or the ConfD CLI when there is a firmware update in progress.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the firmware update is taking a long time.
bugs.impact: When the user logs onto ConfD CLI or the webUI, the firmware update status banner will not be shown.
bugs.fix: The banner now correctly displays on the ConfD CLI and the webUI when there is a firmware update in progress.

bugs.title: Unable to restore backup file containing expired TLS certificate
bugs.symptoms: If a user attempts to restore a configuration backup whose contents include a TLS certificate that has expired, the configuration restore will fail.
bugs.conditions: User attempts to restore a configuration backup file which contains an expired TLS certificate.
bugs.impact: User is unable to restore their backed up configuration.
bugs.workaround: While there is no workaround for the issue, once the backup has been collected, this can be avoided by de-configuring any TLS certificates before collecting a configuration backup, and re-setting them manually after the configuration backup has been restored.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue where configuration backup files containing expired TLS certificates could not be successfully used for configuration restore.

bugs.title: Crypto devices are not released after tenants are deleted
bugs.symptoms: Deleting the tenants does not release the crypto devices that were allocated to those tenants while creating them.
bugs.conditions: When a software upgrade was initiated incorrectly such as: 1. Upgrading only OS version 2. Upgrading only Service version
bugs.impact: Crypto devices behavior will be unexpected.
bugs.workaround: Always upgrade the software with ISO that contains the correct OS and services combination.

bugs.title: On upgrade, systems might overwrite key due to automatic firmware updating
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading to a new version (such as 1.4.0), automatic firmware updates occur, and these interfere with the encryption key retrieval, causing a new key to be generated, which blocks api-service-gateway.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading to a new version where automatic firmware updates get started at boot-up.
bugs.impact: The api-service-gateway container does not come up and there is no communication with the tenant.
bugs.workaround: Docker exec -it system_manager bash /confd/bin/confd_cmd -c "mdel /tenants/platform-self-signed-cert/self-signed-key" /confd/bin/confd_cmd -c "mdel /tenants/platform-self-signed-cert/self-signed-cert"
bugs.fix: The encryption key will not generate a new key unless the TPM module has none. The code will continue to retry until it succeeds or ConfD timeout occurs (300 seconds).

bugs.title: Docker network is not updating as part of internal IP ranges configurations
bugs.symptoms: Docker network needs to be updated as per network-range-type.
bugs.conditions: Configuring the network-range type is not affective on docker network.
bugs.impact: This bug causes docker network to not update as per network-range-type.
bugs.workaround: Edit the/etc/sysconfig/docker file manually and restart the docker.
bugs.fix: The root cause was '/etc/sysconfig/docker' getting overridden while running pre-deployment-setup. This task fixes the above issue.

bugs.title: Running RPM package should not be removed one by one without a reboot in between
bugs.symptoms: A running RPM package cannot be removed without a reboot in between.
bugs.conditions: A reboot is required in between packages removals to prevent the next package removal from failing.
bugs.impact: A running RPM package cannot be removed without a reboot in between.
bugs.workaround: Wait until the reboot happens to perform the next package removal.
bugs.fix: Until the first removal is complete, block the user from performing the next removal.

bugs.title: Config restore fails if it contains an SNMP user
bugs.symptoms: Error when restoring the config appliance-1(config)# system database config-restore name with.mgmt.snmpuser.xml A clean configuration is required before restoring to a previous configuration. Please perform a reset-to-default operation if you have not done so already. Proceed? [yes/no]: yes Error: access denied Database config-restore failed.
bugs.conditions: Backup contains an SNMP user.
bugs.impact: Cannot restore configuration.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Issue is fixed. Now the user can take a configuration backup and restore it, even with an SNMP user configured.

bugs.title: Show system health reports unhealthy during bootup
bugs.symptoms: In FIPS supported hardware, during the device boot-up, show system health report shows unhealthy due to fips-state reports -1 during boot-up.
bugs.conditions: -- during boot-up -- FIPS partition not initialized
bugs.impact: No functionality impact, it's a cosmetic issue and reports unhealthy in confd and logging.
bugs.fix: While the device is booting, the fips state starts with -1 and it shows unhealthy till the device completely boots up, but actually, the -1 state is not initialized, so updated the code that, don't report the -1 state as unhealthy.

bugs.title: IPv6 connections made through port 80 fail
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 connections made through port 80 are failing as there are no NAT rules present for port 80.
bugs.conditions: Issue is observed in all conditions.
bugs.impact: IPv6 connections through port 80 will fail.
bugs.fix: Added a NAT rule for port 80 which allows IPv6 connections.

bugs.title: Appliance Orchestration Manager core file may consume entire root filesystem
bugs.symptoms: If the Appliance Orchestration Manager daemon crashes, it may write an extremely large (~80-90 GiB) core file that consumes all of the free space on the root filesystem and causes the system to become inoperative.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: System is inoperative, and only accessible by logging in to the system command line as root: - Tenants are inoperative/inaccessible - System webUI is inaccessible - Attempts to log in to CLI as any user other than "root" fails
bugs.workaround: There is no way to avoid this issue. Once a system is affected, the system can be recovered by removing the large core file from /var/shared/core/container/ and then rebooting the system. 1. Log in to the system CLI as root and check the amount of free space on the root file system: df -h / 2. If that reports no free space, check whether there are large core files present in /var/shared core by running: du -h /var/shared/core ls -lSh /var/shared/core/container/ 3. To free up the space, remove the large "core.appliance_orch.appliance_orchestration_manager" core files from /var/shared/core/container/

bugs.title: Users are seeing prompt cannot identify you when password expires.
bugs.symptoms: When a user uses SSH to connect to the system with an expired password, the system will show a prompt indicating it cannot identify the user.
bugs.conditions: User's password has expired.
bugs.impact: Only users whose password has expired. Impact is negligible.
bugs.workaround: Reset password.
bugs.fix: The behavior is controlled through nss-pam-ldapd interactions with sshd. Now users will see the correct message indicating that the password has expired.

bugs.title: Patch releases report the wrong version in various log files.
bugs.symptoms: F5OS-A patch files are not correctly set for patch versions.
bugs.conditions: Patch version release.
bugs.impact: Patch releases falsely report it as a non-patched release in log files.

bugs.title: Some aggregation interface names can cause ethernet interfaces in LACP aggregations to be erroneously down
bugs.symptoms: One or more interfaces in LACP aggregations may be considered down when they should not be.
bugs.conditions: Internally, LACPD hashes interfaces to an integer, and some aggregation interface names hash will collide with ethernet interface name hash. Changes to the these aggregation interfaces can impact the ethernet interface.
bugs.impact: Traffic through the affected ethernet interface in LACP aggregations may be disrupted. This can cause either degraded performance or traffic failure for LACP aggregations that the interface is a member of.
bugs.workaround: Only use aggregation interface names that don't hash to the same port numbers as ethernet interfaces. In order to determine if an existing aggregation interfaces port number conflicts with an ethernet interface, review the lacpd_interface_stat table. For a VELOS partition, use the lacpd container on any blade in the partition to run tmctl. For an appliance, use system_lacpd container to run tmctl. The following example from a rSeries appliance shows the aggregation interface "vlag" with the same port number as interface 1.0 [root@appliance-1 ~]# docker exec -it system_lacpd bash [root@appliance-1 partition]# tmctl lacpd_interface_stat -s name,port_num name port_num ---- -------- 1.0 1024 10.0 10240 2.0 2048 3.0 3072 4.0 4096 5.0 5120 6.0 6144 7.0 7168 8.0 8192 9.0 9216 mgmt 43008 vlag 1024 If an aggregation interface hashes to the same port number an Ethernet interface: 1. Delete the conflicting aggregation interface 2a. You can either restart the lacpd containers or 2b. Reboot the appliance, or for VELOS reboot each blade in the partition.
bugs.fix: Aggregation interface names will never impact ethernet interfaces in a LACP aggregation.

bugs.title: LLDP is allowed to configure on interfaces when virtual wire is enabled
bugs.symptoms: LLDP is allowed to configure on interfaces although virtual wire is enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1) Enable virtual wire on interface. 2) Attach interfaces to a lag. 3) Enabled LLDP on the interfaces.
bugs.impact: When virtual wire is enabled, BIG-IP will function in transparent mode and is not expected to see interfaces on either side. With this issue, F5 interfaces will be visible when LLDP is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure LLDP on the interfaces when virtual wire is enabled.

bugs.title: Error logs while generating the qkview
bugs.symptoms: System logs following errors under platform.log while capturing qkview --- 2023-04-09T13:21:23.774606+00:00 appliance-1 tcam-manager[78]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6b01000000000007 msg="ERROR" MSG="handle_dbg_cmd_snapshot: bad tcam id 2". 2023-04-09T13:21:32.905003+00:00 appliance-1 tcam-manager[78]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6b01000000000007 msg="ERROR" MSG="handle_dbg_cmd_snapget: bad row id 512". ---
bugs.conditions: Generating a qkview
bugs.impact: The errors are false alarms, they don't have any functional impact.

bugs.title: Ping failing after removing aggregate ID from interface and adding trunk VLANs in the same commit
bugs.symptoms: Ping to self IP of tenant failing.
bugs.conditions: This issue will be observed only when tried from F5OS ConfD CLI. Removing aggregate ID and assigning trunk VLANs to an interface in the same commit from ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: Ping to self IP of tenant will fail.
bugs.workaround: From F5OS CLI 1)Remove aggregate ID from interface. 2)commit the changes. 3)Add trunk VLANs to interface and commit the changes. For example: 1)no interfaces interface 3.0 ethernet config aggregate-id 2)commit; top 3)interfaces interface 3.0 ethernet switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 3700 3800 3900 ] 4)commit
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: ISO with special characters in name will not import
bugs.symptoms: An ISO named with special characters like "()" will not be imported and gets deleted from the import directory silently.
bugs.conditions: Only when the ISO name contains special characters.
bugs.impact: User will not have any status on the imported image with a name that contains special characters.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The "show system image" API will display the status as "Import error. File name is incorrect."

bugs.title: Unable to transfer files with admin account using SCP
bugs.symptoms: Unable to copy files from a rSeries device with the admin account using SCP.
bugs.conditions: - Create a packet capture from the ConfD CLI (using system diagnostics tcpdump). - Try to copy the file with admin credentials using the SCP command.
bugs.impact: Users with admin credentials are unable to copy files using SCP.
bugs.fix: Added support for file transfer for admin users in specific directories.

bugs.title: EHF build number is not being displayed in ConfD
bugs.symptoms: The EHF build number is not being displayed in ConfD. The only thing being displayed is the type of build. There is no way to identify the build number of the EHF build.
bugs.conditions: Using 'show system image' in the CLI, there is no way to identify the build number of the EHF build.
bugs.impact: User is not able to identify the build number of the EHF build in ConfD if multiple EHF builds are present.
bugs.fix: The build number of the EHF build is now included underneath 'Type'.

bugs.title: DAGD component crashes during live upgrade or downgrade
bugs.symptoms: The DAGD component crashes occasionally during live upgrade or downgrade. However, these incidents won't affect the overall system, and the DAGD component will restart automatically without requiring any user action.
bugs.conditions: The DAGD component crashes occur rarely during live upgrade or downgrade.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on the overall health of the system.

bugs.title: Incorrect PSU mismatch indication for two Murata M1845 PSUs operating at different AC input voltages
bugs.symptoms: If two Murata M1845 AC PSUs are installed in the system and one is operating with an AC input at or above 100V and the second is operating with an AC input below 100V, then an incorrect PSU mismatch condition may occur. Use the F5OS command "show components" to view voltage details for the PSUs.
bugs.conditions: Two Murata M1845 AC PSUs, one with an AC input at or above 100V and the other with an AC input below 100V.
bugs.impact: An incorrect "PSU mismatch" condition may occur.
bugs.workaround: Ensure both Murata M1845 AC PSUs have input voltage at or above 100V or below 100V.
bugs.fix: There is no PSU mismatch for two M1845 PSUs that are operating at different AC input voltages.

bugs.title: Provide ability to manage services through systemd/docker commands from F5OS CLI
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to start/stop/check service status for systemd units or docker containers.
bugs.conditions: -- Confd CLI -- You would like to check status of specific containers
bugs.impact: You are unable to check service status for specific containers.
bugs.fix: You can now start/stop/check service status for systemd services or docker containers: system diagnostics os-utils docker [start|stop|restart] node platform service <name>

bugs.title: Allowed IP rule name, which contains all underscores, will be deleted while upgrading to F5OS-A 1.7.0 and later versions
bugs.symptoms: Customer are able to create an allowed-ip rule with a name containing all underscores, hyphens or dots, which is not readable.
bugs.conditions: Creating an allowed-ip rule with a name which contain only allowed special characters.
bugs.impact: Created allowed-ip rule, with a name containing only underscores, hyphens or dots, will be deleted during upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Customer must rename the allowed-ip rule name that contain all special characters with a name containing at least one alpha-numeric character before upgrading to F5OS-A 1.7.0 or later Versions.

bugs.title: Interface persists with removed VLAN
bugs.symptoms: When a VLAN is deleted while being referenced by an interface or LAG, it cannot be de-referenced from the interface/LAG.
bugs.conditions: Delete the VLAN before removing the VLAN from the interface.
bugs.impact: Cannot add the interface to a LAG after deleting VLAN(s) that used the interface.
bugs.workaround: Recreate the removed VLAN, then edit the interface which shows defined VLAN, remove the defined VLAN, then remove the recreated VLAN.
bugs.fix: With the fix, the user will be able to view and remove the VLAN in the Add/Edit Interface/LAG screen even if the VLAN was deleted, and thus will be able to detach it from the interface/LAG.

bugs.title: Downgrade/upgrade issues are seen because ISO has special characters in the file name
bugs.symptoms: If an F5OS-A ISO with a filename containing 'special characters' ('+ , * , ? , ^ , $ , ( , ) , [ , ] , { , } , | , ＼') is imported, and the system is downgraded/upgraded to that version, it can result in the upgrade failing and the ISO being automatically removed.
bugs.conditions: 1. Download and import an ISO with a 'special character' in its name, ex. 'F5OS-A-1.5.0-*.iso'. 2. Attempt an upgrade to the imported ISO version. 3. Upgrade will fail.
bugs.impact: An upgrade to a version of software marked as successfully imported can fail unexpectedly, requiring manual intervention to recover the system.
bugs.workaround: 1. Before performing a platform software upgrade, compare versions referenced by the "show system image" ConfD CLI command with the names of files present in the "/var/import/staging” directory. If the iso is not present in /var/import/staging but it is shown in "show system image" command output, then import again to "/var/import/staging”. 2. If there is any iso file with a name containing a special character present in "/var/import/staging” remove that version of platform software and re-import it by re-downloading the file with a name that does not include special characters. You may then attempt upgrade. 3.In-order to remove that iso file with a name containing a special characters use below command. appliance-1(config)# system image remove iso <iso version> 4.In scenarios where above command fails or not possible to use above command please follow below procedure to delete the image. * login to the device using root. * chattr -i "/var/import/staging/<iso with special characters>” * rm -rf "/var/import/staging/<iso with special characters>” Incase downgrade or upgrade failure is already happened, because this issue, follow these steps to recover the system: 1.Download another copy of the ISO with a proper name to /var/import/staging. 2.Wait for five minutes for it to import. if confd is unavailable, you can check the logs in /var/log/sw-mgmt.debug for import status. 3.Once the import is complete, reboot the system. This should recover the system.

bugs.title: Toggling lag-type can sometimes cause an F5OS LACP aggregation to pass traffic while the peer does not have LACP configured.
bugs.symptoms: An F5OS LACP aggregation can sometimes allow traffic to pass when it should not.
bugs.conditions: 1) With peer devices that cause link status to flap on aggregation configurations: Toggle F5OS aggregation lag-type from LACP, to STATIC. Toggle peer aggregation from LACP to STATIC. Toggle F5OS aggregation lag-type from STATIC to LACP. 2) Create an aggregation interface with STATIC lag-type, change the lag-type to LACP, then create a lacp interface. Configure the peer aggregation as a STATIC aggregation.
bugs.impact: Traffic will pass on an aggregation when LACP has not negotiated for affected interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Disable, then enable affected interfaces.
bugs.fix: Under no scenario will traffic pass on an interface in a LACP aggregation that has not negotiated LACP with its peer.

bugs.title: Certain tenant configuration options should be unavailable on webUI after tenant deployment
bugs.symptoms: In the "Edit Tenant Deployments" screen on the webUI, certain configuration options are not allowed after the tenant is created. Some other configurations are not allowed when the tenant is in "running" state. These options are still enabled for editing instead of being disabled.
bugs.conditions: A user edits tenant configurations that they should not be able to change once a tenant is created or in "running" state.
bugs.impact: A server error will be shown to the user if they change the configurations.
bugs.fix: The options that are not allowed to be configured cannot be edited now.

bugs.title: FIPS devices show incorrect vCPUs
bugs.symptoms: 1. The Dashboard System Summary shows 36 vCPUs rather than the actual number of vCPUs available for Tenant Deployment. 2. The Add/Edit Tenant deployments screen allows selecting up to 36 vCPUs instead of the maximum vCPUs that the platform supports.
bugs.conditions: FIPS device.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: Users can view the correct value for total vCPUs for tenant deployment on the device from the CLI using the following command: "show cluster nodes node node-1 state node-info"
bugs.fix: vCPUs information will show appropriately on the dashboard based on the platform support, and Add/Edit Tenant deployment screen will have vCPU options up to the maximum that the platform supports and not beyond that.

bugs.title: Ability to suppress the proceed warning generated when portgroup mode is changed
bugs.symptoms: When the user commits portgroup mode changes, the system generates a proceed warning to inform the user of the potential consequences.
bugs.conditions: When committing portgroup mode changes.
bugs.impact: While the proceed warning is present, the user needs to input “yes” or “no” before the transaction is committed.
bugs.fix: Now you have the option to suppress the proceed-warning for the entire system. The setting is called portgroup-confirmation-warning and can be disabled in confd with the following command: system settings config portgroup-confirmation-warning off

bugs.title: Tenants fail to come up due to abrupt power cycle
bugs.symptoms: The helper task terminates instantly due to glibc rpm corruption. The abrupt reboot has caused corruption in the container DB.
bugs.conditions: Abrupt power cycle during AFU Update.
bugs.impact: Tenant.
bugs.workaround: Uninstall and reinstall the K3S cluster.

bugs.title: VELOS Software version may not be collected consistently across platform by QKView
bugs.symptoms: The QKView version format is different as collected by F5OS-A and F5OS-C, and this is reflected when the QKView is displayed by the iHealth service.
bugs.conditions: This always occurred when capturing a QKView.
bugs.impact: Occasional parsing difficulties on the iHealth service.
bugs.workaround: Examine the /etc/PRODUCT file contained in file collection for the host subpackage.
bugs.fix: Version information format as reported in the manifest.json file within a QKView is now consistent between F5OS-A and F5OS-C.

bugs.title: Modified network prefix range for the internal addresses on rSeries
bugs.symptoms: In the older versions, the prefix shows /16. It has been modified to /12 in the current release.
bugs.conditions: In case of running below help command. $ system network config network-range-type RFC1918 prefix ? Description: The network prefix index is used to select the range of IP addresses used internally within the appliance. The network prefix should be selected such that internal appliance addresses do not overlap with site-local addresses that are accessible to the appliance. Network Prefix Index Appliance Network Range 0 10.[0-15].0.0/12 1 10.[16-31].0.0/12 2 10.[32-47].0.0/12 3 10.[48-63].0.0/12
bugs.impact: No functionality impact.

bugs.title: Display option "universal-time" is not supported
bugs.symptoms: The display option "universal-time" is a built-in third-party command that F5OS does not support.
bugs.conditions: User attempts to access the built-in third-party command "universal-time."
bugs.impact: The correct output for "universal-time" is not displayed. Proper documentation for this third-party command also cannot be found.
bugs.fix: F5OS has suppressed this display option.

bugs.title: LLDP/STPD/LACPD in rSeries is flooding SEP_POLLERR when dma-agent restarts
bugs.symptoms: Below log is flooded in platform.log when dma-agent restarts "SEP library in ERR state, sep_client_poll() returns SEP_POLLERR".
bugs.conditions: dma-agent restart.
bugs.impact: l2 functions such as LLDP/STPD/LACPD will be affected.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the device.
bugs.fix: Fixed code from flooding logs.

bugs.title: Invalid memory read in appliance orchestration manager
bugs.symptoms: "Invalid read" identified in OMD. During "show cluster events" we are hitting the code flow, where the ConfD API is reading the freed memory. It is leading to an invalid read.
bugs.conditions: Executing "show cluster events".
bugs.impact: Using a freed memory may cause unexpected behavior in the system.
bugs.fix: Code changes to address memory violations in the code.

bugs.title: LACP Mode is passive for a static trunk in tenants running r2800/r4800 platforms
bugs.symptoms: LACP Mode set to active or passive mode causes a LAG to participate in negotiation whereas a static LAG configuration does not participate in negotiation. Hence lacp-mode does not make sense for static LAG interfaces.
bugs.conditions: When a static LAG is created on a platform, and a tenant is launched with a VLAN to which the static LAG interface is associated.
bugs.impact: An LACPd daemon is running on R2800/R4800 platforms which is responsible for running LACP protocol; the tenant is not dependent on LACP mode configurations and hence there will not be any impact. This is more of a display issue where one might confuse displaying LACP mode as passive for a static LAG interface.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this behavior.

bugs.title: LCD application does not update if appliance is power-cycled during firmware update
bugs.symptoms: After an OS update, an automatic firmware update runs and attempts to update all necessary firmware images. If the appliance is power-cycled or rebooted while the LCD application is being updated, the LCD update can fail and the system will report the old firmware version.
bugs.conditions: The OS is updated and an LCD firmware update is required. During that update, the appliance is rebooted or power-cycled, causing the LCD application update not to complete.
bugs.impact: The LCD application has not been updated and needs to be updated to get the latest features and bug fixes.
bugs.workaround: After verifying that the automatic firmware update process is complete, wait at least 5 minutes, look at the file /var/F5/system/AFU_COMPLETE, look for "AFU_STATUS: FWU_DONE", restart the system allowing automatic firmware to restart, and reprogram the LCD.
bugs.fix: After updating the OS, if the LCD firmware update failed, wait at least 5 minutes and verify AFU is complete by looking at the file /var/F5/system/AFU_COMPLETE and looking for "AFU_STATUS: FWU_DONE"; restart the system allowing automatic firmware to restart and reprogram the LCD.

bugs.title: Cannot set local user password if LDAP user with same name exists
bugs.symptoms: When LDAP authentication is enabled and a user exists both on the local device and in the LDAP directory, changing the local user password may fail.
bugs.conditions: LDAP authentication is enabled. User in question exists both on the local device and in the LDAP directory.
bugs.impact: Cannot change local user password.
bugs.workaround: It is generally considered best practice to prevent username collisions between the local device and remote authentication server. Either create a new username on the local device for the user in question, or change the name of the user in the remote directory, so there is no collision.

bugs.title: LCD shutdown does not work on r2800 and r4800 platforms
bugs.symptoms: In F5OS-A versions 1.4.0 and later, the button on the LCD menu that is used to shut down the system, when pressed, does not shutdown the system.
bugs.conditions: With F5OS-A 1.4.0 or later installed, from the LCD touchscreen, click the System button. Select Shutdown from the menu. Click the Shutdown button at the 'Shutdown the system?' prompt.
bugs.impact: The LCD touchscreen is lacking functionality the user is expecting it to have.
bugs.workaround: In an external terminal, connect to the unit's AOM. Select P for "Power on/off host subsystem", and then 0 for "Turn host subsystem off". Or, if the system is off, 1 for "Turn host subsystem on"
bugs.fix: Going into the AOM menu and powering off or powering on the system works as expected and achieves the same thing as using the LCD Shutdown button.

bugs.title: Some log messages/timestamps do not observe configured timezone
bugs.symptoms: Some logfiles and timestamps report the time as UTC even when the system is configured with a non-UTC timezone.
bugs.conditions: The orchestration-manager is not aware of the configured timezone, so Openshift/Kubernetes/Ansible log files produced by this component are reported as UTC. Also, the 'user login/last login' times reported by the CLI are always in UTC.
bugs.impact: Difficult to correlate timestamps across log files.
bugs.fix: Orchestration Manager recognizes the current timezone setting, and produces all timestamps as localtime using RFC3339 format (localtime + offset). All debug logfiles produced by this component are now timezone aware. The sshd/login programs report login/last login times as localtime, not UTC. The CLI no longer (incorrectly) reports login time.

bugs.title: Loading saved configuration on BIG-IP fails if host modifications are made after "tmsh save sys config" on R2800/R4800 platforms
bugs.symptoms: Loading saved configuration on BIG-IP tenant running on R2800/R4800 fails when host has a different configurations compared to what is being loaded on the tenant. Fails with an error message similar to below: 01070257:3: Requested VLAN member (1.5) is currently a trunk member Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- rSeries 4x00 or R2x00 platform -- Configuration is backed up using tmsh -- A change is made to one or more VLANs, interfaces, trunks, or type of VLANs on the host -- The BIG-IP system loads the configuration
bugs.impact: Configuration load fails, which puts TMM into an inoperative state.
bugs.workaround: When tenant is in inoperative state because of this issue, the steps below help in recovering the system: 1. Revert the configuration on the platform related to VLANs attached to the tenant moved to INOPERATIVE state. 2. Check if reverted configuration is loaded in tenant. 3. Restart the mcpd service or reboot the tenant to bring back tenant to active state. 4. Once the tenant is back to active state, save the config using "save sys config". 5. Now subsequent reboots will not let tenant to go into INOPERATIVE state.

bugs.title: "show components component storage state disks disk state" is not auto populating
bugs.symptoms: "show components component storage state disks disk state" command does not show data. But State data is shown using cmd - “show components component storage state”.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: “show components component storage state” can be used for displaying state data.
bugs.fix: Removed the state option for disk i.e “show components component storage state disks disk state” or “show components component platform storage state disks disk state” as the data can be displayed using "show components component storage state".

bugs.title: During upgrade/downgrade, VM failed to come up and remained in pending state
bugs.symptoms: The VM went to a pending state in a series of multiple F5OS live upgrades/downgrades.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently on multiple F5OS live upgrades/downgrades.
bugs.impact: VM status shows pending.
bugs.workaround: Move the VM to the configured state and re-deploy it.

bugs.title: AAA server group Port and Type are not displayed on ConfD
bugs.symptoms: When a server group is created on an F5OS appliance, "show system aaa server-groups" does not display the Port and Type of the server group.
bugs.conditions: When a AAA server group is created (LDAP/RADIUS/TACACS).
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. Port and Type information is not displayed on ConfD: appliance-1# show system aaa server-groups NAME TYPE ADDRESS PORT ------------------------------------------- ldap-group - 10.50.5.25 -
bugs.workaround: The Port and Type information can be viewed via Web UI.

bugs.title: LAG interface status is not updated on the BIG-IP tenant
bugs.symptoms: Symptom 1: Trunk is down in tenant but the LAG is up in F5OS-A. Symptom 2: LAG is down in F5OS-A but the trunk is up in tenant.
bugs.conditions: For symptom 1: 1. Set up new rSeries device. 2. Config static LAG and VLAN. 3. Deploy new tenant. 4. In tenant, LAG will be shown as down but interfaces shown as up. 5. This happens only at initial tenant deployment. For symptom 2: 1. LAG is shown as down in F5OS-A. 2. Trunk is shown as up in tenant.
bugs.impact: Symptom 1: On r2x00/r4x00 platforms, as LAG will be in DOWN state, datapath will not be working. Symptom 2: On r2x00/r4x00 platforms, LAG status is shown as UP but it's actually DOWN on the platform. Datapath will not be UP, but as LAG is UP in tenant we expect Datapath to be UP. Symptom 3: If trunks are used for HA Group the scores associated to the trunks are not deducted from the overall health scores regardless of whether the interfaces in the trunks are up or not.
bugs.workaround: For symptom 1: Restarting "system_api_svc_gateway" service on host. #docker restart system_api_svc_gateway For symptom 2: Restarting "system_api_svc_gateway" service on host. #docker restart system_api_svc_gateway

bugs.title: The system freezes if abruptly rebooted during software upgrade process.
bugs.symptoms: The system software upgrade process freezes infinitely if the system rebooted abruptly.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs if the system is rebooted abruptly when the software upgrade is triggered.
bugs.impact: Not able to perform upgrade/downgrade to other build as the process is frozen in upgrade state.
bugs.fix: It is possible to upgrade/downgrade to a new build even after the system is frozen due to an abrupt reboot.

bugs.title: When OCSP is disabled, configurations are not accurately shown outside of 'config' mode
bugs.symptoms: When the OCSP feature is disabled, making any changes to OCSP configurations (i.e. nonce request, override-responder) are not being updated outside of 'config' mode on the ConfD CLI. When the OCSP feature is enabled, there is no issue.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when OCSP is set to 'disabled' and changes are made to the OCSP configurations. Running 'show system aaa authentication ocsp' will display incorrect information.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. User will not be able to see an accurate display of the OCSP configurations while the feature is disabled.
bugs.fix: Starting in F5OS 1.8.0, OCSP configurations are accurately displayed even if the feature is disabled.

bugs.title: webUI header shows FQDN for IP address field instead of management IP
bugs.symptoms: When user accesses F5OS webUI using FQDN, the header shows the FQDN for the IP address instead of showing the actual management IP address.
bugs.conditions: When user accesses F5OS webUI using FQDN.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on functionality. The IP address label on the login screen is renamed to Address. The header displays the management IP instead of the FQDN.
bugs.workaround: To view the management IP address, navigate to the Management IP screen.
bugs.fix: Login using FQDN shows the IP address on the header instead of the FQDN. Additionally, the IP address label on the login screen is renamed to Address.

bugs.title: Ability to change SNMPD listening port
bugs.symptoms: When using default 161 SNMP listening port, user was not able to change/configure this to another port.
bugs.conditions: snmpwalk was working only on default 161 port.
bugs.fix: Added below API to configure SNMP port. Configuration: CLI# system snmp config port <port_num> Show: CLI# show system snmp state port

bugs.title: ARP probes to rSeries management IP are answered by both mgmt and mgmt0-system
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent management connectivity issues.
bugs.conditions: ARP probers to rSeries mgmt-ip.
bugs.impact: Intermittent management connectivity issues.
bugs.workaround: A temporary workaround is to update the arp-related kernel paraments on the mgmt interface. sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.mgmt.arp_ignore=2 sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.mgmt.arp_announce=1 sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.mgmt.rp_filter=1

bugs.title: BIG-IP-Next tenant does not function correctly with incorrect vCPU core values
bugs.symptoms: When an incorrect vCPU core value is committed, the BIG-IP-Next tenant may not be fully functional.
bugs.conditions: User commits an invalid vCPU core value.
bugs.impact: The tenant may not be fully functional. However, it will still deploy and be in a 'running' state.
bugs.workaround: Use the recommended vCPU core value for tenant.

bugs.title: qkview may capture log files truncated in a reverse way
bugs.symptoms: qkview captures log files, but may truncate them if too large (greater than 100 MB). A regression was introduced such that the most recent log entries would be truncated rather than the oldest.
bugs.conditions: Collection of qkview.
bugs.impact: Log entries may be missing in qkview capture.
bugs.workaround: When running a qkview capture, specify the maxfilesize argument to 1000 (1 GB). system diagnostics qkview capture maxfilesize 1000
bugs.fix: QKview now collects the tail end of log files.

bugs.title: Large core files can cause system instability
bugs.symptoms: When a system generates and stores large core files, it can cause the system unstable.
bugs.conditions: F5OS generates a large core file.
bugs.impact: F5OS core-writing script does not check filesystem availability before writing a core file and can fill up the filesystem, causing catastrophic system instability until disk-space is reclaimed. For more information of other impacts see 1185577 - F5OS-A memory leak in ImageAgent process on rSeries hosts may affect tenant performance or lead to unexpected restarts of tenant or host https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1185577.html 1284705 - Appliance Orchestration Manager core file may consume entire root filesystem https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1284705.html 1290949 - Invalid memory read in appliance orchestration manager https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1290949.html 1327701 - Space in SNMP community/user/target name causing snmpd container restart https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1327701.html
bugs.fix: F5OS now takes into account the available filesystem space before writing a core file. If the core file is too large then it will be truncated and deleted to maintain system stability. The system log message will indicate if the core file was too large to safely write.

bugs.title: Error with 'show system image' when same image is copied into /var/import/staging
bugs.symptoms: When an image is copied into /var/import/stating system more than once, calling "show system image" will show incorrect information. The status for both images will return "error". The date and size information will also be incorrect.
bugs.conditions: Copying the same image to /var/import/staging and calling "show system image".
bugs.impact: The "show system image" command shows improper output.
bugs.fix: An image will now appear only once when "show system image" is invoked, regardless of the number of times the image is in /var/import/staging. The output is also correct now.

bugs.title: SNMP requests to the partition were failing after the platform-stats-bridge process failed
bugs.symptoms: SNMP stops working.
bugs.conditions: platform-stats-bridge stops and does not restart.
bugs.impact: SNMP requests to the partition will fail.
bugs.workaround: Reboot or docker restart platform-stats-bridge or systemctl restart platform-services-deployment.service.
bugs.fix: The platform stats bridge containers will restart if it exits due to segmentation fault.

bugs.title: Tightening controls on uploading files to F5OS
bugs.symptoms: The File Upload Manager permits arbitrary file types to be uploaded by an admin user.
bugs.conditions: -- Uploading files -- User role is admin
bugs.impact: Arbitrary file types can be uploaded.
bugs.workaround: Do not upload untrusted files to the F5OS system. Reduce access to the management plane to trusted users.
bugs.fix: Only .iso, .os, .img, and .patch files are permitted to be uploaded.

bugs.title: WebUI authentication does not follow best practices in some situations
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, the WebUI interface and RestConf requests do not follow best practices when handling authentication-related requests.
bugs.conditions: Undisclosed.
bugs.impact: Undisclosed.
bugs.workaround: Secure access to the F5OS GUI and expose only to trusted users and networks.
bugs.fix: WebUI and RestConf requests now follow best practices.

bugs.title: Occasionally diagnostic agent reports as unhealthy for unpopulated PSU_Slot in health summary and ihealth reports
bugs.symptoms: Diagnostic agent reports as unhealthy for unpopulated PSU_Slot in ihealth reports and "show system health summary" output.
bugs.conditions: Occurs only when any empty PSU slots are in the system and diagnostic agent receives PSU Input State events in different order.
bugs.impact: It causes diagnostic agent to report as unhealthy for PSU on the unpopulated slot in health summary.

bugs.title: Tcpdump capture fails
bugs.symptoms: SELinux shared label set by identifier container for the common path shared across all the containers. This issue started when node-agent container was introduced without dependency. The system repeatedly logs this message to the platform log: tcpdumpd-manager[8]: priority="Crit" version=1.0 msgid=0x5406000000000018 msg="[] global_dmaa_comm init_comm failed ret:" this=0x17c6b50 ret=3.
bugs.conditions: This issue seems to occur when downgrading a system to an affected version.
bugs.impact: Tcpdump capture fails.
bugs.workaround: This issue can be resolved by doing the following: 1. Log into the system as root 2. Edit /var/docker/config/platform.yml 3. Locate the configuration for 'tcpdumpd-manager', and replace the volume that reads: - /var/F5/system:/var/tcpdump:z with: - /var/F5/system:/var/tcpdump 4. Save the file 5. Reboot the appliance
bugs.fix: Root cause of this issue was fixed as part of ID1326157.

bugs.title: Part number and serial number of an F5OS-A system not displayed on webUI
bugs.symptoms: User cannot find the part number and the serial number of an F5OS-A system on the webUI.
bugs.conditions: A user logs onto the webUI and looks for information about their part number and their serial number.
bugs.impact: There is no way for a user to know the part number and the serial number of their system using the webUI.
bugs.fix: The part number and the serial number are now shown on the 'SYSTEM SETTINGS/General' screen in the 'System Inventory' data-table.

bugs.title: Upgrade compatibility issue from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C
bugs.symptoms: As a part of this bug fix: We are not allowing webUI banner text and color detail when webUI banner is disabled. We are only allowing to configure/show webUI banner test and color when webUI banner is enabled. After this fix, We have some upgrade compatibility issue from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C (or latest). If we enable webUI banner without providing values for color and text in 1.6.0-A/C and 1.7.0-C build and if we upgrade to latest version(1.7.0-A build and 1.8.0-C) from 1.6.0-A/C and 1.7.0-C where we cannot enable banner without text, upgrade will fail with compatibility issue.
bugs.conditions: If webUI banner is enabled without text and color details then upgrade from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C will fail with compatibility error.
bugs.impact: We will not be able to upgrade from 1.6.0-A to 1.7.0-A, 1.6.0-C to 1.8.0-C, and 1.7.0-C to 1.8.0-C with webUI banner enabled and color and text fields empty.
bugs.workaround: Either disable the webUI banner or enable the webUI banner with color and text fields.
bugs.fix: We are not allowing webUI banner's text and color details when webUI banner is disabled. We are only allowing to configure/show webUI banner's text and color when webUI banner is enabled.

bugs.title: Syslog target files do not use the hostname configured via system user interface.
bugs.symptoms: Syslog target files, for example: /var/F5/system/log/platform.log, use a fixed nodename (appliance-1) for every device as a hostname.
bugs.conditions: Viewing syslog files, especially on a remote syslog server.
bugs.impact: In a remote log collector, source IPs are the only way to differentiate among devices.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to do an iRule workaround that replaces custom strings in syslog traffic depending on the client's IP address. This iRule is applied to the virtual server on another LTM that consumes the syslog traffic and load balances. when CLIENT_DATA { switch [IP::client_addr] { "10.10.10.10" { UDP::payload replace 38 11 "ABCDC01F5OS01" } "10.10.10.20" { UDP::payload replace 38 11 "ABCDC01F5OS02" } } } Below is the example message after irule workaround. Jul 31 03:33:50 10.10.10.10 2023-07-31T07:33:50.181136+00:00 appliance-1 lacpd[1]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000046 msg="" info_str="check_if_op_modify(): new oc_if_enabled: 0 (1:Enabled 2:Disabled ... )". to this Jul 31 06:00:01 10.10.10.10 2023-07-31T10:00:01.356324+00:00 ABCDC01F5OS01 lacpd[1]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000046 msg="" info_str="check_if_op_modify(): new oc_if_enabled: 1 (1:Enabled 2:Disabled ... )". Jul 31 06:00:04 10.10.10.20 2023-07-31T10:00:04.983677+00:00 ABCDC01F5OS02 lacpd[1]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3401000000000046 msg="" info_str="check_if_op_modify(): new oc_if_enabled: 0 (1:Enabled 2:Disabled ... )".
bugs.fix: Infrastructure to use the system hostname user configuration in the syslog target logs has been added with the setting 'system logging config include-hostname'. It is enabled by default, and can be turned off if old behavior is preferred.

bugs.title: Allowing the tenant configuration with more memory than max memory in the appliance
bugs.symptoms: This will not have any functional impact. Tenant configuration will be accepted but the tenant won't be up. And we see a failure message in "show tenants" with resource allocation failed.
bugs.conditions: Configuring the tenant with the memory that is beyond the max limit.
bugs.impact: It is the faulty config for the tenant. No impact on the existing/running tenants.
bugs.workaround: Delete the config and re-configure with valid memory.

bugs.title: K3S goes down when OMD is restarted
bugs.symptoms: K3S went down and failed to come up when OMD restarted due to memory corruption.
bugs.conditions: This is caused by not having essential flags in the system. The appliance OMD is dependent on the flags inside /var/omd directory.
bugs.impact: When K3S goes down, the cluster is down, which results in service down.
bugs.workaround: When the cluster goes down due to missing flags, it can be brought back up by clearing the stale flags and tokens. Please contact F5 Support. Follow instructions in https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K08061420
bugs.fix: 1. Logs are in place if the /var/omd/ flags gets deleted or added. 2. Cluster will come up even if it is going to a bad state.

bugs.title: A remote admin user is not able to enter the ConfD config mode when logged in from SSH
bugs.symptoms: When a remote user's GID is mapped to the F5OS system's local GID, the GID mapping is not parsed correctly by the system. If the remote GID is known to the F5 system, there is no issue. For example, a mapping of the form 9000:9000 works fine. However, mapping of the form 5555:9000, 6666:9000 etc. will not work.
bugs.conditions: Local GID is being mapped to a remote GID.
bugs.impact: The admin user mapped to a remote GID cannot access the ConfD config mode.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Update the system to the version with the fix.

bugs.title: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' state when downgrading F5OS partition or appliance services from 1.6.0+ to versions below 1.6.0
bugs.symptoms: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' state when downgrading F5OS partitions or appliances from 1.6.0+ to versions below 1.6.0. If there are running tenants at the time the downgrade is attempted, it will be blocked.
bugs.conditions: A downgrade of a VELOS partition or rSeries appliance from ISO version 1.6.0+ to <1.6.0 is attempted.
bugs.impact: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' for the downgrade to succeed.
bugs.workaround: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' for the downgrade to succeed.
bugs.fix: Tenants must be moved to 'provisioned' or 'configured' state when downgrading F5OS partition or appliance services from 1.6.0+ to versions below 1.6.0

bugs.title: Unable to set local user's password if the same user exists on a remote LDAP server
bugs.symptoms: If a user exists locally (in F5OS) as well as on a remote LDAP server, and LDAP-based authentication is configured as an accepted authentication method, attempting to set the user's local password in F5OS will fail. In the ConfD CLI, an error like the following will be observed: syscon-1-active(config)# system aaa authentication users user ldap_user config set-password Value for 'password' (<string>): **************** Error: Rejected, Configured password-policy: min-length:6 required-differences:8 max-letter-repeat:3 policy applies to root:true It should be emphasized that in the case of such duplicate user definitions locally/remotely, the local user's credentials will need to be used to login even if remote authentication is preferred.
bugs.conditions: A user exists locally (in F5OS) as well as on a remote LDAP server, and LDAP-based authentication is configured as an accepted authentication method.
bugs.impact: Unable to set the local user's password.
bugs.workaround: Temporarily remove LDAP as an authentication method, set the user's password, and then re-configure the preferred authentication method(s).
bugs.fix: Fixed issue with setting a local user's password when an identically named user exists on a remote LDAP server and LDAP is enabled as an authentication method

bugs.title: tcam-manager does not support all the possible system network subnets
bugs.symptoms: The connection from the tenant (TMM) to the tcam-manager is continuously restarted. tcam-mgr logs show the wrong tenant-id and hence rejected connection from the tenant: msg="INFO" MSG="Connection from client address:10.245.3.1". msg="ERROR" MSG=" Confd access error obtaining tenant info for tenant:12291 slot:1". msg="INFO" MSG="neuron_handle_responses: dropping resp to non-existent client". TMM periodically logs neuron client errors, such as: notice hudproxy_neuron_client_closed_cb: Neuron client connection terminated notice pva_sc_frs_neuron_stopped_cb/2373: FRS SC: Neuron client stopped. notice [DDOS Neuron]Neuron daemon stopped
bugs.conditions: The 'system network' configuration is changed from its default setting in F5OS.
bugs.impact: TCAM based features don't work.
bugs.workaround: Select either the default RFC6598 subnet or any of the unaffected RFC1918 subnets.
bugs.fix: tcam-manager now correctly calculates the tenant-id for all possible system network subnets.

bugs.title: A remote LDAP user with an admin role is unable to make config changes through the F5 webUI
bugs.symptoms: When a remote user's GID is mapped to the F5OS system's local GID, the GID mapping is not parsed correctly by the system. If the remote GID is known to the F5 system, there is no issue. For example, a mapping of the form 9000:9000 works fine. However, mapping of the form 5555:9000, 6666:9000 etc. will not work.
bugs.conditions: Local GID is being mapped to a remote GID.
bugs.impact: The admin user mapped to a remote GID cannot access the ConfD config mode.
bugs.fix: Update the system to the version with the fix.

bugs.title: F5OS file download API does not work with basic authentication
bugs.symptoms: File upload and download using basic auth is not supported.
bugs.conditions: When trying to upload or download the file from F5OS using basic auth.
bugs.impact: Upload/download failed with authentication error.
bugs.fix: File download API work with basic auth and x-auth-token.

bugs.title: Error handling in F5OS file-download API
bugs.symptoms: Upon file download failure, API is returning an Apache error page that isn't an F5OS-specific error and isn't aligned with other F5OS API errors. This is a negative user experience.
bugs.conditions: Due to unhandled errors, when data not in the FormData format are passed through a Curl request, an Apache error page is thrown, misaligning from other F5OS APIs errors.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. It is a negative user experience.
bugs.fix: All errors are handled in the file-download API and aligned with other F5OS APIs errors with no more Apache error pages in error cases.

bugs.title: Tenant image tab completion will not show Next tenant images
bugs.symptoms: When user tries to deploy Next tenant, tab completion for image field will not work.
bugs.conditions: When user tries to deploy Next tenant, tab completion for image field will not work if type is not given.
bugs.impact: Tenant image tab completion will not show the Next tenant images.
bugs.workaround: Enter tenant type first and then image field. example: tenants tenant next-tenant config type BIGIP-Next image ...

bugs.title: iHealth upload not supported on F5OS-A
bugs.symptoms: The iHealth upload service has changed its authentication schema to OKTA, and requires a Client ID and Client Secret rather than a User ID and Password. Version 1.5.1 (and previous versions) of F5OS-A do not support this authentication schema.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Users will not be able to directly upload QKView files to iHealth from the appliance because of change in the authentication schema.
bugs.workaround: 1. Use the file export feature to download the QKView from the appliance to a local PC. 2. Sign on to ihealth.f5.com. 3. Use the upload feature to upload the QKView to the iHealth service.
bugs.fix: Added Client ID and Client Secret fields in the iHealth page on webUI. User can upload QKView files to iHealth.

bugs.title: Multiple CVEs in SQLite package
The "show system image" command is taking more time than expected to display the output
bugs.symptoms: The "show system image" command is taking more time than expected to display the output.
bugs.conditions: Execute the "show system image" command. Check for the CLI output.
bugs.impact: Degraded user experience when executing the "show system image" command.

bugs.title: Low mixed IPv4/IPv6 performance
bugs.symptoms: Mixed IPv4/IPv6 performance does not increase after changing the ‘PVA Offload Initial Priority’ (fastl4 profile) to ‘High’.
bugs.conditions: Mixed IPv4 and IPv6 traffic with ‘PVA Offload Initial Priority’ (fastl4 profile) set to ‘High’.
bugs.impact: Lower than expected performance of mixed IPv4 and IPv6 traffic.
bugs.fix: Lower the allowable rate of incoming broadcast/DLF packets.

bugs.title: Rapid removal and re-insertion of 10G optics may result in link failure
bugs.symptoms: An interface link remains down.
bugs.conditions: Removing and re-insertion of the SFP module within a few seconds.
bugs.impact: Interface link remains down.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: 1. After removing the SFP module, wait for 2 to 3 minutes before re-inserting the SFP module. This may not work 100% of the time. 2. Reboot the appliance.

bugs.title: The file download API is not working with the x-auth-token header
bugs.symptoms: The x-auth-token in the header of the request is not working for file download.
bugs.conditions: Try to download a file using the file download API with the x-auth-token header.
bugs.impact: The file download fails when using the file download API with the x-auth-token header.
bugs.workaround: Pass x-auth-token as part of the form-data of the API instead of in the header.

bugs.title: Add more resilience to the file download API
bugs.symptoms: If basic authentication is being used in place of the x-auth-token, then the system blocks the requests and eventually stales in the request queue.
bugs.conditions: Use of basic authentication instead of the x-auth-token causes this situation in file download.
bugs.impact: No new download requests can be made.
bugs.workaround: Restart the platform-services.

bugs.title: System does not report ISO as in use in "show system image"
bugs.symptoms: When setting the ISO within the ConfD CLI using set-version, "show system image" will not show the ISO as in use.
bugs.conditions: Using set-version within the ConfD CLI to set the ISO version. Then, running the command "show system image".
bugs.impact: Users does not know which ISO is in use. For that they have to cross correlate with OS and Service versions.
bugs.fix: A user can now see which ISO currently is in use with "show system image".

bugs.title: ICMP traffic gets received on a physical interface in r4000 and r2000 HA configured while moving the VLAN between interfaces
bugs.symptoms: ICMP traffic is not successful when pinging a tenant floating IP while a VLAN is moving between interfaces. Tcpdump shows that ICMP traffic can be observed at the physical interface but not at the virtual interface assigned to the tenant.
bugs.conditions: - r4000 or r2000 systems running BIG-IP HA Pair - Moving the VLAN between interfaces
bugs.impact: Traffic on the interface where the VLAN was configured cannot be processed by TMM.

bugs.title: For a system that has interfaces with 1GB speed, the network tab on the webUI dashboard is not showing all information
bugs.symptoms: If a system has an interface with a speed of 1GB, when the user opens the Network tab on the webUI dashboard, the data that is supposed to be shown on the system graphic (such as interface speed and operational status) are not shown.
bugs.conditions: A system that has an interface with 1GB speed.
bugs.impact: The system graphic on the Network tab of the webUI dashboard is not showing interface information.
bugs.fix: Now the code is made to handle any port speed coming from the back-end response.

bugs.title: On r2k or r4k systems, improved VF creation by adding health checks and retrials
bugs.symptoms: On r2k or r4k systems, the VFs creation process under each PF were intermittently not having relevant sysfs entries under each VF created. 1. Not all the 4VFs are created under a PF(Ex: ip link show <PF>) 2. `driver` soft link is not created for VF in sysfs 3. `net` directory is missing for VF in sysfs 4. `net` directory had no entries when creating a new VF in sysfs
bugs.conditions: When the r2k or r4k system boots up, VF creation under each PF gets triggered and checks for the VF state and retries the VF creation, if we hit any of the following: 1. Not all the 4VFs are created under a PF(Ex: ip link show <PF>) 2. `driver` soft link is not created for VF in sysfs 3. `net` directory is missing for VF in sysfs 4. `net` directory had no entries when creating a new VF in sysfs
bugs.impact: Tenant creation stalls as there are insufficient/Unready/Unhealth VFs to consume for Datapath.
bugs.workaround: Even on six retrials for about three minutes after booting the system, if the VF creation does not succeed, reboot the host system with a message(s) in /var/log/messages. "Intel NIC PFs/VFs are not ready to deploy tenant(s). Only ${valid_pf_count}/${no_of_active_pfs} PFs had valid VFs. Suggest to reboot host system. " "Intel NIC PFs/VFs are not ready to deploy tenant(s). Suggest to reboot host system."
bugs.fix: Fixed validating the VF entries in sysfs. Added finite retrials to recreate VFs, if found unhealthy. If the finite retrials, not helped recovering the VFs, suggests to reboot the host system.

bugs.title: Platform-services-deployment service does not come up when system reboots early after PXE install
bugs.symptoms: Observed that platform-services-deployment service fails to come up if the system reboots while image import is in-progress after a system PXE install.
bugs.conditions: Issue only happens after PXE install if the system reboot is triggered while image import is in-progress. The platform-services-deployment startup script was not waiting long enough to setup the env_var file by sw-mgmt.
bugs.impact: Platform-services-deployment does not come up for the system.
bugs.fix: Implemented retry mechanism in platform-services-deployment startup script which will wait for the env_var file setup by sw-mgmt service.

bugs.title: User expiration is not configurable nor viewable on the webUI
bugs.symptoms: User expiration is not configurable nor viewable on the webUI.
bugs.conditions: Trying to configure/view user expiration on webUI.
bugs.impact: The user cannot view or modify the expiry information for a system user account.
bugs.workaround: The expiry information for a user account can be viewed or configured at CLI.
bugs.fix: On the webUI the "Account Locked" widget will be replaced by the "Expiry Status" configuration which will allow locking the user in a similar fashion as the CLI.

bugs.title: Downloaded F5OS ISO file missing after reboot
bugs.symptoms: The system deletes the ISOs which are not verified. If a user reboots the system while an ISO import in progress, the ISO "fails" the verification and is deleted.
bugs.conditions: Seen if a user reboots the system while an ISO import is in progress (e.g. verifying state).
bugs.impact: ISO file will be deleted.
bugs.workaround: Download the ISO again and wait until it has been verified to reboot.
bugs.fix: There is no longer an issue with rebooting the system while an ISO import is in progress.

bugs.title: Tenant service-id mismatch between fdb mac-table and service-instance entries
bugs.symptoms: The tenant service-instances IDs are not matching with the fdb mac-table service-ids. This happens when the system attempted to read a field that does not exist in the /services table.
bugs.conditions: Configuring tenants on F5OS-A.
bugs.impact: Fails to add all the additional services of a tenant to the service instance.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for older F5OS releases. Need to upgrade to F5OS-A 1.6.0 or later.
bugs.fix: The system no longer attempts to read a field that does not exist in the /services table. The tenant service-instances IDs are now matching with the fdb mac-table service-ids.

bugs.title: Datapath is broken when LAG type is changed from LACP to Static on r2000/r4000 platforms
bugs.symptoms: On r2000 and r4000 platforms, we can create a LAG as type LACP with a BIG-IP tenant. Later, when the datapath is up and running, if we change the LAG type to Static, the datapath on the tenant is broken. The platform sends the state of the members of the LAG as DOWN and hence LAG is DOWN on the BIG-IP tenant.
bugs.conditions: When LAG type is changed from LACP to Static.
bugs.impact: Datapath is completely broken while using the LAG configured.
bugs.workaround: Bringing the DOWN members of the LAG back to UP by below configurations 1. interfaces interface <ifc name> config admin disable This will make interface to DOWN state and then move back to enabled state. 2. interfaces interface <ifc name> config admin enable
bugs.fix: Datapath no longer breaks when changing the LAG type from LACP.

bugs.title: Unable to delete the static LAG from webUI
bugs.symptoms: User is unable to use the webUI to delete the static LAG that is created through the CLI.
bugs.conditions: a) If lag is created with LACP type and later changed to STATIC. b) User is trying to delete lag from webUI. LAG can not be deleted from webUI. commands > interfaces interface lag1 aggregation config lag-type LACP > once lag1 is created change the lag1 type to STATIC
bugs.impact: LAG can not be deleted from webUI.
bugs.workaround: Delete the lag from the CLI: > no lacp interfaces interface lag2 > commit > no interfaces interface lag2 > commit

bugs.title: Command "show system health components component psu-2" results in errors
bugs.symptoms: When a second PSU is added to an R2/R4 device, the system health does not show psu-2 as a known component.
bugs.conditions: After inserting a second PSU, if a power cycle or system reboot happens, sometimes diag-agent as diag-agent is not completely up; it is missing the bmc-events generated for PSU presence and updating as not present.
bugs.impact: This will cause diag-agent to update the PSU as not present, and it will not be shown in "show system health".
bugs.workaround: Provided below platform-hal psf action as work around, which will generate bmc-events for psu-presence again. docker exec -ti platform-hal psf run POST:bmc/rearm-sensor-events sensorNumber=1 docker exec -ti platform-hal psf run POST:bmc/rearm-sensor-events sensorNumber=2
bugs.fix: Updated diag-agent to initiate bmc re-arm sensors only once diag-agent is up properly, so that it does not miss any bmc-events.

bugs.title: RSA-1024 SSH public keys should not be allowed in FIPS mode
bugs.symptoms: When logging into an F5OS or BIG-IP system that is in FIPS mode, RSA-1024 SSH public keys should not be allowed to make the connection. Users should instead be prompted for a password.
bugs.conditions: User creates a RSA-1024 SSH public key and uses it to connect to the system, while the system is in FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: The user is allowed to authenticate with the key, which should not be allowed.
bugs.fix: Users cannot authenticate with a RSA-1024 SSH public key while the system is in FIPS mode.

bugs.title: Key migration failure and potential corruption updating to 1.5.0 or later with deployed tenants
bugs.symptoms: When setting a new primary key after upgrading from an older release (such as 1.1.1 or older), where tenants are deployed, to 1.5.0 or newer, the key migration may fail. The migration failure may cause configuration database corruption for the entire system.
bugs.conditions: Tenants are deployed on release 1.1.1 or older. Upgrade to 1.5.0 or newer (including through intermediate upgrades, such as 1.1.1 -> 1.3.2 -> 1.5.1). Set new primary key.
bugs.impact: Setting a new primary key may fail. When this failure occurs, system configuration corruption may occur.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation to prevent failure: - Change all tenants to the configured state - Set a new primary key - Wait for key migration to complete - Return tenants to deployed state. Recovery for corruption: - Reset device to default configuration - Set the primary key to the known primary key for a known-good backup - Restore with known-good backup
bugs.fix: Fix known causes of database corruption on primary key migration failure. While the primary key configuration may still fail if tenants are in deployed state, it should no longer cause system corruption.

bugs.title: Users authenticated via TACACS+ cannot log in via serial console
bugs.symptoms: If remote authentication is configured to use TACACS+, users authenticated via TACACS+ cannot log in via the system serial console. SELinux errors in /var/log/audit/audit.log similar to the following: type=AVC msg=audit(1691528610.427:121): avc: denied { name_connect } for pid=13249 comm="login" dest=49 scontext=system_u:system_r:local_login_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 tcontext=system_u:object_r:reserved_port_t:s0 tclass=tcp_socket permissive=0
bugs.conditions: -- TACACS+ remote authentication. -- Attempting to log in to system via serial console.
bugs.impact: Only locally-defined users can log in to the system via serial console.
bugs.workaround: Configure the SELinux policy to allow this traffic. On a VELOS chassis, these instructions must be run on each system controller separately. 1. Connect to the F5OS system via SSH as root. 2. Examine the SELinux audit denials and confirm all of them are associated with traffic that should be allowed: grep 'denied.*name_connect.*comm="login"' /var/log/audit/audit.log > /root/login-audit-denials.log cat /root/login-audit-denials.log Remove entries from the file /root/login-audit-denials.log that you do not want to allow. 3. After confirming the contents of the file /root/login-audit-denials.log, run the following commands to create and install an SELinux policy to allow that traffic: audit2allow -M login.allowtacacs < /root/login-audit-denials.log semodule -i login.allowtacacs.pp
bugs.fix: A missing SELinux exception has been added. Users authenticated via TACACS+ are now able to log in via serial console without having to manually add the exception or turning off SELinux.

bugs.title: QAT devices not populated in ConfD
bugs.symptoms: When the tenants are deployed before a live upgrade, sometimes the tenant's QAT devices are not updated in the ConfD table after the upgrade. Hence the show command to list QAT devices does not display the devices. All other functionality is intact.
bugs.conditions: Tenant is deployed before a live upgrade.
bugs.impact: The below ConfD show command does not display the QAT devices allocated to the tenant. show cluster nodes node node-1 state cryptos tenants tenant

bugs.title: LAGs not programmed when adding VLAN to LAG
bugs.symptoms: Traffic from a LAG is not reaching the tenant.
bugs.conditions: 1) Add a VLAN to a LAG and add that VLAN to a tenant in the same commit. 2) Configuration read following blade reboot.
bugs.impact: LAGs are not programmed; traffic doesn't reach tenant.
bugs.workaround: Workaround for condition (1): Add the VLAN to the LAG, commit; then add the VLAN to the tenant.
bugs.fix: Fix usage of mutexes to prevent deadlock with LAG programming is happening in parallel with VLAN programming.

bugs.title: F5OS qat-support-pod service crashed with SIGBUS error
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, a script inside qat-support-pod cannot handle when it gets a SIGBUS signal.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently seen without any specific conditions.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, only a core file gets generated.
bugs.fix: We haven't seen this issue since the fix went in. However, since there isn't a specific use case to repro, the exact scenario can't be tested.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenants created before F5OS-A 1.3.0 may be allocated a smaller disk than required
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP tenant is created before F5OS-A 1.3.0 with default storage size, the displayed size values in "show tenants tenant" are not correct. They will be displayed as "0".
bugs.conditions: Happens when the BIG-IP tenant is created before F5OS-A 1.3.0 with default storage size and upgrades to F5OS-A 1.5.1 (or a later version).
bugs.impact: No effect on BIG-IP tenant's functionality.
bugs.workaround: From F5OS-A 1.4.0, the user does not need to adjust the size unless the user needs a bigger size. The right/minimum size will be auto-allocated when the state is changed.

bugs.title: DMA Agent crash after SEP file mapping error
bugs.symptoms: When DMA Agent is unable to map the SEP block for a newly deployed tenant it may crash during shutdown.
bugs.conditions: Insufficient resources to deploy the tenant.
bugs.impact: The crash occurs on shutdown, it has no impact.
bugs.fix: DMA Agent does not crash after a SEP mapping failure.

bugs.title: Config restore fails on system with lower size if the tenant is deployed with max size on original system
bugs.symptoms: If a tenant is deployed with maximum storage size on a system, and the same configuration is tried to restore on another system with lesser disk space compared to the original device, the configuration restore fails.
bugs.conditions: * Tenant deployed with maximum storage size. * Restoring the configuration across the devices with different disk sizes.
bugs.impact: Configuration restore fails.
bugs.workaround: Edit the configuration backup file and adjust the tenant size as per the target system. Note: There could be other workarounds.

bugs.title: F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB::diskPercentageUsed not available.
bugs.symptoms: The diskPercentageUsed OID is not available. snmpwalks/getnext of diskUtilizationStatsTable will not return diskPercentageUsed. snmpget of diskPercentageUsed will fail with a no Such instance error. snmptable of F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB:diskUtilizationStatsTable shows a question mark (?) for diskPercentageUsed.
bugs.conditions: Snmpget of diskPercentageUsed
bugs.impact: The disk percentage used statistic is not available via SNMP.
bugs.fix: Support for disk percentage used statistic is added via SNMP.

bugs.title: Observing tenant pods are stuck in pending state after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, a tenant that was deployed in an older version (e.g. 1.5.0) will not come up after upgrading. An UnexpectedAdmissionError is logged stating "Allocate failed due to rpc error: code = Unknown desc = No matching tenant., which is unexpected"
bugs.conditions: Intermittently happens when upgrading a tenant from an older version.
bugs.impact: Tenant is stuck in pending state.
bugs.fix: Tenants should now run as expected. No UnexpectedAdmissionError should be logged.

bugs.title: Tcpdump sessions are terminated when interfaces are enabled or disabled.
bugs.symptoms: All tcpdump sessions terminates abruptly when an administrator enables or disables an interface on the system, even if the interface is not participating in the tcpdump session.
bugs.conditions: When an administrator enables or disables an interface on the system.
bugs.impact: All the current running tcpdump sessions are terminated and have to be restarted.
bugs.workaround: Do not make modifications to interfaces when the tcpdump sessions are active.

bugs.title: FEC configuration support for 25G interfaces on r2000/r4000
bugs.symptoms: All previous releases of F5OS-A did not support manual FEC configuration.
bugs.conditions: The r2000/r4000 is using the 4x25G port-profile mode.
bugs.impact: Unable to manually configure forward error correction.
bugs.fix: This release adds support for manual FEC configuration for the 25G interfaces.

bugs.title: 4600 does not boot up after a shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Powering on the system does not take you back to the "System" menu
bugs.conditions: Powering on the system via the LCD UI You may briefly see a "Please wait" message which quickly disappears, after which you see the Power On menu again.
bugs.impact: The rSeries LCD power control options are unreliable and do not give adequate information about the state of powering on
bugs.fix: "System" page options with confirmation pop-ups now (correctly) navigate back to the "System" page after confirming via the pop-ups.

bugs.title: LCD "System - Power On" option may not be available immediately after system is powered off
bugs.symptoms: The "System - Power On" option on the LCD may not be available immediately after the system is powered off. It may take some time before the LCD recognizes the system has been powered off and provides access to the "Power On" option within the "System" menu.
bugs.conditions: System is powered off yet the "System - Power On" option is not available on the LCD.
bugs.impact: Power-on via the LCD will not be available until the LCD recognizes that the system is powered down and makes the "Power On" option available. As an alternative, the system may be powered on via the AOM menu.
bugs.workaround: Use the AOM menu to power on the system instead of the LCD.
