bugs.fix: Fixed in LCD UI v1.13.10 and later.

bugs.title: The output of the command "ethtool --show-priv-flags" on all interfaces needs to be collected in QKView
bugs.symptoms: Before, output from the command "ethtool --show-priv-flags" was not being collected in QKView for any of the interfaces.
bugs.conditions: The user generates a QKView file. The output of the command "ethtool --show-priv-flags" is missing in the 'Commands' section of the QKView.
bugs.impact: Having access to this command's output will help to identify if the 'vf-true-promisc-support' flag is SET/UNSET. This additional information can help the support team debug issues.
bugs.fix: Output for the command "ethtool --show-priv-flags" is now collected for each interface in the 'Commands' section of QKView.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Next tenants have different namespaces in kubectl output and 'show tenants' output
bugs.symptoms: When support for BIG-IP Next tenants was added, the processing times for creation grew quite a bit. Every time a tenant is deleted and created again with the same name, the backend processing work is only keyed by the tenant name. Therefore, it could end up executing cleanup operations on the wrong tenant id, leaving the original tenant id configuration intact on the nodes, causing collision problems for the new tenant.
bugs.conditions: Deploy a new tenant with the same name immediately after deleting the old tenant.
bugs.impact: The kubectl output will still show the information of the old tenant, but the 'show tenants' output shows the new tenant's information.
bugs.workaround: If a user wants to delete and recreate a tenant with the same name, they need to wait a few minutes after tenant deletion.

bugs.title: A vqfdm system software core file is occasionally observed on system reboot
bugs.symptoms: The line-dma-agent or vqf-dm occasionally hits a cosmetic failure state as the entire system is rebooting, leading to a core file being produced prior to shutdown. There is no problem with the state of the system.
bugs.conditions: Due to left over data on a communication buffer from the tcpdump daemon to the line-dma-agent, on live-upgrade reboot the line-dma-agent can segfault during its shutdown after the tcpdump daemon already has gone down.
bugs.impact: A core file is observed on the system after the system finishes rebooting. This will happen during an upgrade from a version that is affected by this bug. The core file can be ignored.
bugs.fix: The memory for the communication buffer between the line-dma-agent and the tcpdump daemon has been refactored so this is no longer a possibilty during shutdown. The only way this core care be seen now is if a system is live-upgrading from a version without the fix in the line-dma-agent to a new version with this fix, even then the core is completely cosmetic. Once the system is updated to a version with the fix the core will never be reproduce again on sequential upgrades/reboots.

bugs.title: Corrupted state of data plane in r5600 can result in egress packet corruption
bugs.symptoms: Networking connectivity issues, such as ARP resolution issues, high availability (HA) failures, health monitor instability, etc. Packet captures with Wireshark or tshark can be used to show bit-errors/corruption in the network packet for traffic passing through the data plane. This corruption can occur in various parts of the packet such as the MAC address, EtherType, packet checksums, etc. Corresponding spike in bad_ifh_crc_drop counter value.
bugs.conditions: Rare condition that can affect r5600 platform.
bugs.impact: Network connectivity problems on some traffic passing through the affected data plane. Could be reflected in the status of Config Sync or more health monitors down on one member of HA pair.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the r5600 to reload the bitfile. If the bitfile reload does not resolve the issue, then its most likely a hardware issue. Please work with Support on a RMA.

bugs.title: RADIUS authentication fails if F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute is not specified
bugs.symptoms: Authenticating F5OS users against an external RADIUS server fails if the server does not specify an F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute. The F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute is supposed to be optional.
bugs.conditions: F5OS system authenticating against a RADIUS server
bugs.impact: F5OS authentication fails even if the server sends back the required F5-F5OS-GID attribute.
bugs.workaround: Configure the RADIUS server to include an F5-F5OS-HOMEDIR attribute with a value of "/tmp"

bugs.title: Observed multiple containers restarting and cores generating after PXE installation
bugs.symptoms: As a result of "permission denied" errors, some containers begin crashing after a PXE installation. Core files are also generated.
bugs.conditions: Seen due to a timing issue after PXE installation. Some containers come up before they can be supported.
bugs.impact: Containers crash or functionality is impacted. Core files are generated.
bugs.workaround: Modify the /var/docker/config/platform.yml with information below: + selinux_labeler: + container_name: selinux_labeler + image: +${platform_services_registry}/system_network:1.4.14 + volumes: + - /var/F5/system:/var/F5/partition:z + labels: + f5.service.type: "system" identifier: container_name: system_latest_vers image: ${platform_services_registry}/system_network:1.4.14 + depends_on: + - selinux_labeler Then, restart the platform-services-deployment.service.
bugs.fix: Containers should not be crashing after a PXE installation now. No core files should be generated.

bugs.title: In r2000 and r4000 systems, alarm LED is not set when there are alerts raised in the system
bugs.symptoms: When system has any alarm, alarm LED will not be set, and diag-agent is not clearing all the alarms during the boot up.
bugs.conditions: Applicable for r2000 and r4000 systems.
bugs.impact: Alarm LED will not be set when system generates any alarm, and diag-agent will not clear all the alarms during the boot up.
bugs.workaround: When system generates alarms, they can be seen using ConfD.
bugs.fix: When system generates any alarm, alarm LED will be set and diag-agent will clear all the alarms while during the system boot up.

bugs.title: Unable to generate SNMP Trap for IPV6
bugs.symptoms: Generating SNMP traps for IPv6 is not working.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure SNMP traps for an IPv6 address: appliance-1# show system snmp system snmp engine-id state engine-id 80:00:2f:f4:03:00:94:a1:38:33:02 system snmp engine-id state type mac system snmp state port 5000 system snmp targets target v1_target state name v1_target state community c1 state security-model v1 state ipv6 address 2620:128:e8:49:f816:3eff:fe9:248e state ipv6 port 5011 SECURITY NAME NAME MODEL ---------------------- c1 c1 [ v1 ] 2. Try to collect SNMP traps on targeted system: [root@testvm ~]# snmptrapd -Lof 2620:128:e008:4009:f816:3eff:fe09:248e:5011 NET-SNMP version 5.7.2
bugs.impact: SNMP traps for IPv6 addresses won't work.
bugs.fix: We corrected the code for generating SNMP traps for IPv6 addresses.

bugs.title: Using UI, unable to configure the account expiry date for the user as the request is not delivered to the backend.
bugs.symptoms: Even if the user account is locked using GUI, the authentication is successful for the current user account.
bugs.conditions: Unable to configure the locking of a user account in the backend.
bugs.impact: The user account is not locked thus enabling successful authentication.
bugs.workaround: Added expiry-status to ConfD and UI to define an expiry date for a specific user account with "enabled", "locked", or <string>[YYYY-MM-DD] value. Or Add expiry-status in ConfD instead of UI to configure expiry of any user account except Admin or Root user account.
bugs.fix: Added expiry-status to configure expiry of any user account.

bugs.title: Interfaces take longer than expected to come up
bugs.symptoms: -- Interfaces take longer than expected to be marked UP (40+ seconds) -- LACP status remains down until the interfaces are marked UP
bugs.conditions: -- rSeries appliance -- F5OS-A -- 100G interfaces
bugs.impact: For SFP/QSFP interfaces: -- 25G/10G interfaces take over 10 seconds to be marked UP -- 100G interfaces take 30+ seconds to be marked UP.

bugs.title: Some nuisance messages are sent to the platform log after every authentication configuration change
bugs.symptoms: Messages similar to the following may be added to the platform log after every authentication configuration change: 2023-08-03T09:43:49.150901+00:00 appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000149 msg="System's IPv6 management address isn't configured.". 2023-08-03T09:43:49.157934+00:00 appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000092 msg="LDAP server:" server="ldap://ldapserver.example.com:389". 2023-08-03T09:43:49.157951+00:00 appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000096 msg="LDAP SSL:" ssl="off".
bugs.conditions: The user makes a change in system aaa authentication.
bugs.impact: There are nuisance messages in the platform log.

bugs.title: Manually remove root and user keys before entering Appliance Mode
Space in SNMP community/user/target name causing snmpd container restart
bugs.symptoms: When there is a space in any SNMP community/user/target name configuration, this will cause an F5OS snmpd service restart.
bugs.conditions: When there is a space in an SNMP community/user/target name configuration.
bugs.impact: F5OS snmpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the SNMP community/user/target without a space in the name.
bugs.fix: Added a space restriction in SNMP community/user/target name configuration so the user can no longer configure with a space.

bugs.title: Data path to tenant does not work with LAG on virtual wire on r12k
bugs.symptoms: Data path does not work, ping to self ip/virtual server is not working.
bugs.conditions: On r12k system > LAG is created with interfaces. > LAGs are attached to virtual-wire and virtual wire is configured on tenant. > At initial tenant deployment, data path/ping traffic does not work.
bugs.impact: Data path does not work.
bugs.workaround: Upon restart, the tenant data path/ping traffic works correctly.

bugs.title: Observing r12k interfaces going down after enabling Fast L4 mode
bugs.symptoms: Soon after enabling Fast L4 traffic, interfaces go down as traffic locks up. Example: LACP status is DOWN
bugs.conditions: The bandwidth engine component (BE2) is attached to ATSE FPGA and is used for Fast L4. The BE2 hardware initialization can fail if a serial link does not successfully complete its training sequence.
bugs.impact: The FPGA datapath locks up and cannot be recovered.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the r12k to reload the FPGAs.

bugs.title: F5OS system stopped generating tmstat snapshots
bugs.symptoms: The F5OS system is not generating the tmstat snapshots, which helps us in diagnosing issues.
bugs.conditions: System is running an affected version of F5OS software (F5OS-A 1.2.0 and above, or F5OS-C 1.6.0 and above).
bugs.impact: Impacts the supportability of the device; the support teams usually rely on the snapshots while working on field issues.

bugs.title: Slow memory leak when processing tenant telemetry
bugs.symptoms: The system will eventually run out of memory. Up until the point of service restart, the memory utilization will negatively impact running tenants, causing potential memory allocation errors.
bugs.conditions: When a BIG-IP tenant version </= 15.1.7 is running.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory utilization will impact operational performance of the F5OS and tenants.
bugs.workaround: The mitigation is to update a BIG-IP tenant version to 15.1.8 or newer, or to update to F5OS 1.5.1.

bugs.title: Tenants on rSeries system will not deploy, stuck in "Starting" state, with status "Not ready: containers with unready status: [compute]"
bugs.symptoms: Tenants fail to start. - F5OS reports the tenant status as "Starting" - F5OS reports the tenant instance status as "Not ready: containers with unready status: [compute]"
bugs.conditions: - rSeries appliance - DNS search domain for system is configured with an uppercase letter in a domain, e.g.: r5900# show system dns state search system dns state search [ Example.com ]
bugs.impact: Tenants will not start.
bugs.workaround: Modify the DNS search domain list so that all entries contain only lowercase letters. On an r2000 or r4000 series appliance, reboot the system. On an r5000 or r10000 series appliance, either reboot the system or set the tenant to a "provisioned" state and then back to "deployed".

bugs.title: Appliance Orchestration Manager fails due to memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: Appliance Orchestration Manager fails, leading to a restart of the docker container. We can observe a core as well.
bugs.conditions: There are no preconditions. It is happening to memory corruption in the systems. The issue is not consistent.
bugs.impact: OMD restarts; this will not generally disturb the tenant's functionality.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issues related to memory corruptions in the appliance Orchestration Manager.

bugs.title: Display order of interfaces/portgroups in ConfD CLI are not in numerical order
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces/portgroups are not listed in numerical order when viewing from the ConfD CLI.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when running the following commands on the ConfD CLI: show interfaces interface state oper-status show running-config portgroups portgroup
bugs.impact: Affects readability.
bugs.fix: Interfaces/portgroups are now listed in numerical order when displayed from the CLI.

bugs.title: In non-FIPS mode, added support for the SSH-RSA host key algorithm
bugs.symptoms: Not able to establish an SSH connection using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.conditions: Connect to the device from the SSH client using the SSH-RSA host key algorithm in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: The SSH connection to the device could not be established.
bugs.fix: Added SSH-RSA host key algorithm support in non-FIPS mode.

bugs.title: Missing days-valid, store, and key type logging items of a certificate
bugs.symptoms: Logging most of the certificate request fields but not logging days-valid, store, and key type fields. This was because some fields were added for the creation of the certificate and the logging was done as part of the certificate request.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: The user will still see logging of all items used in the creation of a self-signed certificate, except for a few that are not necessary for the certificate request.
bugs.workaround: Check the history and observe the values that were entered.
bugs.fix: The key type and days-valid will now be logged. The store-tls is a logic value and not loggged.

bugs.title: RADIUS user logs in through the WebUI without configuring the F5-F5OS-UID, will be disconnected after 10 minutes
bugs.symptoms: When a RADIUS user is configured without F5-F5OS-UID and then logged in through the WebUI, they will be disconnected after 10 minutes. This problem has also been observed with other remote authentication methods where the UID and GID are configured.
bugs.conditions: 1) Create a RADIUS user without F5-F5OS-UID configured 2) Logged in as the RADIUS user through WebUI
bugs.impact: If logged in as the RADIUS user through the WebUI, they will be disconnected after 10 minutes. This problem has also been observed with other remote authentication methods where the UID and GID are configured.
bugs.workaround: To avoid encountering this problem, the F5-F5OS-UID should be provided. Additionally, the UID for every user (which spans across all remote users as well as local users) should be unique (or have the same GID).
bugs.fix: UID is not defaulting to 1001 for RADIUS and TACACS+ users anymore. UID is assigned from the range 40,000 - 65,000 for remote users.

bugs.title: When MAC masquerade is enabled on r5k/r10k/r12k systems with a live upgrade, an FDB entry is seen on Active and Standby
bugs.symptoms: When a MAC masquerade address is configured on BIG-IP in R5K/R10K/R12K based systems and a live upgrade of F5OS is done, an FDB entry can be seen in both Active F5OS appliance as well as Standby: f5-appliance-active# show fdb NDI MAC ADDRESS VLAN TAG TYPE VLAN TAG TYPE VID ENTRY TYPE OWNER AGE ID SVC VTC SEP DMS DID CMDS MIRRORING INTERFACE ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 00:94:a1:ab:cd:ef 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2b - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - - 02:94:a1:ab:cd:ee 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2b - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - - f5-appliance-standby# show fdb NDI MAC ADDRESS VLAN TAG TYPE VLAN TAG TYPE VID ENTRY TYPE OWNER AGE ID SVC VTC SEP DMS DID CMDS MIRRORING INTERFACE ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 00:94:a1:ab:ee:ef 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2a - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - - 02:94:a1:ab:cd:ee 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2a - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - -
bugs.conditions: On r5k/r10K/r12K systems where BIG-IP is configured in HA mode and MAC masquerading is addressed and configured, and F5OS is upgraded.
bugs.impact: Active and Standby act as if they are the owners of Floating MAC and IP.
bugs.workaround: From Standby system remove fdb entry from confd. f5-appliance-standby# show fdb NDI MAC ADDRESS VLAN TAG TYPE VLAN TAG TYPE VID ENTRY TYPE OWNER AGE ID SVC VTC SEP DMS DID CMDS MIRRORING INTERFACE ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 00:94:a1:ab:cd:ef 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2b - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - - 02:94:a1:ab:cd:ee 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2b - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - - f5-appliance-standby(config)# no fdb mac-table entries entry 02:94:a1:ab:cd:ee 3920 tag_type_vid f5-appliance-standby(config)# comm Commit complete. f5-appliance-standby# show fdb NDI MAC ADDRESS VLAN TAG TYPE VLAN TAG TYPE VID ENTRY TYPE OWNER AGE ID SVC VTC SEP DMS DID CMDS MIRRORING INTERFACE ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 00:94:a1:ab:ee:ef 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 tag_type_vid 3920 L2-LISTENER vm2a - 4095 9 - - - - 1 - -

bugs.title: Port Mappings screen on webUI displays "GB" for bandwidth instead of "Gb"
bugs.symptoms: When a user navigates to the "Port Mappings" screen on the webUI, Capacity Bandwidth and Allocated Bandwidth incorrectly display "GB" as the units. It should be "Gb" [gigabit].
bugs.conditions: Going to the "Port Mappings" screen on the webUI.
bugs.impact: This does not affect the functionality. Capacity Bandwidth and Allocated Bandwidth values are correct except for the units.
bugs.fix: The "Port Mappings" screen now displays appropriate units for Capacity Bandwidth and Allocated Bandwidth, correcting the representation to "Gb."

bugs.title: LLDP neighbors are not getting discovered
bugs.symptoms: When a user configures LLDP at one time, the LLDP details will not show up.
bugs.conditions: Configure LLDP interfaces at one time.
bugs.impact: The "show lldp" command will not show neighbor details even if the interfaces/ports are connected to a peer switch.
bugs.workaround: The issue arises when all LLDP interfaces are configured at one time. However, if the LLDP interfaces are disabled and then enabled one by one, the issue is generally not observed.
bugs.fix: The issue arises when all LLDP interfaces are configured at one time. However, if the LLDP interfaces are disabled and then enabled one by one, the issue is generally not observed.

bugs.title: Interfaces removed from LACP trunk due to traffic congestion
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces repeatedly removed and added to a LACP LAG due to dropped LACP PDUs.
bugs.conditions: High traffic volume resulting in weighted-random-early-drop (WRED) being invoked.
bugs.impact: LACP PDUs dropped resulting in loss of LACP state.
bugs.workaround: Reboot affected blade.
bugs.fix: Adjust traffic management settings for Class-of-Service '0' (highest priority) so it is never dropped due to weighted-random-early-drop.

bugs.title: Interfaces removed from LACP trunk due to traffic congestion
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces repeatedly removed and added to a LACP LAG due to dropped LACP PDUs.
bugs.conditions: High traffic volume resulting in weighted-random-early-drop (WRED) being invoked.
bugs.impact: LACP PDUs dropped resulting in loss of LACP state.
bugs.workaround: Reboot affected blade.
bugs.fix: Modify LACP, STP and LLDP to use class-of-service 0 (highest priority) for PDUs.

bugs.title: Tcpdump performed with an interface filter on VELOS or rSeries will show broadcast traffic from all interfaces
bugs.symptoms: When performing a tcpdump in VELOS or an rSeries appliance, a traffic capture limited to a specific interface will show broadcast traffic hitting other interfaces.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS platform or r5000 / r10000 / r12000 series appliance - Running a packet capture on a specific interface (e.g. 1/1.0 or 1.0)
bugs.impact: This can cause confusion or impede troubleshooting when unexpected broadcast traffic is seen in a capture such as ARP or Miscabling Protocol traffic.
bugs.fix: This issue is now corrected.

bugs.title: A remote user with the same username as the local F5OS user will be granted the local user's roles
bugs.symptoms: If you create a remote user on the RADIUS, TACACS+, or LDAP servers with the same username as a local F5OS user, the remote user will be granted the local user's roles upon authentication.
bugs.conditions: A remote user is created with the same username as a local user and remote authentication is enabled.
bugs.impact: Remote user will take the local user's privileges.
bugs.workaround: Do not create a remote user with the same username as the local user. If you have created already, change the username for either the local user or the remote user.
bugs.fix: If a remote user is created with the same username as a local user, the remote user's authentication will be rejected. Only the local user will have access to the F5OS system.

bugs.title: Device stuck at "unmounting containers" after performing reboot
bugs.symptoms: When we open the console session of any tenant on F5OS-A using virtctl console <tenant_name>. when you reboot the system, during reboot sometimes the system might end up in "unmounting containers"
bugs.conditions: Open the console session to any of the tenants using virtctl utility and reboot the system.
bugs.impact: After rebooting, system takes time to fully start up.
bugs.workaround: Power off and on the system whenever the issue is hit.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue related to device stuck at unmounting containers after the reboot.

bugs.title: Qkview is not collecting log data from kubernetes pods
bugs.symptoms: Qkview does not collect log data from kubernetes pods found on an F5OS Appliance
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS-A -- Qkview
bugs.impact: Limited ability to diagnose kubernetes pod issues
bugs.workaround: Collect log files for kubernetes pods manually. Use the command: kubectl logs <pod-name>
bugs.fix: Qkview will now collect kubernetes pod logs.

bugs.title: Unable to login when accessing F5OS GUI through a network proxy on a port other than 443.
bugs.symptoms: Users are not able to log in to the UI when trying to access F5OS GUI through a network proxy running on a port other than 443.
bugs.conditions: GUI should be accessed via a network proxy running on a port other than 443.
bugs.impact: Users are not able to log in to the GUI.
bugs.fix: After the fix, GUI now reads the port along with the hostname from the URL and can use the port in making API calls (including login API calls).

bugs.title: VM events are not captured inside the log file
bugs.symptoms: The VM logs seen on kubernetes events will not be recorded in the log file. The log file k3s_events is helpful in identifying the life cycle of the VM.
bugs.conditions: K3s events related to BIG-IP VM are not captured in k3s_events log.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.

bugs.title: Tenant goes to INOPERATIVE state after rSeries reboot
bugs.symptoms: - Tenant state shows running ConfD. - Tenant management IP is not reachable. - Inside tenant VM, prompt shows INOPERATIVE.
bugs.conditions: -- Large number of tenants (>36) on r12000 system. -- The system is rebooted
bugs.impact: Tenant goes to INOPERATIVE state.
bugs.workaround: Move the tenant to configured and then deployed state.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue preventing BIG-IP tenants from becoming active.

bugs.title: R2000/R4000 silent reboot
bugs.symptoms: R2xxx/R4xxx system experiences a silent reboot. This is caused by a compatibility issue between the system and the solid-state storage device.
bugs.conditions: NVME fails to initialize after multiple reboots. (1) The following matching signature is found in the system event log: Ex: MCA Error-Reporting Registers Capture. Bank: 6 Core: 0 STATUS Register: 0x0419 Value: 0xb980000000000e0b MCA Error-Reporting Registers Capture. Bank: 6 Core: 0 MISC Register: 0x041b Value: 0x0000000000180000 (2) The NVME SSD installed in the system is a 480GB Micron NVME SSD, model 7450_MTFDKBA480TFR . ex: Model: Micron_7450_MTFDKBA480TFR
bugs.impact: 1.System will reboot by its own 2.System is unresponsive
bugs.workaround: Follow the workaround steps described in K000151762: rSeries 2000/4000 systems with NVME SSD may fail to initialize after multiple reboots, available at https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000151762
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in the BIOS version 1.00.160 and later.

bugs.title: Intermittently tenant is stuck on the Liveness probes failures on r12k platform reboot
bugs.symptoms: - Tenant operational state shows "Liveness probe failed: no domain running under libvirtd yet＼n" - Tenant pod is in failure /restart state. - K3S Event "failed to open /dev/vfio/140: Device or resource busy" is reported by the pod.
bugs.conditions: On appliance reboot when multiple tenants are deployed (>36).
bugs.impact: Tenant becomes inoperational.
bugs.workaround: This is an auto-recoverable error. Allow some time for tenant to auto-recover.

bugs.title: OpenShift cluster failure due to disk exhaustion from oversized log file's
bugs.symptoms: When log files in system grown several gigabytes(GB) and exhaust the disk space, resulting in OpenShift cluster failures.
bugs.conditions: When log rotation is configured on a daily basis and a log flood occurs in the system.
bugs.impact: The log file size can increase by several gigabytes during a flood event, potentially exhausting available disk space.
bugs.fix: The log rotation job configured to run hourly instead of daily to prevent log files from growing excessively large. This will ensure timely rotation and manage file sizes more effectively.

bugs.title: Incorrect subnet mask returned for GET call for /systems
bugs.symptoms: Subnet mask returned from Get call for /systems returns the wrong netmask for the management IP on VELOS and rSeries.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Next instances on VELOS and rSeries.
bugs.impact: Does not impact any functionality. GET API call for /systems returns the wrong subnet mask for the management IP.
bugs.workaround: Log in to the machine/tenant and check the management IP address by using the ip addr show command.

bugs.title: Unable to launch tenant, as VF interface is getting incorrect name while attaching to tenant.
bugs.symptoms: On r2x00/r4x00 related systems, tenant launch fails with an error in ConfD tenant status leaf: "[default/virt-launcher-bip1-1-9sblf:sriov-net3-bip1]: error adding container to network "sriov-net3-bip1": failed to set up pod interface "net7" from the device "x557_4": failed to set netlink MAC address to 00:94:a1:db:bd:0c: resource temporarily unavailable" Linux network manager udev rules and sriov cni try to access the VF and change the interface name of VF. During this process, VFs fail and unable to retrieve. Thus, resource temporarily unavailable error occurs.
bugs.conditions: On r4x00 or r2x00 based systems: 1. In kubectl get pods -A output, the tenant pod goes into Init:0/1 state. default virt-launcher-bip1-1-t6rkh 0/1 Init:0/1 0 36s 2. And in kubectl events, "resource temporarily unavailable" occurs on one of the VFs. 3. In /sys/class/net folder unable to see the below VF interfaces. Instead, some interfaces point to ensp* names which are wrong. Actual result should be as follows: [root@appliance-1 ~]# ls /sys/class/net apigw-dummy-1 lcd sfp_7 sfp_p6v0503 veth0c09f23b veth6cec172f vethea3619d5 x557_p1v1100 x557_p3v1902 br_appliancenet lcd-intf sfp_8 sfp_p7v0900 veth2765115 veth80370796 vetheccdd5fb x557_p1v1101 x557_p3v1903 cni0 lo sfp_p5v0100 sfp_p7v0901 veth3f32fd86 veth82a8440b vethf4081a48 x557_p1v1103 x557_p4v1d00 default-intf mgmt sfp_p5v0101 sfp_p7v0903 veth4ab82fc6 veth8cda0b4d x557_1 x557_p2v1500 x557_p4v1d01 docker0 mgmt0-system sfp_p5v0102 sfp_p8v0d01 veth50d18b0 veth9e8b2e8c x557_2 x557_p2v1502 x557_p4v1d02 dummy0 sfp_5 sfp_p6v0500 sfp_p8v0d02 veth5fe12ffd vethac6590f8 x557_3 x557_p2v1503 flannel.1 sfp_6 sfp_p6v0502 sfp_p8v0d03 veth64783052 vethb688f03e x557_4 x557_p3v1901
bugs.impact: Tenant launch is unsuccessful and unable to connect to the tenant console or tenants' management connection.
bugs.workaround: 1. Move tenants to configured state 2. Remove ice, iavf drivers using the following commands, a. "rmmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice.ko" b. "rmmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf.ko" 4. Load ice and iavf drivers using the following commands a. "insmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.1.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice.ko" b. "insmod /lib/modules/3.10.0-1160.71.1.F5.1.el7_8.x86_64/updates/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf.ko" 5. Run config_ice_vfs.sh script present in /usr/omd/scripts/ folder using - "sh /usr/omd/scripts/config_ice_vfs.sh" 6. Wait until script is completed and VFs are created correctly. 6. Move tenants to running state and check the running state of tenant, after some time.

bugs.title: Failed to delete tenant pods
bugs.symptoms: Stale tenant pods will persist in Kubernetes. kubectl get pods will list the tenant pods, although tenants are deleted.
bugs.conditions: When user deploys 10 to 15 tenants and deletes all of them at the same time.
bugs.impact: Deleted tenant resources will still be running in Kubernetes and consuming resources.
bugs.workaround: Create a tenant with the same name and delete.

bugs.title: Command 'show component' does not show psu-power-in and psu-power-out in CLI and API
bugs.symptoms: The command does not show psu-power-in and psu-power-out in CLI and API.
bugs.conditions: Running show components component <psu> in confd
bugs.impact: PSU power details are not retrieved using ‘show component' command.
bugs.workaround: PSU power details can be retrieved through the following HAL APIs: docker exec -it platform-hal psf run GET:lop/object/sensor-psu-power-in docker exec -it platform-hal psf run GET:lop/object/sensor-psu-power-out
bugs.fix: The ‘show component’ command shows psu-power-in and psu-power-out in CLI and API.

bugs.title: Rapid deletion and recreation of tenant with same name will result in false running status of tenant
bugs.symptoms: Repeated rapid deleting and re-creation of tenant with the same name will result in the subsequent failure of the tenant with the following symptoms: 1. Affected tenant state will show "running" and the running-state will show "deployed" 2. There is no actual VM running.
bugs.conditions: Rapid deleting and re-creation of the tenant with the same name.
bugs.impact: False reporting of tenant status.
bugs.workaround: 1. Ensure that there is at least 30 seconds between deletion and re-creation of tenant. 2. Use different tenant name.

bugs.title: The "show system state boot-time" command does not display any entry
bugs.symptoms: The "show system state boot-time" command does not work properly. r10900-2# show system state boot-time % No entries found.
bugs.impact: r10900-2# show system state boot-time % No entries found.
bugs.workaround: This command is disabled in F5OS-C 1.6.0; it must be disabled in F5OS-A as well.
bugs.fix: This command is disabled in F5OS-C 1.6.0; it must be disabled in F5OS-A as well.

bugs.title: Failed to register/deregister logs observed when tenants are deleted
bugs.symptoms: Deploy two BIG-IP Next tenants and one BIG-IP tenant. After deleting the running tenants in the system, we can see error logs flooding. There are multiple register and deregister failed error logs observed. This is because when a tenant is deleted in ConfD, it is deregistered automatically, but when a tenant is deleted in ConfD, the pod persists, and is still trying to make calls to api-svc-gateway. Since api-svc-gateway has deregistered based on ConfD operation of the tenant, it rejects any of these calls.
bugs.conditions: Deploy two BIG-IP Next tenants and one BIG-IP tenant. After deleting the running tenants in the system, we can see error logs flooding.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Logs will flood until the pod is deleted.

bugs.title: Timezone configuration logs "Timezone is invalid" warning
bugs.symptoms: The system log a warning 'Timezone is invalid' when the timezone is configured. Ex: 2023-08-14T03:50:38.263725-04:00 appliance-1 platform-mgr[17]: priority="Warn" version=1.0 msgid=0x104000000000043 msg="Timezone is invalid" ZONE="America/Los_Angeles".
bugs.conditions: When the system timezone is changed.
bugs.impact: No known functional impact, timezone is updating on the system.

bugs.title: libpng: underflow read in png_check_keyword()
Appliance-setup-wizard traceback on invalid NTP input
bugs.symptoms: Appliance setup wizards throw an uncaught Python traceback if you enter non-numeric input for the NTP port [root@appliance-1 ~]# appliance-setup-wizard Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/bin/appliance-setup-wizard", line 1355, in <module> curses.wrapper(main) File "/usr/lib64/python2.7/curses/wrapper.py", line 43, in wrapper return func(stdscr, *args, **kwds) File "/usr/bin/appliance-setup-wizard", line 1329, in main if scene.setting.is_valid(input_string) is not True: File "/usr/bin/appliance-setup-wizard", line 282, in is_valid_ntp_port int(input_string) < MIN_NTP_PORT or ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'
bugs.conditions: Giving non-numeric value as NTP port configuring via wizard-setup
bugs.impact: Throws an uncaught Python traceback.
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5OS-A 1.8.0

bugs.title: Observing 'Failed to send restarting msg to VF' during reboot with tenants deployed causing reboot time to increase
bugs.symptoms: While rebooting with tenants deployed, the reboot time increased by 2-3 minutes. A "Failed to send restarting msg to VF" message also appears.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when rebooting a system where tenants are deployed.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.fix: Rebooting time is no longer negatively impacted by tenants being deployed.

bugs.title: Incorrect file path reported in the telemetry log records
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect file path reported in the telemetry log records.
bugs.impact: The log file data being collected for telemetry is: /var/F5/system/log/platform.log. However, the file location value in the telemetry log records is shown as /var/F5/partition/log/platform.log.

bugs.title: GUI virtual server CLI has different limitations for days-valid
bugs.symptoms: The range of acceptable values for days-valid for a certificate had inconsistent range limits between the GUI and CLI.
bugs.conditions: Creating a self-signed certificate.
bugs.impact: Possible to enter a value that cannot be reflected in both the GUI and CLI.
bugs.workaround: Limit the number of days-valid to the smaller of the two limits (65535).
bugs.fix: Both the CLI and the GUI now have the same range limits.

bugs.title: F5OS VELOS is polled as Unix device by SNMP using BMC Discovery
bugs.symptoms: Hostname polling via SNMP interface is not available.
bugs.conditions: Using SNMP
bugs.impact: You are unable to see the hostname using SNMP interface.
bugs.fix: User can get hostname via SNMP interface using below oid: SNMPv2-MIB::sysName.0

bugs.title: Partition s/w upgrade compatibility check doesn't use correct target version
bugs.symptoms: When performing the partition database compatibility upgrade check (check-version/set-version), the check logic does not always use the correct target version. This potentially can cause the compatibility check to pass, but the actual database upgrade can fail and automatically roll back.
bugs.conditions: When the target partition version is a patch release (such as 1.5.1, 1.6.1), the compatibility check will use the wrong (base release) version.
bugs.impact: The check-version/set-version database compatibility check might pass even though the actual upgrade would fail.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade the controller s/w to version F5OS-C 1.6.1 or later prior to attempting upgrade to a partition patch release.
bugs.fix: The controller OS services uses the correct partition patch version for the compatibility check.

bugs.title: K3S Cluster will be reinstalled during upgrade from 1.5.0 or lower versions to 1.7.0
bugs.symptoms: K3S Cluster will be reinstalled during upgrade to 1.7.0, from 1.5.0 or lower versions, and this will cause a slight increase in the upgrade time.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 1.5.0 or lower versions to 1.7.0.
bugs.impact: Slight increase in the upgrade time.
bugs.workaround: Cluster deployment status can be seen using "show cluster install-status".
bugs.fix: K3S Cluster will be reinstalled during upgrade 1.5.0 or lower versions to 1.7.0.

bugs.title: Setup wizard script gives an "All IP addresses must be unique" error when NTP and DNS servers match
bugs.symptoms: When the given IP addresses of NTP and DNS servers match, the setup wizard script gives the error, "All IP addresses must be unique" even though it is a valid configuration.
bugs.conditions: The IP addresses of NTP and DNS servers given to the Setup wizard tool are the same.
bugs.impact: Through the setup wizard tool, the user is not able to provide the same IP address for NTP and DNS servers, which is a valid configuration.
bugs.workaround: The same IP address for NTP and DNS servers can be configured using the webUI or CLI instead of the setup wizard tool.

bugs.title: Setup wizards fails and immediately exits if it is given incorrect credentials.
bugs.symptoms: If incorrect credentials are entered while using the setup wizard tool, it fails and exits immediately without allowing the user to correct the given credentials. The setup wizard utility should make it clear that only non-root admin accounts can be used.
bugs.conditions: Incorrect credentials are passed to the setup wizard tool.
bugs.impact: User is not given the chance to correct incorrect credentials.

bugs.title: Error message when attempting to delete a service or OS image that was imported as part of an ISO bundle on rSeries 5600
bugs.symptoms: On rSeries 5600, there will be an error if we attempt to delete a Service or OS image that was imported as an ISO bundle, as they cannot be deleted separately. The corresponding image is removed from the software management list anyway after the error message. appliance-1(config)# system image remove os 1.7.0-3869 service 1.7.0-3869 iso 1.7.0-3869 response error: Image 1.7.0-3869 is part of 1.7.0-3869 ISO error: Image 1.7.0-3869 is part of 1.7.0-3869 ISO Success: Image 1.7.0-3869 is removed appliance-1(config)#
bugs.conditions: Try deleting a base OS image or service on rSeries.
bugs.impact: The "Service cannot be removed" error is displayed.
bugs.workaround: Always use the ISO to remove an F5OS version if the F5OS version is imported as part of an ISO. appliance-1(config)# system image remove iso 1.7.0-3869 Success: Image 1.7.0-3869 is removed

bugs.title: Fixing the log issue stating "UNSUPPORTED STP state" when STP global is configured
bugs.symptoms: A log message appears, stating "UNSUPPORTED STP state" when STP global is configured to RSTP.
bugs.conditions: Removing the global config (initially set to STP) and setting it to RSTP.
bugs.impact: Reliable and correct log messages.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Unable to remove the ISO images that share the same minor version with the running version
bugs.symptoms: Removal of ISO (controller/partition/appliance) fails when a same minor version is shared. Example: Import 1.5.1 and upgraded the system to 1.6.1. Later import 1.6.2(1.6.*) and upgraded the system to 1.6.2. When the system is on 1.6.2 unable to delete 1.6.1.
bugs.conditions: The major and minor version of the current ISO must be same as the ISO version that is being removed/deleted.
bugs.impact: Unable to remove the unused ISO.
bugs.workaround: For controller/appliance, you must remove the ISO on a software version that includes different minor release. For example, you can remove 1.6.1-5555 while running ISO version 1.5.X or 1.7.X. For partition, disable and unset the ISO versions of any partitions that use the same minor version of the ISO that needs to be removed. For example, you can remove 1.6.1-5555 by disabling all the partitions running on 1.6.X and de-configure the SW versions.

bugs.title: ConfD Logging 'Failed to change working directory' Error Message
bugs.symptoms: When running the tcpdump client from the ConfD command line interface, ConfD logs 'failed to change working directory /var/roothome' error message in the devel.log file.
bugs.conditions: Running tcpdump client from the ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: No known impact.
bugs.workaround: No work around.
bugs.fix: When ConfD executes external commands, the working directory is set to the user home directory by default. ConfD logs error if unable to find the user's home directory.

bugs.title: QAT count is not dynamically updated for active tenants after license upgrade
bugs.symptoms: The QAT count of BIG-IP Next tenants does not change for active tenants after license upgrade. The QAT count does not match the expected value for the particular license.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen only for BIG-IP Next tenants that are deployed with the old license.
bugs.impact: Incorrect QAT count for active (old) BIG-IP Next tenants. No impact on new tenants after license upgrade. No impact on BIG-IP tenants.
bugs.workaround: Deployed BIG-IP Next tenants need to be moved to configured and back to deployed for the right QAT value to be updated.

bugs.title: Not able to connect to tenant console via virtctl after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Unable to connect to tenant console via virtctl after upgrading from an older version to 1.7.0. It will happen only if any virtctl console is active while doing upgrade. After upgrading, there will be stale kubectl process with older certificates present which will cause errors.
bugs.conditions: Virtctl console is active for tenant at the same time live upgrade is initiated.
bugs.impact: Not able to connect console to any tenant after upgrade to 1.7.0.
bugs.workaround: Kill kubectl process manually.
bugs.fix: User is able to connect to the tenant console via virtctl after upgrading.

bugs.title: Remove integrity-check configurable option from CLI
bugs.symptoms: In F5OS systems, root and admin users are allowed to toggle the integrity-check option from the CLI. When in FIPS mode, integrity-check should always execute on system startup and when demanded. Since the integrity-check option is configurable, users can disable it which puts the integrity of the system at risk.
bugs.conditions: The configurable integrity-check option is visible when the device is in FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: An admin or root user could access the CLI and disable integrity-check. This could replace files and packages which could impact the integrity of the system.
bugs.fix: We have removed the enable/disable integrity-check option from the CLI.

bugs.title: L2 services (LACP/LLDP) are down on r2000 and r4000 series appliances
bugs.symptoms: LLDP and LACP will appear to be non-functional on the F5OS system. LLDP/LACP PDUs reach the F5OS system, which can be verified with tcpdump.
bugs.conditions: -- r2000 and r4000 series appliances. -- LLDP or LACP is configured. -- Links are up.
bugs.impact: L2 protocols fail to negotiate or register inbound data.
bugs.workaround: Reboot.

bugs.title: iHealth upload is failing with error "certificate signed by unknown authority"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use the QKView upload feature, the upload may fail with the message "certificate signed by unknown authority". This is due to a recent change in certificate authority that is inconsistent between F5OS and iHealth.
bugs.conditions: Always, after mid-September 2023.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload QKView files to iHealth with a single click.
bugs.workaround: Users may use the File Export feature to download QKView files to their PCs, and then upload those files to iHealth. You can find the qkview files in the GUI at System Settings :: File Utilities, then choose "diags/shared" as the base directory, then select "qkview".
bugs.fix: Certificate authorities used by the iHealth upload feature in F5OS will be updated.

bugs.title: On rSeries systems, VLANs can get deleted but are still associated with the interface
bugs.symptoms: On rSeries systems, if the user deletes a VLAN, which is configured/attached to an interface, there is no warning prompted. On both the ConfD CLI and the webUI, it will show that the VLAN is still associated with the interface. The VLAN is deleted from ConfD database. However, a stale entry for the deleted VLAN can be seen associated with the interface.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a user deletes a VLAN that is associated with an interface.
bugs.impact: No functional impact was observed. However, a stale entry of the deleted VLAN is present with the associated interface in the ConfD database.
bugs.workaround: On finding the stale entry, we can delete the VLAN entry from the interface database. For an example, we have a switched-vlan interface with VLAN's 1024, 1025: appliance-1# show running-config interfaces interface intf interfaces interface intf config type ieee8023adLag aggregation config lag-type STATIC aggregation config distribution-hash src-dst-ipport aggregation switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 1024 1025 ] After deleting VLAN 1024, the interface database is still showing the 1024 entry in the database. Now we can delete the 1024 entry from the interface database using the following command: appliance-1(config)# no interfaces interface intf aggregation switched-vlan config trunk-vlans 1024 appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1(config)# exit The deleted VLAN no longer appears: appliance-1# show running-config interfaces interface intf interfaces interface intf config type ieee8023adLag aggregation config lag-type STATIC aggregation config distribution-hash src-dst-ipport aggregation switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 1025 ]

bugs.title: Some internal log content may not appear in external log server
bugs.symptoms: When a remote log server is configured, some internal log content may not appear in the logs on the remote server. Notable are logs related to audit login failures.
bugs.conditions: Remote logging server is configured. Log messages do not appear on remote server for user trying to log in with wrong password repeatedly, causing account lockout.
bugs.impact: Brute-force password attack indications may not be seen on external log server.
bugs.workaround: For logs of this type, consult the log files directly on the appliance.

bugs.title: tcpdump service improvements
Configure admin/operator roles in LDAP without uidNumber or gidNumber attributes
bugs.symptoms: In previous versions of F5OS, when using LDAP for third-party authentication, having uidNumber and gidNumber LDAP attribute mappings was required. These attributes are common on unix systems and unix-based directories, but are optional in Windows environments. In Windows environments (For example, Active Directory), admin may be required to manually add uidNumber attributes to users, and gidNumber attributes to admin/operator groups.
bugs.conditions: Third-party LDAP authentication using Active Directory or other LDAP directory where uidNumber and gidNumber attributes are not provided by default.
bugs.impact: In the above conditions, administrators are required to add uidNumber attributes to users in the directory, and gidNumber attributes to admin/operator groups.
bugs.workaround: Create uidNumbmer/gidNumber attributes if not present in directory.
bugs.fix: A feature was added to map LDAP groups to F5OS roles using LDAP filter (group names) instead of numeric IDs. Additionally, code was added to use objectSid mapping instead of uidNumber/gidNumber to eliminate the need to create missing attributes in Active Directory environments.

bugs.title: Snmpd daemon stuck in loop deleting and recreating 'system snmp communities community' entry after recreating and deleting SNMP config a few times
bugs.symptoms: Snmpd daemon stuck in loop deleting and recreating 'system snmp communities community' entry after recreating and deleting SNMP config a few times.
bugs.conditions: 1. Put an SNMP configuration, e.g.: curl -sku admin:admin -H "content-type: application/yang-data+json" https://localhost/api/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-snmp:snmp -XPUT -d @put2.json # jq -c . <put2.json {"f5-system-snmp:snmp":{"targets":{"target":[{"name":"i10_2_108_100","config":{"name":"i10_2_108_100","community":"verynicecommunity","security-model":"v2c","ipv4":{"address":"10.2.108.100","port":162}}},{"name":"i10_2_108_101","config":{"name":"i10_2_108_101","community":"verynicecommunity","security-model":"v2c","ipv4":{"address":"10.2.108.101","port":162}}}]},"communities":{"community":[{"name":"verynicecommunity","config":{"name":"verynicecommunity","security-model":["v2c"]}}]},"engine-id":{"config":{"value":"mac"}}}} # 2. Wait 10 seconds or so 3. Delete/clear the SNMP config, using one of the two methods: a. curl -sku admin:admin -H "accept: application/yang-data+json" https://localhost/api/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-snmp:snmp -XDELETE b. from the confd CLI in config mode: no system snmp ; commit no-confirm 4. Wait 15 seconds, while monitoring /var/log/messages for repeating audit messages related to the SNMP config. 5. Repeat first three steps.
bugs.impact: High CPU and inconsistent state (SNMP community string comes and goes from 'show running-config system snmp' output while the user is watching it).
bugs.workaround: Restart snmpd container using docker command.
bugs.fix: We obsoleted old SNMP configuration commands.
bugs.behavior: In latest F5OS releases (from F50S-A-1.2.x and F5OS-C-1.6.x onwards) SNMP configuration commands have been simplified. For backward compatibility, the old style SNMP configuration works until F5OS 1.7.0 and keeping a confirmation warning in the CLI asking user to use new simplified snmp commands and the old style commands will be obsolete in future releases. In latest release (from F50S-A-1.8.x and F50S-C-1.8.x), the old SNMP configuration commands are obsolete.

bugs.title: Suppress LOP SEEPROM object did not find errors during re-licensing
bugs.symptoms: During licensing, F5OS can request data from platform SEEPROM that has not been programmed into the SEEPROM. In such cases, platform-hal logs an error message: “appliance-1 platform-hal[8]: priority="Err" msg="Action Error" index=0 message="LOP Result Error: SeepromObjectNotFound (0x11)".
bugs.conditions: During licensing, platform-hal requests un-programmed values. Therefore, an error message is logged in the platform log.
bugs.impact: These log messages are not harmful and do not impact the operation of the system.
bugs.fix: To suppress these messages, upgrade to a newer version of F5OS. Updated F5OS has these messages suppressed and no longer present in the logs.

bugs.title: Unable to access tenant through console access.
bugs.symptoms: Admin can create a user with 'tenant-console' as its primary role from the ConfD CLI. This may create tenant console access issues if a tenant gets created with the same name as the user. The 'tenant-console' role is only for tenant and a new user with 'tenant-console' role cannot be created.
bugs.conditions: Admin has created a user with the 'tenant-console' role and then created a tenant with the same name as the 'tenant-console' user.
bugs.impact: Console access to the tenant (with the same name as a user, which is created earlier with tenant-console role) won't be working.
bugs.fix: Added a warning to be displayed during user creation with the 'tenant-console' role from ConfD CLI. Example: appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication users user test_1 config role tenant-console appliance-1(config-user-test_1)# commit Aborted: 'system aaa authentication users user test_1 config role': tenant-console role cant be assigned to users other than tenant users.

bugs.title: Changing a VLAN from trunked (tagged) to native (untagged) on a LAG in a single transaction can cause traffic outage
bugs.symptoms: Traffic outage after changing a VLAN assigned to a LAG from Trunk to Native in a single commit.
bugs.conditions: Changing a VLAN assigned to a LAG from Trunk to Native in a single commit.
bugs.impact: Traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: First remove the Trunk VLAN from the LAG, then commit the change. Then add the Native VLAN to the LAG and commit the change.

bugs.title: WebUI malfunctions when navigating to HSM Details with inactive FIPS drivers
bugs.symptoms: If the FIPS card is not initialized properly due to inactive FIPS drivers, navigating to certain pages will break the webUI.
bugs.conditions: When the FIPS card is not initialized properly due to inactive FIPS drivers, the "HSM Details" and "Add FIPS Partition" screens on the webUI break.
bugs.impact: A blank screen appears, and users are unable to see the left navigation bar to switch to other screens.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, remove the screen name from the URL, which will navigate the user to the dashboard screen.
bugs.fix: On a system where the FIPS card is not initialized properly, navigating to the "HSM Details" and "Add FIPS Partition" screens no longer results in a break.

bugs.title: VELOS software upgrade does not inform about KubeVirt component upgrade
bugs.symptoms: During F5OS software upgrades with VELOS chassis systems, there is a lack of visibility into which individual software components will be updated before the upgrade. This can lead to tenant degradation. In particular, when upgrading system controllers, the upgrade may include an update to the KubeVirt Kubernetes Extension, which will disrupt tenant operations.
bugs.conditions: VELOS F5OS system controller software upgrades include an update to the KubeVirt Kubernetes Extension.
bugs.impact: The traffic of all tenants that have been deployed will be disrupted.
bugs.fix: During an F5OS software upgrade on VELOS chassis systems, it is important to consider that the traffic of deployed tenants may experience temporary interruptions until the upgrade is finished.

bugs.title: Incorrect Vlan Listeners when a Static FDB is configured
bugs.symptoms: When a Static FDB is configured on an interface, Vlan Listeners associated with that interface will have an extra Service ID configured for Service ID 1.
bugs.conditions: A Static FDB is configured on an interface.
bugs.impact: Extra broadcast traffic will be generated on the system, which could affect performance.

bugs.title: ConfD CLI timed out and subsequently sees Error: application communication failure
bugs.symptoms: CLI times out if the respective action is not completed within the specified time interval.
bugs.conditions: The action to perform takes more time than the specified timeout interval.
bugs.impact: Unable to perform ConfD action.
bugs.workaround: The respective container can be restarted or a system reboot can be performed.
bugs.fix: When there is a timeout event, the CLI disconnects from handler and is not able to connect with handler again to perform subsequent actions. A fix has been implemented to reconnect successfully in case of a timeout event. This prevents application communication failure error. You might still see a timeout when the system is busy but you will still be able to perform required actions a few minutes/seconds later.

bugs.title: rSeries link down events can be missed
bugs.symptoms: The rSeries platform can occasionally fail to detect a link going down due to the removal of the cable.
bugs.conditions: Remove fiber optic cable.
bugs.impact: Links that are DOWN stay operationally UP. This can lead to erroneous LACP and/or LAG state.

bugs.title: Unexpected log messages in /var/log/boot.log post-integrity recovery
bugs.symptoms: Users may observe the following inappropriate log message in /var/log/boot.log after recovering from integrity failure: Sep 28 08:45:08 appliance-1 journal: FIPS Integrity Check: This system has been placed in an error state. Try to recover the system using /usr/libexec/ostree_recover utility or reinstall the system. On many devices pressing the escape key followed by '(' key will bring up a menu that allows the system to be restarted.
bugs.conditions: The integrity failure occurs when the device is in FIPS mode, and a user alters or removes a file, subsequently executing an on-demand integrity test or a boot-up integrity test.
bugs.impact: There are no noticeable performance issues or anomalies associated with these log messages, and the issue does not affect the overall system performance or user experience. There are no potential risks or security concerns related to the inappropriate log messages.
bugs.fix: The code has been modified to provide more user-friendly log messages.

bugs.title: ha-1-deployment pod may get restarted when tenant HA is configured
bugs.symptoms: When HA is configured on the BIG-IP Next tenants, a new pod of name <tenant-name>ha-1-deployment-<replica-set-hash>-<pod-id> will get created in the tenant namespace. In some cases, the pod restart count may be 1.
bugs.conditions: When HA is set up on BIG-IP Next tenants on r-Series.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The pod will come to running state automatically.

bugs.title: Traffic loss of 5-10 seconds after disable/enable of LACP Lag member on r5000/r10000
bugs.symptoms: Disabling and then re-enabling a LACP Lag member can result in traffic loss of up to 10 seconds on r5000/r10000 platforms.
bugs.conditions: Disable then re-enable LACP Lag member on r5000/r10000 platforms.
bugs.impact: Traffic loss lasting up to 10 seconds.
bugs.fix: Don't hold a mutex while processing the set of links to initialize. Make a copy of the links and release the mutex instead.

bugs.title: Container daemons running as PID 1 cannot be cored on-demand
bugs.symptoms: - kill -QUIT (or any other core-producing signal) to a container process running as PID 1 does not cause a core file. - Actual runtime errors do generate cores as expected.
bugs.conditions: Containers that run their services directly as PID 1.
bugs.impact: Not possible to force a core file for diagnostic purposes.
bugs.fix: Containers that were running directly as PID 1 have been modified to use a minimal "init" process to catch and forward signals to the real service process. The command: "docker exec {containername} kill -QUIT 1" can be used to core a daemon running as a child of /dev/init. More complicated containers that have multiple processes running under 'bash' script may need to use "docker exec {containername} kill -ABRT -1" Note that if the "docker kill" or "docker stop" commands are used instead of "docker exec", the container will not restart, resulting in an inoperative system.

bugs.title: GID role mapping may not work with secondary GID
bugs.symptoms: When a user in an external authentication system (LDAP, Radius, TACACS) is given a GID for an F5 role, and that GID is a secondary GID, the role assignment may not be discovered. This would result in the inability to access the system or be able to configure the system for that user.
bugs.conditions: - User in an external authentication system (LDAP, Radius, TACACS) - GID corresponding to F5 role is a secondary GID (for example, it is not the user's default GID, rather a GID from a group to which the user belongs)
bugs.impact: Inability to log into the system, or inability to configure the system for the user in question.
bugs.workaround: The GID for the desired role should be the GID directly mapped to the user in the external authentication system (for example, in LDAP, the gidNumber on the user object should be the F5 role GID), rather than a secondary GID (for example, in LDAP, the gidNumber on a group of which the user is a member).
bugs.fix: All GID role mappings are properly considered when discovering role assignments for users in external authentication systems.

bugs.title: Warning needed about creating tenant with same name as existing user account name
bugs.symptoms: When a tenant is created with the same name as an existing user account, the end user will not be able to log into the tenant console with that user account. A warning is not included.
bugs.conditions: Creating the tenant with the same name as an existing user account.
bugs.impact: The end user will not be able to connect to the tenant mgmt-ip with the user account.
bugs.workaround: Delete and re-deploy the tenant again with a different name.
bugs.fix: A warning that a console user won't be created if it matches the same name as a user account has been added.

bugs.title: Adding a system raid drive fails after successful removal
bugs.symptoms: If the system is set up using bare-metal installation of F5OS-A 1.5.1, the user will not be able to add a SSD after removing an existing SSD from RAID.
bugs.conditions: The system must have been bare-metal installed using F5OS-A 1.5.1.
bugs.impact: User is unable to remove/add SSD into RAID.
bugs.fix: SSD can be added and removed from RAID.

bugs.title: Long BIG-IP tenant names will cause not having virtual console access
bugs.symptoms: No access to the BIG-IP tenant virtual console.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant name is longer than 32 characters.
bugs.impact: The creation of the tenant-console user fails, preventing access to the virtual console for that tenant.
bugs.workaround: Use tenant names that don't exceed 32 characters in length.
bugs.fix: Warn the user when using BIG-IP tenant names that exceed 32 character in length.

bugs.title: K3S is getting reinstalled after live upgrade, even though there is no K3S version change
bugs.symptoms: The CLI "show cluster install-status" shows K3S as installing, even though there is no version change. This happens just after live upgrade.
bugs.conditions: This issue is seen during reboot just after live upgrade.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact.

bugs.title: It is not possible to restore backups from iSeries systems with 4.x FIPS HSM cards to rSeries
bugs.symptoms: Key migration (backup and restore) from iSeries devices with 4.x FIPs HSM cards to rSeries is not working. HSM4.x cards are not supported.
bugs.conditions: If an iSeries device has a 4.x model HSM card, then key migration (backup and restore) to rSeries won't work.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to migrate data/keys from an iSeries device with a 4.x model HSM card to a rSeries device.
bugs.workaround: N/A. FIPs devices with HSM4.x cards will not be supported.

bugs.title: Qkview can crash collecting telemetry database
bugs.symptoms: If there is activity in the telemetry database while qkview is collecting it, the collection of the platform monitoring container will be incomplete, due to the qkview collection executable crashing.
bugs.conditions: Telemetry database is in flux during a qkview collection
bugs.impact: 1. A qkview core file will be created. 2. platform monitor container debug data is not collected
bugs.workaround: Re-run qkview
bugs.fix: The qkview configuration file for the platform monitor has been revised so that the telemetry database will not be truncated.

bugs.title: Failed to ping tenant mgmt-ip
bugs.symptoms: Failed to ping tenant mgmt-ip. Existing and deployed tenant config mismatch.
bugs.conditions: When the user modifies tenant config and moves the tenant to Deployed state before the old tenant instance gets cleaned up completely.
bugs.impact: Tenant will be running with old config and will not be able to ping tenant mgmt-ip.
bugs.workaround: Move the tenant to configured state and once tenant is terminated completely, move it to deployed state.

bugs.title: During integrity failure condition, not able to see the error entries in fipserr file
bugs.symptoms: When we bypass the boot time integrity check using the GRUB parameter NO_FIPS_INTEGRITY=1, the services successfully start. Within the initialization process of the fips-service, the fipsMonitor constructor takes action by resetting the fipserr and entropyerr files.
bugs.conditions: Such case would only trigger when the user tries to disable integrity-check using GRUB on a halted system.
bugs.impact: The cause of the integrity failure won't be seen in the error file pointed by the logs.
bugs.workaround: When the device is halted, recover it first using the RECOVER_FIPS=1 as a GRUB option. After recovery, the user can disable the integrity check again using GRUB.

bugs.title: system AOM allows static configuration of IP address with DHCP enabled
bugs.symptoms: The system allows the user to statically configure an IP address while DHCP (dynamic configuration) is enabled. This causes the IP address to be different from what the user may have intended.
bugs.conditions: The user sets the IP address to a static value and enables DHCP.
bugs.impact: If the user sets the IP address to a static value *and* enables DHCP, the IP address will not stay as the chosen static value. Instead, the IP address will be dynamically configured. This may cause confusion.
bugs.workaround: If the user wishes to use static configuration, set dhcp-enabled to false.

bugs.title: Clearing system AOM data does not reset idle timeout value to default
bugs.symptoms: When clearing system AOM data, the SSH session idle timeout value does not get reset to the default value of 180. Instead, the value is set to 45.
bugs.conditions: Clearing the system AOM data - "system aom clear-data"
bugs.impact: System AOM SSH session idle timeout value is set to 45 instead of expected default of 180.

bugs.title: Error occurs when changing LAG type for an existing LAG interface on webUI
bugs.symptoms: On the webUI, if a LAG type changes from LACP, an error displays when that LAG type changes back to LACP.
bugs.conditions: The error occurs when attempting to change the LAG type on an existing LAG interface to a previously used type. (i.e. Creating a LAG interface with type LACP, changing that type to Static, and then changing it back to LACP)
bugs.impact: This issue does not affect functionality; however, an unnecessary "Object Already Exist" error pop-up appears.
bugs.workaround: To avoid the pop-up, change the LAG type to LACP using the CLI in this scenario.
bugs.fix: Changing the LAG type on an existing LAG interface to a previously used type no longer triggers an error pop-up on the webUI.

bugs.title: FIPS partition details are not seen in the tenant console when it is configured without waiting until its status is 'Running'
bugs.symptoms: FIPS partition details are not seen after connecting to the tenant console when it is configured without waiting until its status is 'Running.'
bugs.conditions: Ensure the tenant is deployed and the running-state is changed to 'configured.' Then, change the running-state to 'deployed' along with the FIPS partition details without waiting for tenant to start.
bugs.impact: The tenant does not show the FIPS partition details.
bugs.workaround: Wait until the tenant comes up and either change the configuration or redeploy the tenant with the required configuration.

bugs.title: Observing QKView start from 100% and then going back to 1%
bugs.symptoms: On a second execution of QKView, it is possible that the percent complete reported by the system diagnostics QKView status command will remain at the previous setting until the QKView collection set-up has been completed. This has no effect on the QKView collection, but it can be confusing.
bugs.conditions: QKView is executed two or more times.
bugs.impact: Confusing percent-complete number for a few moments.
bugs.workaround: Wait for a few moments until QKView capture set-up has finished (up to 30 seconds).

bugs.title: Changing the max-age attribute in password policy is not reflecting immediately
bugs.symptoms: Even after setting max-age value (maximum age, in days, after which password will be expired) less than 7 days, the warning for password expiration is not displaying at the time of next login.
bugs.conditions: Set max-age attribute to less than 7 (days) and check if password expiration warning is prompted at the time of next login.
bugs.impact: Password expiration feature is not working as expected.
bugs.fix: Fix is provided to sync the max-age value, updated from ConfD CLI, with the user's password expiration attribute in the /etc/shadow on the system.

bugs.title: F5 rSeries ATSE2 v72.5.3.00 firmware
bugs.symptoms: ATSE2 v72.5.3.00 firmware
bugs.conditions: RSeries r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance. This update is not applicable to r2000 or r4000-series appliances.
bugs.impact: Not applicable.
bugs.workaround: Not applicable.
bugs.fix: Fixes RRDAG issues. See ID1347997 or ID1785385 for more information.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenant is stuck during boot up after doing tenant upgrade from 15.1.x to 17.1.x
bugs.symptoms: [ 183.888473] [ OK ] Started dracut initqueue hook. [ OK ] Reached target Remote File Systems (Pre). [ OK ] Reached target Remote File Systems. dracut-initqueue[251]: Warning: dracut-initqueue timeout - starting timeout scripts [* ] A start job is running for dev-disk...54e.device (3min 36s / no limit) The problem does not occur in all the deployed tenants. The main cause is that the BIG-IP tenant fails to boot when its LVM cache/metadata is not synced or is corrupted.
bugs.conditions: Host reboots followed by guest upgrade. Tenants get rebooted and retain LVM info, the host gets rebooted, and tenants lose LVM info. There is a timing issue for LVM caching.
bugs.impact: Datapath and tenant configuration will be lost.
bugs.workaround: No workaround except recovery of the tenant. To recover the tenant we need manual intervention. We need to enter Maintenance mode, recover the LVMs, and reboot. Booting into TMOS Maintenance: Easiest way to do this is in one window while [ 1 ];do virtctl console cbip-tenant1-1 -n default;done in another window ps auxww|grep cbip-tenant1-1 kill that qemu pid Then go back to the console window in the grub menu and select maintenance and execute vgcfgrestore Please note this is not full proof.

bugs.title: Cluster IP is unavailable for some time during tenant reboot
bugs.symptoms: Cluster IP/Floating IP becomes inactive, causing API calls failure temporarily.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently when the system/tenant is rebooted. When tenant running-state is toggled (deployed->configured->deployed).
bugs.impact: API calls are failing temporarily. CM will not be able to get the status of the HA.
bugs.workaround: 1. Login to the rSeries device on which the current ACTIVE HA node is running. 2. execute the below command with appropriate changes, docker exec -it node-agent arping -q -c 5 -W 0.01 -U -P -I <tenant mgmt interface> -S <tenant mgmt VIP> <tenant mgmt VIP> tenant-mgmt interface can be found using 'ip a s | grep mgmt' on the root.

bugs.title: Opening and closing preview pane is causing the page scrollbar to disappear on View Tenant Deployments screen
bugs.symptoms: On the "View Tenant Deployments" screen, when there are a significant number of tenants on the tenant data table, there will be a page level scroll. Opening and closing the preview pane by clicking on any row makes the page level scroll bar disappear.
bugs.conditions: User should be on the "View Tenant Deployments" screen and there should be many tenants configured on the system so that user can see a page level scroll bar.
bugs.impact: Opening and closing preview pane is causing the page level scrollbar to disappear making it impossible for a user to scroll down and see the tenants that are out of scroll view.
bugs.fix: The issue is now fixed and opening and closing preview pane no longer hides the page level scrollbar. The user can scroll down to see the tenants that are hidden in scroll view.

bugs.title: WS-2022-0322 - d3-color 2.0.0 package
bugs.symptoms: Versions of d3-color prior to 3.1.0 are vulnerable to a Regular expression Denial of Service.
bugs.impact: F5OS-A 1.8.0 may be affected by WS-2022-0322
bugs.fix: d3-color has been upgraded to an unaffected version.

bugs.title: Messages like "Failed to set up mount unit" may flood in /var/log/messages file
bugs.symptoms: This occurs when a BIG-IP Next tenant is deployed on rSeries platforms while generating QKView files on the host (F5OS-A). Messages like "Failed to set up mount unit: Invalid argument" may flood in /var/log/messages file.
bugs.conditions: When a BIG-IP Next tenant is deployed and QKView files on the host (F5OS-A) are generated.
bugs.impact: Log messages with pattern "systemd: Failed to set up mount unit: Invalid argument" in /var/log/messages are flooded for 10-20 seconds.
bugs.workaround: Log messages are flooded while QKView files are generating for 10-20 seconds. After this, the flooding stops.

bugs.title: Most recent login information is not displayed in F5OS webUI
bugs.symptoms: The most recent login information is not available in the F5OS webUI. These details can only be accessed through the CLI.
bugs.conditions: When using F5OS webUI.
bugs.impact: To access the most recent login information, you must use the CLI.
bugs.workaround: Use CLI command 'show last-logins' to access the recent login information.
bugs.fix: From F5OS-A 1.8.0, the most recent login information can be found in the User & Roles screen of the F5OS webUI.

bugs.title: Additional password policy settings
bugs.symptoms: Youa are unable to configure min-days, warn-age, and remember when configuring a password policy. min-days: a limit on how many days a user must wait between password changes warn-age: indicates how many days before their password expires a user will be warned remember: indicates the number of previous user passwords that will be saved in the system
bugs.conditions: Configuring the password policy.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to configure mid-days, warn-age, remember.
bugs.fix: You can now configure warn-age, min-days, and remember when setting a password policy.

bugs.title: platform.log flooded with error messages when the line-dma agent is down
bugs.symptoms: tcpdump needs to connect to the line-dma agent during startup to function properly. However, if tcpdump is unable to establish a connection with the line-dma agent during startup, the platform.log will be flooded with error messages.
bugs.conditions: tcpdump unable to establish connection with line-dma agent during startup.
bugs.impact: Log will be flooded.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: LDAP external authentication fails if there is no group definition for user's primary GID
bugs.symptoms: LDAP external authentication (e.g. REST API or GUI; but not ssh) fails in the following scenario: - User is defined in external auth system (e.g. LDAP) - User has a primary GID assigned - There is no group definition for user's primary GID While this is legal, because the numeric GID should be sufficient, when we try to look up the group info and fail, this short circuits authentication resulting in an error.
bugs.conditions: - User is defined in external auth system (e.g. LDAP) - User has a primary GID assigned - There is no group definition for user's primary GID
bugs.impact: Externally defined users may not be able to log in.
bugs.workaround: Define a group for the user's primary group ID. system aaa authentication roles role <group name> config remote-gid <group ID>
bugs.fix: LDAP external authentication no longer fails if there is no group definition for user's primary GID. The numeric GID is sufficient.

bugs.title: Default GID group mapping authorized even when GID mapped to different group ID
bugs.symptoms: When a role (group) is mapped to a custom remote group ID (GID), the default GID (e.g. 9000 for admin) is also authorized for the same group.
bugs.conditions: The admin role (GID 9000), operator role (GID 9001), user role (GID 9002), or the resource-admin role (GID 9003) are assigned non-default GID.
bugs.impact: Remote users with GIDs 9000, 9001, 9002, or 9003 maintain the default access for their user role.
bugs.workaround: Do not assign the F5's default admin, operator, and resource admin role IDs (GID) to the remote user groups. These GIDs are 9000, 9001, and 9003 respectively. For a customer who uses the versions with the issue, if higher privilege user group IDs are anything different from 9000, 9001, and 9003, do not assign 9000, 9001, and 9003 GIDs to any other group in the external directory, and do not assign default F5 role GIDs to any user. The default GIDs 9000, 9001, and 9003 should be entirely unassigned in the directory, or assigned to placeholder groups that are prohibited from user assignment. See the role GIDs in ConfD CLI with the following command: show system aaa authentication roles role See the 'GID' column in the command output and don't assign those GIDs to users.
bugs.fix: If a remote-GID is configured for a role, the default GID will no longer authenticate for that role.

bugs.title: Exception handling is missing for validating junk files in sw-mgmt code, resulting in crash logs in the sw-mgmt.debug file
bugs.symptoms: Error messages appear in the /var/log/sw-mgmt.debug file when a junk file with an iso name is copied to /var/import/staging.
bugs.conditions: A junk file with an iso name is copied to /var/import/staging.

bugs.title: Incorrect tpm-integrity-status observed rarely
bugs.symptoms: The tpm-integrity-status in ConfD displays "Dictionary Attack Lockout" after multiple reboots. Ideally tpm-integrity-status would be "Valid".
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen after multiple reboots. Possibly TPM reports a wrong status while updating ConfD and the status is corrected later.
bugs.impact: The issue observed as part of this bug was not an actual attack. There is no impact other than the user interface reporting "Dictionary Attack Lockout".
bugs.workaround: Reboot should fix the issue. If reboot does not fix the issue please contact F5 support as "Dictionary Attack Lockout" can be seen during an actual attack or also during a hardware failure.

bugs.title: Large numbers of platform-hal errors logged in platform.log: "Requested Sensor, data, or record not present."
