bugs.symptoms: The platform-hal service is intermittently logging a large number of messages similar to the following in platform.log: appliance-1 platform-hal[8]: priority="Err" msg="Action Error" index=0 message="Requested Sensor, data, or record not present." interface="job-665402" actionKey="GET:lop/pel" jobId=665402 There may be tens of thousands of log messages in some cases.
bugs.conditions: The conditions that trigger this issue are unknown at this time.
bugs.impact: The platform.log file becomes filled up with many of these log messages, and they must be filtered out to review the logs effectively.

bugs.title: Exporting the same file to the same remote location twice throws an error
bugs.symptoms: Exporting a file to a remote location is successful, but an error is thrown if a user exports the same file to the same remote location twice on http protocol.
bugs.conditions: This error is seen only if the export operation is initiated using http protocol. If the user exports a file twice through scp, the transfer succeeds by overriding the previous file.
bugs.impact: The user will not be able to export the same file to the same remote location twice even if there are changes in that file. In short, the previously exported file cannot be overridden when exporting over http protocol.
bugs.workaround: The user can export that same file to the remote host over http protocol by altering either the file name or the remote location.

bugs.title: Fan speed randomly shows as '0'.
bugs.symptoms: The fan speed is randomly and incorrectly reported as '0'.
bugs.conditions: Checking the sensors using GET:bmc/sensors.
bugs.impact: The fan speed is reported as '0'.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed, and the fan speed no longer randomly reports as '0'.

bugs.title: A few SEL entries in /var/log/platform/sel have missing details
bugs.symptoms: A few SEL entries in /var/log/platform/sel have missing details or might be blank.
bugs.conditions: For r2000 and r4000 systems, a few SEL entry types are not fully parsed and details will not be available, particularly those that typically appear during a system restart.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but with missing SEL log entries it can be difficult to investigate other problems.
bugs.fix: Improved the logging of SEL entries.

bugs.title: Libvirt core is generated on downgrade from 1.7.0 -A to 1.6.0 -A
bugs.symptoms: A flawed core file is generated intermittently on downgrade from 1.7.0 -A to 1.6.0 -A. The tenant remains healthy and functional after reboot.
bugs.conditions: Occurs intermittently when a system downgrades from 1.7.0 -A to 1.6.0 -A.
bugs.impact: A libvirt core file is generated, but the tenant is actually healthy and functional.

bugs.title: Calendar navigator skips one month
bugs.symptoms: On the "Time Settings" screen, when using the calendar navigator to "Set Time & Date", the navigation arrows for the next month skips one month.
bugs.conditions: Using the navigation arrow when the currently selected date is the 31st of a month and the next month has only 30 days.
bugs.impact: If the user wants to make a selection in the next month while the current selection is the 31st of a month, they will not be able to do that in the first go with the navigation arrow.
bugs.workaround: Users will be able to navigate to the desired month by using the back arrow.

bugs.title: Hugepages do not get de-allocated after BIGIP NEXT tenant HA disassembly
bugs.symptoms: After BIGIP NEXT tenant HA disassembly, the huge pages allocated for the HA-deployment pod do not get de-allocated. This can be checked in /proc/meminfo.
bugs.conditions: This bug can be observed after HA disassembly.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. 38 MB huge pages will not be available for other processes after the disassembly of HA. After the reassembly of HA, the same huge pages will be used.

bugs.title: LCD panel, indicator, and F5 logo light turned off after system upgrade
bugs.symptoms: The system's LCD panel, as well as LCD indicator and the F5 logo light are off. In the user interface, an error reading 'Module communication error detected' can be seen.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading a r2600 appliance from F5OS-A 1.3.2 to F5OS-A 1.5.1 with LCD current version 1.01.063.00.1 and LCD target version 1.01.067.00.1.
bugs.impact: LCD panel, indicator, and F5 logo light on the system are off, and an error reading 'Module communication error detected' can be found in the user interface.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.

bugs.title: Error log: "PINGLOOP Failed to ssh to 127.0.0.1"
bugs.symptoms: "PINGLOOP Failed to ssh to 127.0.0.1" logged in platform.log by Appliance Orchestration Manager.
bugs.conditions: 1. root user locked with expiry status set to "locked". 2. Appliance rebooted after locking root user.
bugs.impact: Internal processes relying on root user may malfunction.
bugs.workaround: Avoid locking the root user account by not setting the expiry status to "locked". Use appliance mode for root user lockdown.

bugs.title: IP Address empty after enabling DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol)
bugs.symptoms: After enabling DHCP in ConfD, IP address allocation does not show up. This is because DHCP takes around 12 seconds to allocate an IP address after sending the request.
bugs.conditions: Using ConfD, configure the IP address using DHCP: "system aom config ipv4 dhcp-enabled true". Look at the IP address using "do show system aom".
bugs.impact: The IP address appears to be empty if you immediately look at the configuration information after enabling DHCP.
bugs.workaround: Wait around 12 seconds after enabling DHCP, before attempting to view the IP address.

bugs.title: On adding a member to an existing LAG on webUI, the newly added member's speed does not add up to the LAG's "Current Speed" instantly and requires a reload to see the expected response
bugs.symptoms: The status for the newly added member shows as "down" in the REST response and the newly added member's speed does not add up to the "Current Speed" of the LAG on the webUI/REST response.
bugs.conditions: Occurs on the webUI when adding a member to an existing LAG.
bugs.impact: "Current Speed" for the LAG appears stale as it does not reflect the newly added member's speed.
bugs.workaround: The issue only stays momentarily. If the user refreshes the screen, it shows the LAG's Current Speed appropriately.

bugs.title: SElinux denials prevented LDAP users from serial console login
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to log into the serial console as an LDAP-authenticated user would fail.
bugs.conditions: LDAP is configured. User in question is authenticated from LDAP. Logging into the serial console with said user.
bugs.impact: LDAP users unable to log in via serial console.
bugs.workaround: Use an F5OS local user for serial console access.
bugs.fix: SElinux denials have been corrected.

bugs.title: Misleading "unable to read AOM SSH login banner" errors are found
bugs.symptoms: The AOM SSH login banner is an optional field, but a misleading error "unable to read AOM SSH login banner" is found in logs if you do not configure it.
bugs.conditions: Configure AOM SSH and check the AOM info. The errors will appear in the log.
bugs.impact: Benign errors "unable to read AOM SSH login banner" are found in the log.
bugs.fix: Fixed on F5OS-A 1.8.0. The "unable to read AOM SSH login banner" error does not appear if banner has not been configured.

bugs.title: NTP CLI/webUI displays "ntp api, the server or underlying service is unreachable"
bugs.symptoms: 1. Newly configured DNS IPs are not used for FQDN resolution. 2. show system ntp command is unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: 1. The file /etc/resolv.conf is not correctly mounted or configured inside the container. 2. Invalid or unresponsive DNS IPs configured.
bugs.impact: 1. The "ping" command unable to use recent configured DNP IPs 2. Timeout occurs when you execute "show system ntp".
bugs.fix: 1. Ping now correctly uses newly configured DNS servers. 2. The show system ntp command responds faster.

bugs.title: The user should not be created until the user enters 'commit' and 'set-password' command should be only available after the user created
bugs.symptoms: When a user is created, the 'set-password' command is given as an option before the user runs 'commit'.
bugs.conditions: - Creating a new local user via ConfD CLI.
bugs.impact: The functionality of creating a new user, setting a password, changing password, deleting password, and changing user's configuration is working as expected.

bugs.title: Cannot retrieve AOM username after creating it
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to retrieve the AOM username after setting it.
bugs.conditions: Setting the AOM username and password in ConfD: "system aom set-ssh-user-info username password"
bugs.impact: If the user forgets their username, there is no way to retrieve it.
bugs.workaround: You can use "system aom clear-data" to reset all the information and set a new username and password.

bugs.title: Unable to create AOM user
bugs.symptoms: When setting up another user in system AOM, a user gets the error "Unable to set AOM ssh username and password --------> failed".
bugs.conditions: - Creating a second username in AOM - Using the same password as the first username
bugs.impact: User cannot create a second username and password.
bugs.workaround: When creating a new username and password, you must use a different password from the first password that was used. If you wish to setup a new username using the same password, you must first run "system aom clear-data" to clear out the old username and password combination.
bugs.fix: Update: User can now set a new username with the existing password.

bugs.title: Rare LACPD crash during process termination
bugs.symptoms: LACPD crashes, generating a core file.
bugs.conditions: While the LACPD process terminates, it may crash. Operations such as a host reboot and software upgrade cause the process to terminate.
bugs.impact: A core file is generated. No functional impact to the system.
bugs.fix: LACPD no longer crashes during process termination.

bugs.title: Upon configuration changes, the l2-agent container restarts with a core.
bugs.symptoms: On systems running F5OS-A or F5OS-C, wen the owner field of the fdb entry is updated by the system, for L2_LISTENER entries, l2_agent crashes.
bugs.conditions: Configuration changes triggered by system for L2_LISTENER fdb entries. Note that this field is not used by STATIC fdb entries, but the problem can be reproduced easily with STATIC entries.
bugs.impact: When l2_agent crashes there is a potential disruption to configuration processing.
bugs.fix: The fix will avoid the crash, and the update of the owner leaf will be processed accordingly.

bugs.title: File import failure with error "Couldn't resolve hostname"
bugs.symptoms: In a very rare case, even if the DNS server is configured correctly, the user might observe issues importing files with the error "Couldn't resolve hostname".
bugs.conditions: When user tries to import files using 'file import' command, even if the DNS is configured correctly.
bugs.impact: User will not be able to import any files onto the system.
bugs.workaround: - User will still be able to import files using either curl or wget command on the system. - Rebooting the system will resolve this issue.

bugs.title: Unable to add blade to Openshift cluster if VELOS partition root password is expired or locked
bugs.symptoms: If a VELOS partition root password is expired or locked, the system may be unable to add the blade to the Openshift cluster (or manage the cluster). The "show cluster" command output will report that a blade is reachable ("able to ping"), but will not be able to connect to it ("able to SSH"): ABLE ABLE IN READY TO TO PARTITION INDEX NAME INSERTED CLUSTER CLUSTER PING SSH STATE LABEL -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 blade-1.chassis.local true false false true false Not In Cluster 2 blade-2.chassis.local true false false true false Not In Cluster 3 blade-3.chassis.local true false false true false Not In Cluster
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS partition -- root account in partition is expired or locked
bugs.impact: - Blade will not join Openshift cluster. - Unable to deploy Tenants to blade.
bugs.workaround: Re-enable the root user account for the partition: system aaa authentication users user root config expiry-status enabled

bugs.title: The 'file list' command takes a long time and the webUI is stuck in loading
bugs.symptoms: When the 'file list' command is used, it takes a lot of time to get the results for the log/host path. This causes the webUI to be stuck in loading.
bugs.conditions: Using 'file list' command for log/host.
bugs.impact: The webUI will not be able to load the files in the log/host.
bugs.fix: Optimized the code to achieve faster performance when handling file lists.

bugs.title: The affinity script crash seen in /var/log/cron logs
bugs.symptoms: Affinity script crashes due to unhandled exceptions.
bugs.conditions: Due to an unhandled null reference, sys-affinity crash is seen.
bugs.impact: No impact. system-affinity will restart within 1 minute.

bugs.title: rSeries r5000: assertion in qat-device-plugin FilteringResourceEventHandler.OnDelete causing k8s panic
bugs.symptoms: Crash log gets printed in run_plugin.log
bugs.conditions: The application internally crashes some time during tenant deletion.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The log keeps increasing with crash log when it happens.
bugs.workaround: It automatically recovers by restarting the application.

bugs.title: Duplicate platform agent log entries when tenant starts
bugs.symptoms: Multiple f5-platform-agent.log messages may be seen for cluster subscribe: API client already subscribed.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP Next tenant is starting on rSeries hardware.
bugs.impact: No functional issue, tenant starts as expected.

bugs.title: "40001: bind: address already in use" failure logs on BIG-IP Next HA setup
bugs.symptoms: Following error logs/events are displayed as part of HA cluster configuration of BIG-IP Next tenants: "40001: bind: address already in use"
bugs.conditions: Errors are observed when HA is configured between two BIG-IP Next tenants.
bugs.impact: These are just error messages. No functional impact.

bugs.title: F5OS permits non-existent ethernet interfaces to be configured
bugs.symptoms: F5OS allows you to manually type in non-existent interfaces of type "ethernetCsmacd" when adding an interface component. The system later prohibits you from deleting this non-existent interface while the type is ethernetCsmacd.
bugs.conditions: User-triggered command for non-exposed interface type.
bugs.impact: The configuration contains a non-existent ethernet interface with no actual activity. Attempting to delete the interface from the Partition CLI will result in the following error : Partition-1(config)# no interfaces interface 1/1.1 Warning: Some elements could not be removed due to NACM rules prohibiting access. From the Partition GUI The Network-> interfaces Page will show blank "There are no items to show in this view."
bugs.workaround: Delete the non-existent interface. Depending on the type of the created interface , there are 2 ways to delete it . In case the interface is not a valid interface for the blade such as 25.0 or even a fake name like "example" you can delete it using "no interfaces interface 25.0" If the interface is for a real interface, for example you have created interface 1/1.1 while the portgroup is in 100G mode (only 1.0 is valid) you will need the following procedure to delete it : From from the Controller running the Active Partition Login to controller that is the active one for the needed partition (can be seen via "show partitions" command on the controller). Also from "show partitions" on the controller check the partition ID. From controller bash: docker exec -it partition2_manager bash (assuming the partition ID is 2) From inside the partition run the following: confd_cmd -c "mdel /interfaces/interface{1/1.1}"
bugs.fix: With this fix, F5OS will reject the creation of ethernetCsmacd.

bugs.title: OpenTelemetry exporters may not produce data upon first tenant being added to system
bugs.symptoms: Telemetry streaming stops when the first tenant is configured.
bugs.conditions: When OpenTelemetry exporters are configured before the first tenant is configured within F5OS, this can lead to a condition where the exporters stop streaming metrics and logs.
bugs.impact: OpenTelemetry exporters stop producing metrics and logs.
bugs.workaround: The work-around is to disable and re-enable all exporters from the ConfD CLI. system telemetry exporters exporter <name> config disabled system telemetry exporters exporter <name> config enabled

bugs.title: Modifying a remote server with multiple selectors from the web UI removes the AUTHPRIV configuration.
bugs.symptoms: The AUTHPRIV option is not available on the webUI. Modifying a remote log server, which has multiple servers, from the webUI removes the AUTHPRIV configuration
bugs.conditions: Modifying a remote server with multiple selectors from the webUI.
bugs.impact: The AUTHPRIV selector has been removed from the configuration.
bugs.workaround: To modify the configuration of a remote server with more than one selector, use the CLI.
bugs.fix: Added AUTHPRIV option to the webUI. Modifying the configuration of a remote server with more than one selector from the web UI will not remove AUTHPRIV from the configuration

bugs.title: Out of memory issues are seen when multiple telemetry exporters are configured
bugs.symptoms: Out of memory issues are seen when too many telemetry exporters are enabled.
bugs.conditions: When the system is configured with too many exporters with exporter options as "retry-enabled" as "true" and "send-queue-enabled" as "true", and exporter end points are not reachable from device.
bugs.impact: This will increase memory utilization of the system and could cause the restart of random processes/services to free up the memory.
bugs.workaround: Disable the unreachable telemetry exporters from ConfD "system telemetry exporters exporter <name> config disabled" If there are too many exporters configured, disable some of the exporters.

bugs.title: Copying BIG-IP ISO to /var/import/staging/, leaves ISO loopback mounted
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs: ERROR: sw-mgmt: priority=error msgid=0x3501000000000154 msg=Unexpected error processing "import /var/export/chassis/import/iso/<image>.iso": [Errno 30] Read-only file system: 'ace-1.1.7-0.0.3.i686.rpm'
bugs.conditions: Copying a BIG-IP ISO to /var/import/staging/ (rather than /var/F5/system/IMAGES or /var/F5/partition<num>/images)
bugs.impact: An error occurs and the ISO loopback remains mounted
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5OS-A/C 1.8.0

bugs.title: Memory leaks in tcam-manager
bugs.symptoms: TCAM Manager leaks a small amount of memory at each rule add or delete operation.
bugs.conditions: Memory leak happens with rule add/delete operations. These rules are generated by TMM during hardware offload.
bugs.impact: High memory utilization and eventual OOM.
bugs.fix: Allocated objects are now properly freed.

bugs.title: Modifying mgmt interface's description will trigger interface flapping
bugs.symptoms: Management interface description commit may cause an interface flap.
bugs.conditions: Change the mgmt interface description for first time and commit.
bugs.impact: There is a mgmt interface flap.

bugs.title: SNMP IF-MIB misreport the status and speed of LACP LAGs
bugs.symptoms: SNMP polling on IF-MIB provides incorrect status and speed of LACP Lag interfaces.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen only on SNMP interface. The correct status and speed display on CLI or GUI.
bugs.impact: The user will see inappropriate status and speed details when polled for IF-MIB details on SNMP for LACP LAG interfaces.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue to display the correct values of LACP LAG interfaces in IF-MIB SNMP polling.

bugs.title: Ping failing when tenant is reprovisioned from lower vCPU to 60 vCPU
bugs.symptoms: Ping will fail. "ps -ef | grep tmm" will show tmm process waiting for ready. [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] log # ps -ef | grep tmm root 38710 31087 0 09:45 ? S 0:00 bigstart_wait tmm ready
bugs.conditions: Reprovisioning a tenant with 60 vCPU in F5OS. This issue is only applicable for the r12K series.
bugs.impact: Datapath functionality will not work.
bugs.workaround: Reboot tenant.

bugs.title: Dagd component core
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, the dagd component cores when a tenant instance is removed from the tenant cluster. This can happen due to tenant instance restarts or tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: Tenant instance restarts or tmm restarts can trigger this issue.
bugs.impact: No impact is seen.

bugs.title: When more than one PCIe AER error has occurred, diag-agent reports this as a "RAS AER 'unknown' error" instead of the individual AER errors.
bugs.symptoms: When more than one PCIe AER errors are occurred simultaneously, diagnostics will not report the events.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when more than one PCIe AER errors occur simultaneously.
bugs.impact: You are unable to see the individual PCIe errors.
bugs.fix: Updated diagnostics to consider and report more than one PCIe AER errors when occurred simultaneously.

bugs.title: The system's power state may be incorrectly indicated by the Status LED
bugs.symptoms: The power state on an r2000/r4000 system may be incorrectly indicated by the Status LED when the system is in standby. When an r2000/r4000 system is in the standby power state, the Status LED should be solid amber. Instead, the Status LED may be blinking amber which indicates that communication between the LCD and host CPU has been lost.
bugs.conditions: An r2000/r4000 system in standby power state.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.
bugs.fix: Fixed in LCD firmware v1.01.068.00.1 and later.

bugs.title: "Error pf_nic_get_media" failed error for ports with or without SFP connected
bugs.symptoms: Error pf_nic_get_media failed for connected or not connected ports coming intermittently.
bugs.conditions: One or more ports are not connected on R2k/R4K devices.
bugs.impact: The error is confusing because the port does not have an SFP connected.

bugs.title: Audit log entries are missing when creating or deleting objects via UI or API
bugs.symptoms: When creating or deleting multiple remote-server related objects via UI or API, multiple restart happens causing log message drop.
bugs.conditions: While creating or deleting multiple objects related to remote-server, rsyslog restart everytime to apply new configuration. Due to the restart, some log messages are dropped.
bugs.impact: Log messages are dropped due to multiple restarts of the rsyslog.

bugs.title: F5 rSeries platforms incorrectly report phantom/stale for second PSU
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries platforms incorrectly report the presence of a PSU in the system in "show components", when the PSU has been removed from System.
bugs.conditions: -- An existing PSU is removed -- Run "show components" in confd
bugs.impact: Wrong PSU details will be reported.
bugs.workaround: Remove the device using confd docker exec system_manager confd_cmd -c "mdel /components/component{psu-2}" The workaround persists after a reboot, but if you later add psu-2, you would have to reboot the system after psu-2 is inserted. After the system reboots, confd will resume reporting on it.

bugs.title: Observing continuous log messages "Found correct SSH ECDSA key in authorised keys." in /var/log/messages
bugs.symptoms: Seen repeated logs of "Found correct SSH key" approximately every 20 seconds in /var/log/messages.
bugs.conditions: These logs are seen every 20 seconds from the time of system startup.
bugs.impact: Flooding of /var/log/messages log file with "Found correct SSH ECDSA key in authorized_keys".
bugs.fix: Orchestration Manager now redirects these log messages to the /dev/null

bugs.title: SCP as non-root user does not report errors correctly for bad/non-existent files.
bugs.symptoms: Using SCP to retrieve files from F5OS as "admin" or other non-root users should report a proper error when attempting to access an invalid directory or non-existent file. Instead, the SCP command does nothing, reports no error, and exits with an on-zero exit status.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to read a non-existent/inaccessible file via SCP.
bugs.impact: The user is not informed about the failed SCP operation and the reason for the failure.
bugs.fix: SCP server software now reports errors the invalid/inaccessible filenames.

bugs.title: Appliance management plane egress traffic from F5OS-A host going via BIG-IP Next tenant management interface instead of host management when both are in same subnet
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP Next tenant is installed, a default route rule is added on host. If tenant management and host management IPs are on same subnet, then two similar rules are created with destination as same subnet. The tenant route rule is created with higher priority (metric 0) resulting any management egress traffic destination belonging to same subnet is going through tenant management interface instead of host management interface.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Next tenant is deployed on appliance.
bugs.impact: End users receiving traffic from appliance, will observe sender IP as tenant management interface instead of host management interface. Note: a. This issue will be observed only when host management & tenant management subnet is same and also destination to which data is sent is on same subnet. b. This impacts management plane traffic within the appliance's management subnets.

bugs.title: Disk requirement validation is not implemented when tenant is in "Configured/Provision" state
bugs.symptoms: There is no validation for tenant storage size while tenant is in Configured or Provisioned state.
bugs.conditions: Tenant in Configured or Provisioned state
bugs.impact: Any disk size, or even less than required size as well.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuring a tenant storage size that is below the minimum. Refer to https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000140343 for the minimum tenant storage size.

bugs.title: F5OS upgrades fail when SNMP configuration contains special characters.
bugs.symptoms: As part of some security fixes, added a special character restriction in SNMP configuration in F5OS-A 1.5.1. This resulted in an upgrade failure to 1.5.1. If an upgrade to 1.5.1 is successful, the SNMP configuration will get deleted implicitly.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to 1.5.1 fails when the SNMP configuration contains any special characters. The restricted special characters are: /*!<>^,/
bugs.impact: If the user encounters this issue, the system will go to an inaccessible state and require a forced downgrade.
bugs.workaround: Delete the SNMP configuration (community, target, or user) containing special characters before performing an upgrade to 1.5.1.
bugs.fix: The special characters in the SNMP configuration do not inject any security issues and can have special characters. Hence, the special characters restriction is removed in F5OS-A 1.5.2 and F5OS-A 1.8.0.

bugs.title: iHealth upload not supported on F5OS-A
bugs.symptoms: The iHealth upload service has changed its authentication schema to OKTA, and requires a Client ID and Client Secret rather than a User ID and Password. Version 1.5.1 (and previous versions) of F5OS-A do not support this authentication schema.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Users will not be able to directly upload QKView files to iHealth from the appliance because of change in the authentication schema.
bugs.workaround: 1. Use the file export feature to download the QKView from the appliance to a local PC. 2. Sign on to ihealth.f5.com. 3. Use the upload feature to upload the QKView to the iHealth service.
bugs.fix: Added Client ID and Client Secret in the iHealth page on webUI. User can upload QKView files to iHealth.

bugs.title: Restoration of system configuration database may fail if admin user was previously modified
bugs.symptoms: The restoration of the System Configuration Database fails with this error: appliance-1(config)# system database config-restore name config_database1 proceed yes Error: access denied Database config-restore failed.
bugs.conditions: In F5OS-A 1.5.1, the expiry status of the ‘admin’ user has been modified even before the System Configuration Database is saved and restored on the device that is currently installed after RMA/factory or F5OS clean install.
bugs.impact: Unable to restore the System Configuration Database.
bugs.workaround: 1. In F5OS-A 1.5.1, it is recommended not to lock or modify the expiry status of the ‘admin’ user on the RMA/factory or clean installed appliance. If modified, enable the user before taking the backup. 2. Edit the System Configuration Database backup file. For the admin and root user, remove the next line which is highlighted by the arrow, then restore the configuration using the modified file: <username>admin</username> <config> <username>admin</username> <password><REMOVED></password> <last-change>0</last-change> <expiry-date>-1</expiry-date> <role>admin</role> <expiry-status>enabled</expiry-status> <---

bugs.title: Rasdaemon memory leak
bugs.symptoms: Rasdaemon will increase in size when excessive (>10000) MCE memory error events occur and may lead to system instability.
bugs.conditions: Likely due to memory hardware resulting in MCE errors
bugs.impact: System instability
bugs.workaround: Rebooting could be a temporary work-around if MCE rate is excessive.
bugs.fix: Rasdaemon version is upgraded in the current F5OS release.

bugs.title: The rSeries appliance log shows "PSU voltage out value < lower limit, value=0".
bugs.symptoms: The following message appears in the logs: 66305 psu-1 psu-fault EVENT Network Access "PSU voltage out value < lower limit, value=0" "2023-12-08 09:00:00.900082135 UTC".
bugs.conditions: The conditions that trigger this issue are unknown at this time.
bugs.impact: Users see several "PSU voltage out value < lower limit, value=0" logged messages, which could be falsely reported.

bugs.title: iHealth upload client may fail if ConfD database is offline.
bugs.symptoms: If the ConfD service goes offline when migrating primary key, executing the iHealth upload commands (for example, show system diagnostics ihealth), and in the event of performing any other activity, then the iHealth service may generate a core file.
bugs.conditions: If the ConfD service goes offline when migrating primary key, executing the iHealth upload commands (for example, show system diagnostics ihealth), and in the event of performing any other activity, then the iHealth service may generate a core file.
bugs.impact: A core file may be generated.
bugs.workaround: The iHealth client will restart if it cores. Repeat the iHealth commands after the ConfD database is up and running.
bugs.fix: Hardening is added in the iHealth client to avoid generating a core file in certain events.

bugs.title: The Rest API call to list core files returns 500 error when no core files found.
bugs.symptoms: The ConfD List Core Files Rest API call request returns a 500 ERROR when no core files are found rather than returning an empty list. Example: https://10.10.10.1:8888/restconf/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-diagnostics-qkview:diagnostics/f5-system-diagnostics-qkview:core-files/f5-system-diagnostics-qkview:list
bugs.conditions: 1. No core files exist on the system. 2. The Rest API for querying the list of core files is made.
bugs.impact: Limited, but may affect automation.
bugs.workaround: Automation can respond to 500 error.
bugs.fix: Instead of responding with a 500 error, the response is now "none" when no core files exist.

bugs.title: Tcpdump on F5OS does not honor the -c flag
bugs.symptoms: When using Tcpdump on F5OS with the -c flag, Tcpdump will not stop after receiving the given number of packets.
bugs.conditions: A Tcpdump session is started with the -c or --count flag.
bugs.impact: The Tcpdump session will not terminate after receiving the requested number of packets and will continue until manually terminated.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump now honors the -c flag and will terminate after receiving the given number of packets.

bugs.title: GUI error "Unable to get data from stream streams/platform-stats/json"
bugs.symptoms: When viewing usage visualizations on screens that support them (Tenant details, Dashboard cpu Tab etc.), sometimes when switching between browser tabs an error in notification stream occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- Viewing a screen that shows data visualizations using notification streams -- Switching between different browser tabs.
bugs.impact: An error message is dislayed in place of the visualzation charts.
bugs.workaround: Refreshing the page will start the notification stream again and user should start seeing data visualisations
bugs.fix: This issue is happening because GUI is trying to disconnect and reconnect to stream when switching between tabs. This behaviour is prevented now the stream will stay connected even when user switched to different tab.

bugs.title: On a rSeries appliance, config-backup proceed is broken
bugs.symptoms: On a rSeries appliance, system database config-backup 'proceed' is broken. It is about overwriting an existing backup file, but it prompts you to proceed even if a file does not exist.
bugs.conditions: System database config-backup always prompts for the user to proceed even if a file does not exist.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. When you provide input 'yes', the backup file will be generated.
bugs.workaround: When prompted to 'proceed', you must respond with 'yes'.
bugs.fix: The system database config-backup prompts the user with ‘proceed’ option only when the file exists and the user is not provided ‘proceed yes’ in the input CLI command.

bugs.title: Platform-deployment script logs are now captured in both its dedicated log file and the systemd journal
bugs.symptoms: The platform-deployment script used bare echo statements for all output, meaning log messages were not persisted to a dedicated log file and were not captured in the systemd journal. This made it difficult to troubleshoot platform service deployment issues (e.g., container startup failures, registry setup, OS rebase errors) after the fact, as the output was only visible in the service status and could be lost on rotation or reboot.
bugs.conditions: Any F5OS-A or F5OS-C system running the platform-services-deployment service during upgrade/downgrade, reboot, or service start/stop operations.
bugs.impact: Reduced observability during platform service deployment. Operators had limited ability to diagnose historical deployment failures, Docker Compose errors, or registry setup issues because log messages were transient and not written to a persistent, searchable location.
bugs.workaround: Prior to this fix, operators could manually inspect systemctl status platform-services-deployment.service -l for recent output, but historical logs were not reliably available.
bugs.fix: Added structured logging to the platform-deployment script. All output is now timestamped and written to a dedicated log file (/var/log/platform-deployment.log) with logrotate support, and simultaneously forwarded to the systemd journal via StandardOutput=journal on the service unit. This enables operators to use both journalctl -u platform-services-deployment and the persistent log file for troubleshooting platform service deployment issues

bugs.title: Incorrect system-manager version is used in upgrade check while upgrading from 1.3.2 to 1.5.1
bugs.symptoms: The incorrect system-manager version is used while upgrading F5OS-A from one patch release to another patch release. This causes issue in database compatibility checks and provide incorrect validation results.
bugs.conditions: When upgrading from one patch release (such as 1.3.2) to other patch release (such as 1.5.1).
bugs.impact: The database compatibility checks often , occasionally indicating success even in cases of incompatibility.

bugs.title: Tenant pods stuck in terminating/unknown state
bugs.symptoms: After the BIG-IP Next tenant is deleted, a few pods are stuck in a terminating/unknown state.
bugs.conditions: Interrupting the device by any of the operations like rebooting/upgrading/power cycling/changing port modes/licensing/network switching before the proper deletion of the BIG-IP Next tenant causes tenant pods to be stuck in a terminating/unknown state.
bugs.impact: Creating new tenants with the same name before ensuring proper cleanup of the previous tenant may affect the functionality of the new tenant.
bugs.workaround: The user should wait a few minutes after issuing the BIG-IP Next tenant 'delete' command for the tenant to be deleted properly before proceeding with system interrupt operations (rebooting/upgrading/power cycling/changing port modes/licensing/network switching). Command to check tenant is deleted: kubectl get pods -A The above command lists all Kubernetes pods; ensure no pods are starting with the tenant name.

bugs.title: LDAP authentication is consuming several minutes to authenticate via GUI and SSH.
bugs.symptoms: LDAP authentication is working fine. However, authentication takes several minutes, which lacks a user-friendly experience.
bugs.conditions: - Configure LDAP server-group. - Configure LDAP_ALL as an authentication-method. - Log in using LDAP user via GUI or SSH.
bugs.impact: The user is forced to wait for several minutes to get the result of LDAP authentication.
bugs.fix: Removed unnecessary GID lookup to speed up LDAP authentication.

bugs.title: LCD restarting internal services periodically due to memory allocation error.
bugs.symptoms: On a r2000/r4000 system, the LCD may experience an issue causing it to repeatedly restart the ‘platform_monitor’ or ‘bmcservice’ service due to a memory allocation problem. The lcd.log file displays recurring patterns of log messages such as: lcd platform_monitor[1581] Traceback (most recent call last):#012 File "/usr/sbin/platform_monitor.py", line 540, in <module>#012 raise e#012OSError: [Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory lcd /etc/watchdog.d/platform_monitor_watchdog.sh: found platform_monitor is not running <snip> lcd watchdog[1424]: test binary /etc/watchdog.d/platform_monitor_watchdog.sh returned 255 lcd /etc/watchdog.d/platform_monitor_watchdog.sh: Trying to repair platform_monitor ... <snip> lcd /etc/watchdog.d/platform_monitor_watchdog.sh: platform_monitor successfully repaired, pid = 27676 A similar condition may occur for the 'bmcservice' service. lcd /etc/watchdog.d/bmcservice_watchdog.sh: found bmcservice is not running lcd watchdog[1436]: test binary /etc/watchdog.d/bmcservice_watchdog.sh returned 255 lcd /etc/watchdog.d/bmcservice_watchdog.sh: Trying to repair bmcservice ... lcd /etc/watchdog.d/bmcservice_watchdog.sh: bmcservice successfully repaired, pid = 26226
bugs.conditions: Excessive LCD memory consumption may occur if the appliance is turned off while external power is still connected. This excess memory usage will not be resolved when the appliance is turned on again.
bugs.impact: While the LCD is operating in this state, it may not be able to obtain the PSU status from the BMC and update the PSU status LEDs accordingly. Furthermore, the LCD may not be able to ascertain the system’s current power state from the BMC.
bugs.workaround: The excessive LCD memory consumption can be recovered by rebooting the LCD. 1) Log into the appliance as a root user. 2) Issue `docker exec -it platform-hal psf call POST:lcd/reboot waitForBootup=true` at the Linux prompt. 3) Wait 60–90 seconds for the LCD to complete a reboot. Example: [root@appliance-1:Active] ~ # docker exec -it platform-hal psf call POST:lcd/reboot waitForBootup=true field | value ----------+-------- success | true
bugs.fix: The excessive LCD memory consumption is fixed in LCD firmware v1.01.069.00.1 and later.

bugs.title: Inconsistency with time zones displayed in log files
bugs.symptoms: PEL logs in F5OS systems are logged in a different time zone, not the configured time zone.
bugs.conditions: If the configured time zone is different from UTC, then the PEL logs can display different time for log messages.
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting and tracing issues can be difficult, as the time zones used in different logs do not match.
bugs.fix: PEL logs in F5OS systems are logged in the applicable time zone.

bugs.title: Observed Stale QAT entry for the deleted tenant
bugs.symptoms: The "show cluster nodes node node-1" command allows stale entries in the deleted tenants and associates the QAT devices.
bugs.conditions: The following steps can trigger this issue: step 1: On version 1.7.0, a tenant is deployed with a changed new qat redesign code. step 2: The device is downgraded to an earlier version of 1.7.0, where qat redesign is not available. step 3: On the earlier version, the tenant is deleted. step 4: The device is upgraded to the latest version which is the same as or above 1.7.0 where qat redesign code is available.
bugs.impact: QAT entries display stale entries and resources are not utilized. Also, the user does not experience issues while deploying tenants.

bugs.title: GUI freezes during LDAP user authentication if no remote GID mapped locally.
bugs.symptoms: The LDAP remote user authentication freezes for a long time (more than a minute).
bugs.conditions: When trying to authenticate a remote LDAP user through the GUI without mapping any of the remote user GIDs to the F5OS local roles.
bugs.impact: Authentication freezes for a long period before rejecting the user.
bugs.workaround: One of the remote GIDs should be mapped to the local F5OS roles.
bugs.fix: Map the remote GID(s) to the F5OS role(s) to authenticate remote LDAP users successfully.

bugs.title: ARP request for mgmt interface IP resolving to mgmt0-system inferface's mac
bugs.symptoms: 1. Configure IP on mgmt0-system from ConfD. 2. Configure IP on mgmt using linux command. 3. ARP request to mgmt-ip resolves to MAC of mgmt0-system.
bugs.conditions: Configuring IP on mgmt interface using linux and nmcli/ip commands.
bugs.impact: No impact
bugs.fix: Added code changes to make F5OS to resolve to the correct MAC for mgmt-ip.

bugs.title: "show components component state memory full" does not have any meaningful output
bugs.symptoms: The 'full' command displayed under 'show components component state memory' does not have any meaningful output.
bugs.conditions: When the user runs the command 'show components component state memory full', there is no output generated.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.

bugs.title: Timezone changes are not reflected in the log messages until the hardware is rebooted
bugs.symptoms: After configuring timezone, /var/log/messages are logged with old timezone till the hardware is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: Configure timezone from ConfD and verify /var/log/message.
bugs.impact: The log messages are logged with old timezone.
bugs.workaround: After configuring timezone, rebooting the hardware resolves the issue.
bugs.fix: Added code changes to reflect the new timezone changes in /var/log/messages without rebooting the hardware.

bugs.title: LAG aggregated speed is not updated
bugs.symptoms: LAG's aggregation state lag-speed value is not the aggregate of the member port's actual speed.
bugs.conditions: Individual port auto-negotiates to a value lower than its initial port speed configuration.
bugs.impact: The actual speed of the LAG is not displayed when running the show interfaces interface aggregate command. This is just a display issue, with no impact on the actual bandwidth of the LAG.
bugs.fix: The LAG speed reflects accurately the sum of the operational speed of members.

bugs.title: Server error occurs when trying to create LAG.
bugs.symptoms: The following server error occurs and does not create LAG: "Failure for data/openconfig-interfaces:interface API".
bugs.conditions: Using GUI and trying to access the LAG tab under Network Settings.
bugs.impact: The LAG page displays Server Error.
bugs.workaround: Try reopening the LAG tab several times.

bugs.title: LDAP authenticated admins logging in via the serial console may have trouble disabing appliance mode during system instability
bugs.symptoms: If ConfD is not running, F5OS offers an emergency option to disable appliance mode when an administrator logs in successfully via the serial console.
bugs.conditions: The admin role has been configured with a remote-gid that is not 9000 and the admin successfully authenticates via LDAP on the serial console while ConfD is not running.
bugs.impact: Remotely-authenticated admin users cannot disable appliance mode if ConfD is offline.
bugs.fix: Remotely-authenticated admin users can disable appliance mode if ConfD is offline.

bugs.title: Voltage sensor limits incorrect, causing notice messages on r2000 & r4000 appliances
bugs.symptoms: The rSeries 2000 and 4000 appliances can incorrectly report voltage sensor errors when the values are within the allowed range. platform 2023-10-16 19:00:01.263 Z Error appliance-1 diag-agent[8] msgid=0x098200000000001a msg="Component Attribute Changed" component="appliance/hardware/bmc" attribute="p5a:sensor:voltage:p1v05nac" severity="Notice" value="1.03" interface="diag-controller" platform 2023-10-15 19:00:01.322 Z Error appliance-1 diag-agent[8] msgid=0x098200000000001a msg="Component Attribute Changed" component="appliance/hardware/bmc" attribute="p5a:sensor:voltage:p0v83x557" severity="Notice" value="0.81" interface="diag-controller" The 2 sensor limits above should be: - P1V05_NAC == 1.05V +/- 30mV - P0V83_X557 == 0.83 (0.76V - 0.85V) This means log messages that report voltage values within the limits can be safely ignored.
bugs.conditions: RSeries appliances r2x00 or r4x000
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.workaround: Review the warning to ensure it is within the defines ranges stated above.
bugs.fix: The system will not log errors when P1V05_NAC and P0V83_X557 are within the accepted limits.

bugs.title: Configuring Expiry-status of root and admin users should not be allowed
bugs.symptoms: Expiry-status of root and admin users are allowed to be configured and there is a chance of locking out these users.
bugs.conditions: If Expiry-status of any root or admin user is marked as Locked, that root or admin user cannot log in to the system.
bugs.impact: There is a chance that default users, such as root and admin, become locked out.
bugs.fix: You cannot edit the ‘Expiry-status’ field in webUI for admin and root users. Thus, it cannot be configured. The 'Expiry-status' field for root and admin users will now always display the default value as 'Enabled'.

bugs.title: Snmpv1 traps have a agent-addr set to 0.0.0.0 instead of a management IP
bugs.symptoms: When SNMP V1 version is configured for SNMP Traps monitoring, the received traps will have the agent-address as 0.0.0.0 instead of system's mgmt ip. This is issue with only SNMP v1 version traps.
bugs.conditions: SNMP V1 version traps will have the agent-address as 0.0.0.0 and the remaining trap oid values are proper.
bugs.impact: User can't see the system's mgmt ip address in SNMP V1 version trap's agent-address field.
bugs.workaround: F5OS suggest to use SNMP V2 version for monitoring SNMP Traps which will populate the IP address correctly with system's mgmt IP.

bugs.title: A linkUp and linkDown traps are sent when an up interface is disabled, and vice versa
bugs.symptoms: When F5OS system is configured with SNMP Targets for managing the Trap notifications, linkUp and linkDown traps will be sent when interface state is toggled.
bugs.conditions: Always two traps (linkUp and linkDown) will be sent even when the interface state is toggled from UP to DOWN or DOWN to UP.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but when two traps are sent, the interface state over SNMP can be misleading.
bugs.fix: The appropriate trap, that is, linkDown trap when F5OS interface state is down and linkUp trap when F5OS interface state is up, will be sent.

bugs.title: Non-root, local authentication fails when LDAP is configured with chase referrals and an invalid DNS server is configured
bugs.symptoms: Local and remote authentication to F5OS will timeout and fail. Running commands as root may take 60 seconds before each command returns.
bugs.conditions: LDAP authentication is configured with chase-referrals set to true and an invalid or non-responsive DNS server is also configured.
bugs.impact: Users cannot successfully authenticate via the GUI. Local admin users cannot successfully authenticate. Logging in as root takes 2 minutes and many system commands will take at least 60 seconds to complete.
bugs.workaround: Set 'system aaa authentication ldap chase-referrals false' or ensure a working DNS server is always configured.

bugs.title: User with operator role is not having read-access to all pages
bugs.symptoms: - User experiences unauthorized error when trying to access "Tenant Images", "Software Management", "File Utilities", "Configuration Backup", and "System Report" - User sees no items when trying to access "File Utilities", "Configuration Backup", and "System Report" pages
bugs.conditions: User has operator role.
bugs.impact: User is not able to view certain pages.

bugs.title: Config-restore fails when backup file has expiry-status field for admin or root user
bugs.symptoms: For a root or admin user, if the value for Expiry-status in the backup file is not set to enabled, then config-restore fails.
bugs.conditions: During backup, if the "Expiry-status" value for admin or root user is not set to enabled, then restore fails with the backup.
bugs.impact: Database config-restore fails.
bugs.workaround: For admin and root user, comment expiry-status, expiry-date in the backup file and try to restore.
bugs.fix: Added NACM rules in ConfD for successful config-restore.

bugs.title: Allowing user to configure HostKeyAlgorithms parameters
bugs.symptoms: A new config CLI (system security services service sshd config host-key-algorithm) is implemented to allow HostKeyAlgorithms configuration.
bugs.conditions: In non FIPS mode, to enable or disable ssh-rsa HostKeyAlgorithm, this newly implemented CLI can be used.
bugs.impact: HostKeyAlgorithm usage was not configurable.
bugs.fix: This is a new CLI that can be used to enable or disable ssh-rsa HostKeyAlgorithm

bugs.title: ConfD Application Error when tenant interface stats are not available
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to get tenant interface stats, the system displays "Error: application error".
bugs.conditions: The creation or modification of tenants may result in inaccurate handling of historical data by the tenant interface-stats logic. This could lead to the display of an “Error: application error” message when queried. For example: appliance-1# tenants tenant cbip-tenant-b state interface-stats down-sample-to 10 average 10s-avg Error: application error
bugs.impact: Confd reports the error on the command line and logs the error in platform logs. 2024-01-24T20:12:37.123437567Z: [Error]: confd: msg="Action Point reply error" error="confd error: 'Unknown error', last='Invalid confd_vtype value: 0', errno=5"
bugs.fix: The problem has been resolved in more recent versions of F5OS-A. To resolve it, upgrade to a more recent version of F5OS-A. It will resolve once all interfaces are enabled.

bugs.title: FIPS Password Initialization Failure with Special Characters
A key can be created rather using a stored key for CSR creation
bugs.symptoms: When creating a Certificate Request (CSR), a key must be provided. Since a key was provided by the 'store-tls' option for the TLS key, it was assumed that the CSR was intended to be used with that specific key.
bugs.conditions: Generating a CSR request via system aaa tls create-csr in confd
bugs.impact: The certificate request (CSR) functionality is not as flexible as it could be (similar to the self-signed certificate, which allows a key to be created). It is complex to create certificate requests where a new key is required. Additionally, the absence of a stored key meant that no CSR could be produced.
bugs.workaround: Create a new key, store it in TLS, and run the create-certificate-request.
bugs.fix: The create-certificate request now allows a key to be created, or, if none exists, it creates one. If no key is requested and one exists, the process will continue as usual, generating a CSR using the pre-existing key. However, if a key is requested (or does not exist), a new one will be created and both the key and CSR will be shown. It is important to note that a CSR without knowing the key is of no use.

bugs.title: Allowing entry of a Subject-Alternative-Name (SAN) for certificate and CSR creation
bugs.symptoms: There is no method available for inputting the SAN field during the creation of certificates or CSR.
bugs.conditions: While creating a CSR through system aaa tls create-csr in ConfD.
bugs.impact: The option to include the SAN field in certificates and/or certificate request is not available.
bugs.workaround: To add an SAN, you need to edit the /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf file and add it. However, this may not be effective for certain software that does not accurately read the configuration file.
bugs.fix: A new SAN field has been implemented, which is mandatory, and allows users to enter a value in the field. However, if the value “none” is used, the field can be omitted. Additionally, to allow entry of the SAN, a default tls certificate is created in /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert that has the SAN populated with the hostname and management-ip values. In the absence of a user-provided self-signed certificate, the http-server will automatically use the default certificate. As this is a new feature, back-porting to older versions has not been implemented and would be difficult and complex.

bugs.title: User-manager's ConfD socket getting closed.
bugs.symptoms: After repeating the change of network type and device reboot, the device goes into a state where the user-manager is not interacting with ConfD.
bugs.conditions: - Change remote GID role and check '/etc/gid-map.txt' file if the value is reflected. - Switch network type and reboot the device. Repeat the above process until '/etc/gid-map.txt' file is not been updated correctly.
bugs.impact: Any ConfD configuration change that goes through user-manager fails. This includes any of the user’s password changes, or remote GID changes.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the system will get the correct GID value from the ConfD and update the '/etc/gid-map.txt' file.
bugs.fix: The user-manager has no reason to use NSS to lookup any PW/group info, as it deals exclusively with the local user database. Additionally, there is a ZMQ service that belongs in authentication-mgr (which understands remote authentication) that is in the user-manager container. It forces user-manager to use an ‘/etc/resolv.conf’ that can reference remote sources. If the user-manager trips over a lookup that goes to LDAP (usually a local-db miss), it can be very slow and time out. The ConfD->user-manager channel is sensitive of slow responses, and shuts down subscriber/callpoint handler/daemon that takes over 15 to 30 seconds to respond. When this happens, the user-manager is going to see an EOF on its ConfD sockets. This fix forces the user-manager to only lookup on local databases.

bugs.title: Remote GID mappings to F5OS roles are disconnected for TACACS+/RADIUS authentication methods.
bugs.symptoms: Remote GID mappings (on a TACACS+ or RADIUS server) to F5OS GIDs/roles are not working correctly. When attempting to configure a remote mapping, it results in the access rejection with a message similar to below: [root@system ~]# ssh radius_or_tacacs_user@<F5OS system mgmt IP> Password: Last login: <date> from <source IP> No valid role group found in user groups: '9000' Connection to <mgmt IP> closed.
bugs.conditions: A remote GID mapping is configured for a role in F5OS and the authentication method used for remote users is RADIUS or TACACS+.
bugs.impact: Remote users cannot log in to the system.
bugs.workaround: Configure remote user's GIDs in a way that they correspond to the GIDs in F5OS for the desired role(s). Then, remove any remote GID mappings in the F5OS configuration.
bugs.fix: Fixed remote GID mapping to F5OS roles for TACACS+/RADIUS authentication methods.

bugs.title: F5OS SNMP IF-MIB::ifAlias missing from snmpwalk
bugs.symptoms: The following SNMP MIB OID from IF-MIB table is missing on F5OS-A and F5OS-C. 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 Example snmpwalk result: ~ % snmpwalk -c public -v 2c 10.10.10.33 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 IF-MIB::ifAlias = No Such Instance currently exists at this OID
bugs.conditions: Snmpwalk -c public -v 2c 10.10.10.33 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 IF-MIB::ifAlias = No Such Instance currently exists at this OID
bugs.impact: Cannot get results for MIB OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18
bugs.fix: We have added the support for OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18 (IF-MIB::ifAlias), which will represent the value for interface description.

bugs.title: First SSH login after editing remote RADIUS or TACACS+ user privileges will still apply old privileges
bugs.symptoms: The first SSH login after editing role-based privileges for a remote RADIUS or TACACS+ user will still give the user their prior privileges (or, if the user is newly created, login will be rejected with a message saying "This account is currently not available"). Subsequent logins will apply the updated user privileges.
bugs.conditions: 1. RADIUS or TACACS+ Authentication is enabled. 2. A new user is created in one of the above auth systems, or an existing user’s role-based access is modified. 3. The affected user SSHs into F5OS for the first time after the change in step #2.
bugs.impact: First login to system after creation fails, or first login after modification of user privileges gives the user incorrect privileges.
bugs.fix: Fix issue where first SSH login after editing remote RADIUS or TACACS+ user privileges will still apply old privileges.

bugs.title: Learned L2 entries in data-plane L2 forwarding table may disrupt some traffic flows between tenants
bugs.symptoms: While a tenant transitions from active to standby, an egress packet in flight may trigger a L2 learn event in the FPGA data-plane. This can occur for tenants that transmit using a different MAC address while active, such as when MAC masquerading is enabled. If so, a dynamic L2 entry is created from the source MAC address of the egress packet. These dynamic entries also enable the service DAG without setting a service ID, which causes matching packets to be dropped in the VOQ system due to an invalid service DAG lookup result. This can disrupt egress traffic for another tenant on the same device, attempting to transmit to the destination MAC address that was recently relinquished by the standby tenant. These drops increment the 'ic_voq_drops' counter in the tmctl vqf_global table. These L2 entries will not be corrected by subsequent L2 learn events for the same MAC address from a different location. Thus, traffic disruption may persist until entries age out.
bugs.conditions: - MAC masquerade configured on the traffic-group of an HA pair of tenants. - A failover from tenant A to tenant B. - Another tenant running alongside tenant 'A' attempts to transmit to the MAC masquerade address that is now owned by tenant 'B'.
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption from one tenant to another in specific directions.
bugs.fix: L2 entries that are created from host generated L2 learn events, no longer enable the service DAG for matching packets.

bugs.title: Unable to remove the ISO images that share the same minor version with the running version
bugs.symptoms: Removal of ISO fails when a same minor version is shared. And the base version has been imported for the first time as part of the ISO that has been deleted.
bugs.conditions: The major and minor version of the current ISO must be same as the ISO version that has been removed/deleted. And the base version has been imported for the first time as part of the ISO that has been deleted.
bugs.impact: Unable to remove the unused ISO.
bugs.workaround: For controller/appliance, you must remove the ISO on a software version that includes different minor release. For example, you can remove 1.6.1-5555 while running ISO version 1.5.X or 1.7.X.

bugs.title: System integrity check logs are logged with default name instead of system hostname in platform.log file
bugs.symptoms: Logs for the system integrity check are recorded with the default name rather than the system hostname in the platform.log file.
bugs.conditions: Enable fips-licensce on the device and set the system hostname to a different value than default. But system integrity check logs are logged with default name in the platform.log file.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but integrity check logs are logged with default name.

bugs.title: Resource-manager pod runs in the default namespace
bugs.symptoms: After downgrading from 1.7.0 or any higher version to any lower version below 1.7.0, a pod name 'resource-manager' runs in the default namespace.
bugs.conditions: When the system downgrades from 1.7.0 or higher version to 1.5.2 or any lower version.
bugs.impact: No functionality is impacted.
bugs.workaround: This pod can be ignored

bugs.title: If accidentally import bad ISO images, it may not removed automatically
bugs.symptoms: When you accidentally import ISO images from a faulty URL, they cannot be removed or replaced with the correct URL.
bugs.conditions: User accidentally imports faulty ISO images to the system.
bugs.impact: Deleting and importing system ISO images might have an impact.
bugs.workaround: Login to the command line with root user access and remove the image via 'rm' under '/var/import/staging', and import the correct ISO.
bugs.fix: Please refer to the workaround and further detail.

bugs.title: Libvirt core file is generated when the system is rebooted.
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect Libvirt core file is generated when the system is rebooted intermittently. However, the tenant is healthy and functional after the reboot.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently, when the system reboots.
bugs.impact: A Libvirt core file is generated, and the tenant is healthy and functional.

bugs.title: Partition image removal message is truncated
bugs.symptoms: If a partition is enabled and then disabled while running version A, and then upgraded to version "B", attempting to deport partition image "A" fails, the CLI throws truncated error messages.
bugs.conditions: The partition is upgraded with the state is disabled.
bugs.impact: Incomplete error messages for the failure reason. The error that is reported is: "Error: Failed to remove software: 1.5.1-14085, error message: Standby removal failed for following reason: OS version".

bugs.title: During remote logging server configuration, selectors help menu does not display when using Tab key.
bugs.symptoms: While configuring the remote logging server, using the Tab key does not display selector help menu.
bugs.conditions: While configuring the remote logging server, using the Tab key does not display selector help menu.
bugs.impact: No help menu is displayed
bugs.workaround: Use ? key to get help in selectors menu, while configuring remote server.

bugs.title: Subject-Alternative-Name (SAN) feature now supports client-side SSL Validation
bugs.symptoms: Since no SAN was allowed to be inserted into the http-server’s self-signed certificate, client-side SSL validation was not supported. This impacts Central Manager's VELOS/rSeries provider. The missing SAN field causes the certificate to be rejected.
bugs.conditions: Using the default self-signed certificate.
bugs.impact: Client-side SSL validation is not supported.
bugs.workaround: To add an SAN, you need to edit the /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf file and add it. However, this may not be effective for certain software that does not accurately read the configuration file.
bugs.fix: A new SAN field has been implemented, which is mandatory, and allows users to enter a value in the field. However, if the value “none” is used, the field can be omitted. Additionally, to allow entry of the SAN, a default tls certificate is created in /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert that has the SAN populated with the hostname and management-ip values. In the absence of a user-provided self-signed certificate, the http-server will automatically use the default certificate.

bugs.title: Libvirt core file is generated when the system is rebooted.
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect Libvirt core file is generated when the system is rebooted intermittently. However, the tenant is healthy and functional after the reboot.
bugs.conditions: Intermittently, when the system reboots.
bugs.impact: A Libvirt core file is generated, however the tenant is healthy and functional.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenant reports blank interface
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP tenant reports a blank ("") interface member in the trunk when removing one or more interfaces from an aggregation.
bugs.conditions: When removing one or more interfaces from an aggregation.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP tenant has an empty member in the trunk.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP tenant does not report a blank ("") interface member in the trunk when removing one or more interfaces from an aggregation.

bugs.title: Allowed-ips allowed-ip <name> is not accepting the '-' in the names
bugs.symptoms: Allowed IP profile got deleted while upgrading to 1.7.0 from lower versions. allowed-ip profile names with '-' got erased out. which got fixed in 1.8.0
bugs.conditions: While upgrading to 1.8.0 from lower versions other than 1.7.0, all allowed IP profile names should have atleast one alphanumeric and it should have not have any other special character other than ('-', '_' and '.')
bugs.impact: Allowed IP profile gets deleted if it is not matching the pattern.
bugs.workaround: Re-apply the allowed-IP profile configuration without eiphen '-' in the name
bugs.fix: Fixed the schema such that allowed IP profile name accepts the '-' in profile name.

bugs.title: System telemetry exporter send queue and retry settings are causing memory issues
bugs.symptoms: Memory issues are seen in system when telemetry exporter is not reachable for a long time.
bugs.conditions: When exporter is not reachable for a long time.
bugs.impact: System can go out of memory.
bugs.workaround: User can disable the send queue and retry setting using ConfD. For example: appliance-1(config)# system telemetry exporters exporter <<exporter name>> config options send-queue-enabled false appliance-1(config)# system telemetry exporters exporter <<exporter name>> config options state options retry-enabled false
bugs.fix: Send queue and retry settings are removed for telemetry exporters.

bugs.title: System events visible in the CLI may not be visible in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Running "show system events" on the F5OS CLI typically reveals many events that are not visible in the GUI under System Settings > Alarms & Events. The GUI filters the display of events according to their assigned severity. But since many events are not assigned a severity, such events will be hidden from view.
bugs.conditions: Events that are not assigned a severity are instead marked "NA". Such events are not visible in the GUI and can only be seen via the CLI or API.
bugs.impact: The omission of events displayed in the GUI can be misleading. Administrators using the GUI may not be aware of important events that have occurred on the platform.
bugs.workaround: All system events can be seen by running 'show system events' on the F5OS CLI or by retrieving them via the REST API.
bugs.fix: On fixed versions, a new option called 'All' has been added to the Severity drop-down selector in the GUI. This displays all events, including ones without a severity assigned.

bugs.title: Tenant pods/status stuck in Pending
bugs.symptoms: After a reboot or power cycle, the tenant status will be stuck in "Pending" and logs error in getting result from DelNetwork: Link not found＼"" pod="default/virt-launcher-idmdmzgslb-1-6jhj9"
bugs.conditions: When the device is rebooted or power cycled, the tenant status is stuck in Pending.
bugs.impact: Tenant will not be UP and status will be Pending.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the tenant state i.e. Move tenant to configured and back to deployed. This will stop and start the tenant

bugs.title: Password policy option reject-username set to false has no effect
bugs.symptoms: When the administrator configures 'system aaa password-policy config reject-username false', F5OS will still reject passwords that contain the username.
bugs.conditions: System aaa password-policy config reject-username is set to false
bugs.impact: When a user tries to set or change a password containing their username in any part of the password, F5OS will reject that password.
bugs.workaround: Do not use passwords that contain the username.

bugs.title: Tenant images renamed with bracket are not supported
bugs.symptoms: Live upgrades with prior releases with tenants that use images with brackets in their name will fail when going to a version that restricts the tenant image name character set.
bugs.conditions: Tenants using image filename with brackets won't allow upgrades to releases that validate the image filename character set.
bugs.impact: The tenant will have to be recreated or upgrade to a version that does not have the validation.
bugs.workaround: Tenant has to be recreated with the original image that didn't contain brackets.
bugs.fix: Brackets were included in accepted character set for tenant image filename.

bugs.title: BMC self health test falsely logged as failed
bugs.symptoms: The BMC self health test is randomly logged as having failed: appliance-1 alert-service[8]: priority="Notice" version=1.0 msgid=0x2201000000000029 msg="Received event." event="65543 appliance aom-fault EVENT NA "Bmc Health Self test failed: Device-specific 'internal' failure." "2024-03-01 14:00:00.918553424 UTC"".
bugs.conditions: Checking the platform log
bugs.impact: BMC self health test is falsely logged as failed.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed and the BMC self health test no longer falsely logs a failure.

bugs.title: Log messages related to multus in /var/log/messages
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently, during resizing of the tenant leads continuous display of log messages from multus every minute in /var/log/messages.
bugs.conditions: When tenant is resized, we are seeing log messages related to multus every minute in /var/log/messages.
bugs.impact: No impact on functionality.
bugs.workaround: Please reboot the system. This will fix the issue.

bugs.title: Inconsistent case values (upper and lower case) for different F5OS-C SNMP OIDs
bugs.symptoms: AlertSource in SNMP alert contains text as Controller starting with uppercase C instead of lower case in core alert events. Similarly, for core alert events generated in blade, comes with Blade instead of blade.
bugs.conditions: Process crash generating core file and SNMP alerts are enabled.
bugs.impact: Tools processing SNMP alerts might get affected if tooling is case-sensitive.
bugs.fix: Fixed alertSource text for SNMP core alert events to send lower case. Tools modified to read alertSource of SNMP core alert events require to update as per the correction.

bugs.title: Unable to access rSeries system from 172.17.0.0/16 IP subnet
bugs.symptoms: Unable to access the rSeries system from client or server systems in the 172.17.0.0/16 IP subnet
bugs.conditions: -- r5000-series, r10000-series, or r12000-series appliance
bugs.impact: Unable to access the rSeries system from client or server systems in the 172.17.0.0/16 IP subnet
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, do the following: 1. Log into the system as root 2. If running F5OS-A 1.7.0, edit /var/docker/config/platform.yml. If running F5OS-A 1.5.2, edit /var/docker/config/platform.patch.yml. 3. In the specified file, locate the section for "selinux_labeler", and add a line under it that reads 'network_mode: "none"'. The indentation of this line must match exactly the indentation of the "container_name" and "image" lines. For example: selinux_labeler: container_name: selinux_labeler network_mode: "none" image: ${... ... 4. Reboot the system. 5. Once the system is rebooted, log into the system as root, and run "docker network rm config_default"

bugs.title: The ha-1-deployment pod may get restarted after HA setup and system upgrades
bugs.symptoms: When HA is configured on the BIG-IP Next tenants, a new pod name <tenant-name>ha-1-deployment-<replica-set-hash>-<pod-id> will be created in the tenant namespace. In some cases, the pod restart count may be 1 or 5.
bugs.conditions: When HA is set up on BIG-IP Next tenants on rSeries and after upgrading F5OS 1.7.0 to F5OS 1.8.0 version.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The pod will automatically transition to a running state.
bugs.workaround: NoneThe

bugs.title: Remove unhelpful troubleshooting files from QKView
bugs.symptoms: Creating a QKView on an F5OS host appears to make a non-sparse copy of /var/log/lastlog This file is a sparse file and depending on factors, can have a really large file size, though actual consumed disk blocks remain quite low.
bugs.conditions: Creating a QKView file on F5OS.
bugs.impact: Exhausted disk space and caused K3s to reap pods to free up ephemeral storage - including killing running tenant (BAD).
bugs.workaround: Remove the files.

bugs.title: QAT entries for the deleted tenant still show up in cluster
bugs.symptoms: When a tenant is deleted and a reboot scenario such as a live upgrade is performed, a reference to the deleted tenant remains in the cluster via ConfD and internally in qat-support-pod.
bugs.conditions: Deletion of a tenant occurs just before a reboot.
bugs.impact: Incorrect reporting through ConfD.
bugs.fix: A monitor checks for changes to tenant configurations. Upon detecting deletion or un-deployment, the qat-devs.json file is promptly updated. Subsequently, the tenant is marked as terminated, thereby notifying the informer to refrain from updating device records with outdated values.

bugs.title: GRE V1 packets are being dropped before even reaching BIG-IP on F5 r2xxx/r4xxx
bugs.symptoms: GRE V1 packets are dropped at the Intel E810 Firmware before reaching BIG-IP tenant on F5 r2xxx/r4xxx platforms.
bugs.conditions: When GRE V1 packets are received to BIG-IP tenants running on F5 r2xxx/r4xxx platforms.
bugs.impact: GRE V1 traffic will not be reaching BIG-IP tenants on F5 r2xxx/r4xxx platforms.

bugs.title: AOM SSH password requirements are not working
bugs.symptoms: AOM SSH user password requirements are not consistent.
bugs.conditions: Setting up AOM SSH user and password.
bugs.impact: Password requirements may not be clear or consistent.
bugs.fix: AOM SSH password requirements have been updated to match documentation. Now, when trying to enter a password, requirements are clearly shown. Ex: Value for 'password' (<string, min: 8 chars, max: 16 chars>):

bugs.title: Upload/Download API should work with '/api' and '/restconf'
bugs.symptoms: Upload/Download is not working with '/api' endpoint.
bugs.conditions: Use '/api' endpoint to upload/download a file.
bugs.impact: Fails to Upload/Download a file.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue occurring with the Upload/Download API.

bugs.title: User accounts with username which includes only numeric values or special characters like "." or ".." or starts with '-' are inactive
bugs.symptoms: User accounts created with username that include only numeric values are inactive or non-functional. Also, usernames starting with dash ‘-’, contain only “.”, “..”, or any invalid characters (other than letters, digits, underscores, dashes and $ (at the end)) creates non-functional user accounts.
bugs.conditions: User account with username containing only numerics or starts with dash '-' or username like "." or ".." are non-functional.
bugs.impact: Non-functional user accounts are created. User functionalities like set-password, change-password, or other would not be working as expected.
bugs.fix: User account creation with invalid username will not be possible. An error will be displayed for invalid usernames. Following is an example: appliance-1(config)# system aaa authentication users user 12345676578 ? Possible completions: Error: "12345676578" is an invalid value. There wont be 'config' option available to create/configure new user account until you provide valid usernames.

bugs.title: LAG Trunk Configuration is Missing Inside of Tenant
bugs.symptoms: When creating a LACP LAG or Static LAG, the lag and its members will show as up on the F5OS and switch side (Arista and Cisco). However, on the tenant, tmsh will show that neither the trunk nor trunk members are present: root@(localhost)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list net trunk root@(localhost)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)#
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant on F5OS system
bugs.impact: The trunk information will not be visible in the tenant. - On high-end rSeries appliances (r5000, r10000, and r12000-series systems) and VELOS tenants, traffic will still work. - On low-end rSeries appliances (r2000 and r4000-series systems), traffic will not flow.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: System loses its mgmt-ip address after switching between static and dynamic allocation (DHCP) of IP and rebooting
bugs.symptoms: Device not reachable on static IP when DHCP is disabled.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure static IP and enable DHCP. 2. Disable DHCP and reboot the device. 3. Device is not reachable on static IP.
bugs.impact: Device connectivity.
bugs.workaround: Static IP needs to be configured through console.
bugs.fix: Fixed code to persist static IP.

bugs.title: Changing remote authentication methods from RADIUS/TACACS to LDAP may break remote-gid functionality.
bugs.symptoms: If RADIUS or TACACS are utilized for authentication, the user’s ‘passwd’ details will be saved in /etc/libnss-udr/passwd. However, if the user switches to LDAP authentication and disables the previous method, their entry may not be removed from /etc/libnss-udr/passwd. If a user is using GID remapping (by configuring remote-gid), the authentication will fail, at least when logging into the CLI.
bugs.conditions: - Enable RADIUS authentication and log into the system as a remote RADIUS-defined user. - Change the authentication method to LDAP and disable RADIUS authentication. - Configure remote-gid functionality for an LDAP-defined user. This LDAP-defined user should have the same name as the RADIUS-defined user. - Log into the system as that remote LDAP-defined user.
bugs.impact: The authentication will fail for the LDAP-defined user. An error message will appear such as: “No valid role group found in user groups: 9002 123 5340”.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as a ‘root’ user and clear the information in /etc/libnss-udr/passwd.
bugs.fix: The remote-gid functionality will no longer be affected by changing authentication methods from RADIUS/TACACS to LDAP. LDAP users with valid credentials will be allowed in.

bugs.title: Qkview does not collect the files gid-map.txt, /etc/libnss-udr/passwd, or /etc/libnss-udr/group
bugs.symptoms: When a QKView is collected, the files gid-map.txt, /etc/libnss-udr/passwd, and /etc/libnss-udr/group are not present in the QKView.
bugs.conditions: A qkview is collected.
bugs.impact: It may not be possible to troubleshoot certain issues related to authentication.
