bugs.conditions: -- rSeries 5xxx, 10xxx, 12xxx system -- Upgrade to version 1.8.0 build 16036
bugs.impact: Spontaneous system restart could occur.
bugs.workaround: A BIOS change occurred in the F5OS 1.8.0 build 16036 upgrade that enables CMS ENABLE DRAM PM. Disabling it will mitigate this. For instructions on how to perform this procedure, see K000148566: F5 rSeries systems may silently reboot after upgrading to F5OS-A 1.8.0 at https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000148566.
bugs.fix: Fixes introduced in F5OS-A-1.8.0-17564.R5R10.EHF-1.iso

bugs.title: F5 rSeries ATSE v72.5.6.00 firmware
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries ATSE v72.5.6.00 firmware
bugs.conditions: F5 r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance. This update is not applicable to F5 r2000 or r4000-series appliances.
bugs.impact: NA
bugs.fix: Fixes ATSE receive lockup issue.

bugs.title: Tmm may egress broadcast traffic even when VLANs are disabled in F5OS
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios such as restoring a UCS on an F5OS tenant, if the VLANs in F5OS are disabled, tmm may egress broadcast traffic such as gratuitous ARPs onto the disabled VLANs.
bugs.conditions: -- An F5OS tenant where VLANs were assigned and then removed. -- An F5OS tenant where tmm is not in forced-offline mode. -- An action occurs on the tenant (such as restoring a UCS or restarting tmm, or loading the config) that results in gratuitous ARPs.
bugs.impact: This could cause IP address conflicts on the network or other issues related to unexpected broadcast traffic such as gratuitous ARPs on the network.
bugs.workaround: - In F5OS, remove the affected VLANs from the LAG or interface. - On the tenant use forced offline to prevent traffic egress. - If you are restoring a UCS from another BIG-IP such as for a platform migration, put the source BIG-IP into forcedoffline state before taking the UCS. - delete the tenant, and recreate without any VLANs assigned.
bugs.fix: A single tenant with a vlan that was configured and then removed via F5OS will no longer leak broadcast traffic onto the network on the removed vlan. This fix does not address the issue when multiple tenants are attached to the same vlan. F5 has created ID1758957 for that issue.

bugs.title: Snmp is not working if mgmt is in 172.17.x.x network in 1.8.0
bugs.symptoms: The snmpwalk command times out after an upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- The management IP address is in the 172.17.x.x network -- The system is upgraded from 1.5.2
bugs.impact: The snmpwalk command fails if the management IP is in 172.17.x.x network in 1.8.0
bugs.workaround: Remove the iptables entries with 172.x network as source from the file /etc/sysconfig/iptables and reboot the system Steps are as below Verify existing entries: # iptables-save | grep 172.17 -A POSTROUTING -s 172.17.0.0/16 ! -o br-97c791a9e730 -j MASQUERADE -A POSTROUTING -s 172.17.0.0/16 ! -o br-e4f09d90e378 -j MASQUERADE Make a backup of the iptables file # cp /etc/sysconfig/iptables /etc/sysconfig/iptables.bak Edit the entries in the iptables file # grep -v '＼-s 172.' /etc/sysconfig/iptables.bak > /etc/sysconfig/iptables Run this command: # iptables-save | grep -vF 172.17.0.0/16 > iptables Reboot the device: # reboot Verify entries. Either of these commands should return no results # iptables-save | grep 172.17 # grep '172.17' /etc/sysconfig/iptables
bugs.fix: During the upgrade from 1.5.2 to any higher version, the iptables for default docker network (172 network) are removed

bugs.title: Add notification to set-version when downgrading the system from F5OS-A/C-1.8.0
bugs.symptoms: A downgrade to an earlier version of F5OS from F5OS-A/C 1.8.0 can leave the system inoperable. Refer to ID1712009 for more information.
bugs.conditions: Perform a config-restore or config reset-to-default operation to an earlier version of F5OS.
bugs.impact: A downgraded system may be inoperable.
bugs.workaround: Refer to ID1712009 for workaround.
bugs.fix: There is an issue with performing a config-restore after downgrading from F5OS-A/C 1.8.0 (ID1712009). If you intend to perform a config-restore or config reset-to-default operation, please refer to the F5OS-A/C 1.8.0 release notes for information on avoiding this issue.

bugs.title: On rSeries System, QAT devices are not visible after restoring the config backup file
bugs.symptoms: QAT devices are not visible in confd through output of "show cluster nodes node state crypto tenants tenant"
bugs.conditions: After backup-restore through confd
bugs.impact: No functional impact
bugs.workaround: Reboot to recover

bugs.title: F5 rSeries ATSE v72.41.6.00 firmware
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries ATSE v72.41.6.00 firmware
bugs.conditions: F5 r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance. This update is not applicable to F5 r2000 or r4000-series appliances.
bugs.fix: Fixes ATSE receive lockup issue.

bugs.title: ConfD encryption key is recreated when there is an error reading it from the hardware TPM
bugs.symptoms: F5OS stores the encryption key in the hardware TPM module. This is used to encrypt and decrypt sensitive data in the database, and is read at system startup and periodically during normal execution (during "key migrations"). If there is an issue reading the key from the TPM, a new key will be generated and store it in the TPM. The problem is that the database is still encrypted using the old key, and as soon as the system restarts it will run into errors when attempting to decrypt using the new key.
bugs.conditions: Issue is observed intermittently when TPM module encounters ownership contention.
bugs.impact: System encryption key gets corrupted.
bugs.fix: The symptom causing the tpm ownership has been fixed and removed unnecessary ownership calls.

bugs.title: XBAR rate limit not updated when modifying LAG
bugs.symptoms: Traffic performance may be degraded.
bugs.conditions: Add or remove a LAG member when the total speed is less than 100G.
bugs.impact: Degraded performance.
bugs.workaround: Disable and re-enable an interface.

bugs.title: F5OS STP with LAG sends BPDU on single interface regardless of member interface status
bugs.symptoms: BPDU packets are transmitted on only one LAG member interface even when that interface is down. Traffic does not pass even though everything seems in the correct state.
bugs.conditions: F5OS system configured with Link Aggregation Groups (LAG). LAG interfaces participating in Spanning Tree Protocol (STP/RSTP/MSTP). Multiple physical interfaces configured as LAG members. One or more LAG member interfaces become disabled or go down.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted.
bugs.fix: Enhanced STP to properly monitor LACP state changes and select active LAG member interfaces for BPDU transmission. System now detects and reacts to LACP state changes in real-time, ensuring BPDU packets are sent on operational LAG member interfaces only.

bugs.title: VLAN unassigned from Tenant followed by VLAN deletion may result in error
bugs.symptoms: If a VLAN is unassigned from a Tenant and then quickly deleted from the system, an error might be returned from the VLAN deletion: "illegal reference /vlan-listeners/vlan-listener{0.host 1234}/vlan"
bugs.conditions: A VLAN is deleted from the system immediately after being unassigned from a tenant.
bugs.impact: The VLAN deletion operation will fail.
bugs.workaround: The deletion operation can be retried, or wait a moment after unassigning the VLAN before deleting it.
bugs.fix: This fix changes the FDB and Vlan-Listener database schema and api. The Vlan-Listener config mode api has been removed. The Vlan-Listener state table remains as the way to view Vlan-Listener information. An example of the state table is: f5-vlan-listeners:vlan-listeners/vlan-listener=<interface>,<vlan-id>/state The FDB config mode api now only exists to configure Static FDBs. Any FDB created in config mode will be treated as a Static FDB. Non-Static FDBs created by the system will no longer be shown in config mode. Viewing FDB information on the system remains at the same path for Static FDBs. This path is: f5-l2fdb:fdb/mac-table/ Viewing Non-Static FDB information on the system has moved to: f5-l2fdb:fdb/mac-table-l2listeners/

bugs.title: PAM faillock data is deleted on restart, allowing users to log in immediately
bugs.symptoms: The administrator can set up the max-login-failures (Number of unsuccessful login attempts allowed before lockout) to a non-zero number. Also, the unlock-timeout can be increased from the default value of 60 seconds. Once the number of failed login attempts is reached, then the user must wait the alotted unlock-timeout period before being allowed to login with the correct credentials. The number of login-failures for each user is currently reset to zero upon a system reboot.
bugs.conditions: Rebooting simply eliminates the tally count of login failures for all users.
bugs.impact: The max-login-failures setting is set back to zero if the system is rebooted.

bugs.title: Error when creating a server-group name with an embedded space
bugs.symptoms: An error log inside 'platform.log' for the rSeries systems or 'velos.log' in the VELOS systems when you configure a server-group name with an embedded space. In velos.log on F5OS-C or platform.log on F5OS-A: appliance-1 authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000109 msg="Failed to set element in cdb." path="/system/aaa/server-groups/server-group" error="Bad key "my server group" (wrong number of identifiers) at: /system/aaa/server-groups/server-group" errno="Exec format error".
bugs.conditions: Creating a server-group name with an embedded space. Example: my server group
bugs.impact: The configuration change will not take an effect.
bugs.workaround: Remove all spaces from the server-group name. For example, if the server-group name with a space was 'my server group', you can rename it into 'my_server_group' and re-configure the rest of the values. appliance-1(config)# system aaa server-groups server-group my_server_group config name my_server_group appliance-1(config)#commit
bugs.fix: Avoid embedded spaces when you create server-group names.

bugs.title: Multiple docker containers can get assigned the same bridge IP during rolling upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Multiple containers can get the same bridge IP during a rolling upgrade or docker restart [root@controller-2 ~]# docker inspect controller-services-registry-2502 | grep IPAddress "SecondaryIPAddresses": null, "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", [root@controller-2 ~]# docker inspect partition-services-registry-2202 | grep IPAddress "SecondaryIPAddresses": null, "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", "IPAddress": "100.64.0.2", There's a race in IP address allocation in Docker.
bugs.conditions: When multiple containers start at the same time.
bugs.impact: This causes one of the two containers to answer requests depending on which container last refreshed the arp cache. The other container does not work properly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.
bugs.fix: Docker address allocator uses bit map to manage IP address pool but it's not thread safe. Now, set/unset bitmap operations are protected by a lock.

bugs.title: Active Directory LDAP integration without uidNumber/gidNumber does not work after system reboot
bugs.symptoms: After an rSeries appliance reboot, Active Directory LDAP authentication configured with "Unix Attributes" set to false does not work and users from Active Directory are unable to authenticate with the F5OS system. There will be messages similar to the following logged in platform.log shortly after the reboot: authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000101 msg="LDAP API error during : -" oper="SASL bind" code=-1 msg="Can't contact LDAP server". authd[8]: priority="Warn" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000098 msg="Unable to retrieve domain Sid for supplied servers and domains; server will be treated as if it has unix attributes present.".
bugs.conditions: - F5OS device configured with Active Directory LDAP authentication, and the "Unix Attributes" setting configured as false. - System reboots
bugs.impact: LDAP remote authentication does not work.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue on an rSeries appliance, create a cron task to restart the system_user_manager and authentication-mgr docker containers after a system reboot: 1. Log into the system as root and create /etc/cron.d/ldap-post-reboot with these contents (not including the '==='): === # Workaround for post-reboot issue with LDAP auth (ID1782925) # # In the the first five minutes after the system reboots, assume the first # instance of the following log message that we see is a result of the management # port lack of connectivity when the docker containers start up, and restart both # system_user_manager and authentication-mgr once. # # authd[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x3901000000000101 msg="LDAP API error during : -" oper="SASL bind" code=-1 msg="Can't contact LDAP server". @reboot root timeout 5m sh -c 'tail -n0 -F /var/F5/system/log/platform.log | grep -a -m1 authd.*0x3901000000000101 && sleep 20s && echo Restarting authd and user-manager && docker restart system_user_manager authentication-mgr' || echo "Timed out" === This mitigation may fail under some corner cases, e.g. potentially after an upgrade or if something goes wrong with the platform services such that they don't start up within the first five minutes after system boot. In those circumstances, log into the system as root and restart the system_user_manager and authentication-mgr containers: docker restart system_user_manager authentication-mgr

bugs.title: ATSE Datapath lockup on HBM calibration issue
bugs.symptoms: Datapath lockup in the ATSE FPGA. Can be seen at startup with no traffic received at the host, or some time after startup with packet framing errors. This can also show up as a transmit packet path lockup because health check loopback packets can back up into the transmit datapath and block it.
bugs.conditions: No known conditions.
bugs.impact: The impact is no packets can get from the network to host for processing.
bugs.workaround: The datapath lockup requires a reload of the ATSE FPGA. Reload typically done by rebooting the system. This issue has been fixed in ATSE bitfiles v72.5.8.00 and v72.41.8.0 and all newer bitfiles.
bugs.fix: The issue is an FPGA memory reset procedure. The HBM memory inside the ATSE FPGA has a very specific bringup procedure. There was an issue with the initial implementation of that procedure.

bugs.title: SNMP bulk queries for LAGs on VELOS might return incomplete information
bugs.symptoms: SNMP queries for interface statistics for a LAG might return incomplete information
bugs.conditions: - VELOS partition - Querying SNMP for LAGs - The LAG contains multiple members - The SNMP client is issuing bulk SNMP queries - The SNMP client queries for the first member of the LAG, skips another member of the LAG, and then queries information for the LAG
bugs.impact: The SNMP statistics reported by the VELOS system could possibly return incomplete information (failing to include statistics from one or more of the members of the LAG).
bugs.fix: The system will now correctly report SNMP statistics for LAGs.

bugs.title: If 'ldap-group is configured for a role but LDAP search fails, users with the default GID for the role can still get those privileges
bugs.symptoms: When an 'ldap-group' mapping is configured for a F5OS role, and the mapping fails (because the filter is invalid or the LDAP query of remote groups fails for some other reason), the default mapping for the role (or, what is configured in 'remote-gid' for the role) is still used. For example, if you were attempting to map the F5OS role 'admin' (default GID 9000) to an LDAP group 'CN=my-ldapgroup', and the LDAP search for that group failed (because the provided filter was invalid, the group does not exist, etc.), users with GID 9000 would still be able to authenticate and login with 'admin' privileges.
bugs.conditions: 1. LDAP authentication is enabled. 2. A role mapping is applied via the 'ldap-group' configuration for a F5OS role. 3. The provided 'ldap-group' filter is invalid or another unexpected issue is encountered when querying the LDAP server.
bugs.impact: Users can login with privileges in excess of what one might expect given the system configuration.
bugs.workaround: If the LDAP group/users have Posix attributes ('gidNumber'), it is possible to map the F5OS role using this GID number by specifying it in the 'remote-gid' configuration under the role. If this is not feasible, it is possible to directly validate the 'ldap-group' mapping was successful by inspecting this file from a bash shell: [root@appliance-1(test):Active] ~ # cat /etc/ldap-gid-map.txt 1108:=9000 If there is an entry that has the default GID for the role on the right-hand side of ':=' in this file, it means the mapping was applied successfully and users with the default or 'remote-gid' GID will not be able to obtain the role permissions. If such an entry is missing, you will need to fix the 'ldap-group' filter so an LDAP query of the group can be successful.
bugs.fix: If a configured 'ldap-group' mapping fails, deny all role-based access for the mapped role until it is fixed or de-configured.

bugs.title: F5OS device fails to block port based on STP path cost
bugs.symptoms: F5OS fails to change the port to BLOCK based on STP Path Cost.
bugs.conditions: Large path cost applied to a port that is still in a Forwarding state.
bugs.impact: The port is not blocked in the STP topology which leads to loop.

bugs.title: Restoring a backup with an SNMP user on a system with a different SNMP Engine ID will duplicate the SNMP user
bugs.symptoms: If you restore a backup containing an SNMP user, but the SNMP user’s SNMP Engine ID does not match the current system, a new SNMP user will be created with the same name and the current system’s SNMP Engine ID. However, this is only seen when the database is later backed up.
bugs.conditions: -- Restoring a database backup that contains an SNMP user. -- Doing the restore on a system with a different SNMP Engine ID.
bugs.impact: Two SNMP users with the same name (but different SNMP Engine IDs) are saved to subsequent backups. SNMP will not work.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the SNMP user authentication and privacy passwords after restoring the backup. SNMP will work after configuring passwords.
bugs.fix: When backup is restored on a system with a different EngineID, SNMP might not work for SNMP users. However, it can be mitigated by reconfiguring the SNMP user authentication and privacy passwords after restoring the backup.

bugs.title: DDM system alarms triggered when interface is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Running 'show system alarms' reports "Portgroup <N> ERROR Lanes: 1 Transmitter power low alarm"
bugs.conditions: Disabling an interface locally
bugs.impact: Transmitter power low and transmitter bias low alarms occur.
bugs.workaround: To clear the alarms, workaround provided in article K000150155 can be followed.

bugs.title: Insufficient memory on node, retrying tenant deployment
bugs.symptoms: A tenant fails to deploy. The output of the 'show tenant' command: INSTANCE TENANT CREATION READY MGMT NODE POD NAME ID SLOT PHASE TIME TIME STATUS MAC ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 1 tenant-1 1 1 Insufficient memory on node, retrying tenant deployment - Errors in platform.log: 2024-12-21T16:19:02.370251+08:00 TENANT-1 orchestration-agent[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x506000000000042 msg="Failed to allocate memory for tenant" TENANT="tenant-1" node=1. 2024-12-21T16:19:35.547187+08:00 TENANT-1 orchestration-agent[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x507000000000004 msg="Unable to fetch VFs pci address from filesystem". 2024-12-21T16:19:40.757952+08:00 TENANT-1 orchestration-agent[7]: priority="Info" version=1.0 msgid=0x507000000000006 msg="SR-IOV DP pod is at running/ready state, able to access VFs". 2024-12-21T16:20:12.814467+08:00 TENANT-1 orchestration-agent[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x506000000000040 msg="Timeout waiting for response from NodeAgent" TENANT="tenant-1" NODE=1. 2024-12-21T16:20:12.814506+08:00 TENANT-1 orchestration-agent[7]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x506000000000042 msg="Failed to allocate memory for tenant" TENANT="tenant-1" node=1.
bugs.conditions: Exact conditions are unknown. It has been observed after upgrading from F5OS 1.5.2 to 1.8.0.
bugs.impact: Tenants will not start. The GUI reports "Insufficient memory on node, retrying tenant deployment".

bugs.title: Daemons that handle ZMQ messages may crash under certain conditions.
Orchestration Agent process may core
Users unable to login after reboot with LDAP group configured
bugs.symptoms: - CLI/GUI access for all roles other than admin and root is denied - The GUI permit user authentication and then immediately terminate the session; for more information, refer to https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1933645.html. - Repeated log messages from user-manager in platform.log / velos.log with an error of "Lost connection to ConfD" / "Socket to ConfD is closed": user-manager[17]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6802000000000001 msg="cdb_get failed for" ATTRIBUTE="rolename" ERRNOSTR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="Socket to ConfD is closed" ERRNO=45.
bugs.conditions: - LDAP system authentication is enabled - A LDAP group is defined for a role in the system - Queries to the LDAP server take a long time, for example due to connection timeouts or LDAP referral chasing. This issue can also occur when the system is rebooted if user-manager tries to perform LDAP queries before the management network is accessible.
bugs.impact: Users with roles other than admin and root cannot login using CLI or GUI
bugs.workaround: 1. Restart the appropriate user-manager container (system_user_manager on rSeries appliances, controller-userman for VELOS system controllers, and partition<ID>_user_manager for VELOS partitions) 2. Disable LDAP system authentication or remove the LDAP group definitions, and then restart the user-manager container. This will restore connectivity for locally-defined users.
bugs.fix: Fix users unable to login after reboot with LDAP group configured

bugs.title: Optic removed while system down does not get removed from ConfD state
bugs.symptoms: The fpgamgr publishes portgroup state data to ConfD when an optic is inserted in the system. The portgroup state data is erased from ConfD when the optic is removed while the system is operational. If an optic is removed while the system is down the portgroup state data does not get erased.
bugs.conditions: Optic is removed while the system is down.
bugs.impact: Unexpected/undesired operational data appearing in ConfD output.
bugs.fix: Erased the portgroup operational data if the corresponding optic is not present.

bugs.title: Stp stats (ex counters) are not reset when stp mode removed and added again.
bugs.symptoms: Stp stats (ex counters) are not reset to 0 when stp mode removed and added again. steps add STP > stp global config enabled-protocol STP > stp interfaces <> > stp stp interfaces <> remove STP > no stp stp interfaces > no stp interfaces > no stp global config add stp mode > stp global config enabled-protocol RSTP > stp interfaces <> > stp rstp interfaces <> check stp states and check "BPDU RECEIVED" > show stp old BPDU's counters are not reset to 0.
bugs.conditions: STP mode is removed and added again.
bugs.impact: No impact on functionality but you will see old BPDU's counter stats base instead of starting from 0.
bugs.workaround: There is no impact on functionality but restart of the device will reset the stats counters.

bugs.title: Memory leak in l2_agent daemon on F5OS
bugs.symptoms: - Large memory consumption by the l2_agent. - Tenant disruption on F5 rSeries appliance.
bugs.conditions: - An F5OS system with SNMP configured and a LAG (Link Aggregation Group) with more than 1 member. - SNMP monitoring in use. We can check the l2_agent memory consumption by using `top` command. Ex: Top output showed a 15GB l2_agent process: PID USER PR NI VIRT RES SHR S %CPU %MEM TIME+ COMMAND 19454 root 20 0 17.3g 14.9g 1788 S 0.0 5.9 174:04.57 /confd/bin/l2_agent -s appliance-1
bugs.impact: Eventually the system experience OOM (Out of Memory). On an F5 rSeries appliance, a tenant might experience disruptions and slowness, up to and including a TMM SIGABRT core.
bugs.fix: The l2_agent process no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: Port not enabling after SFP connection when previously disabled
bugs.symptoms: The port is disabled, and after connecting the optic to it, enabling the port does not bring it up automatically
bugs.conditions: When Optics connected to a disabled port
bugs.impact: Link is not coming up
bugs.workaround: Remove and reconnected the SFP after port is enabled.

bugs.title: CVE 2020-27743: pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes().
bugs.symptoms: libtac in pam_tacplus through 1.5.1 lacks a check for a failure of RAND_bytes()/RAND_pseudo_bytes(). This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id.
bugs.conditions: The current version pam_tacplus from version 1.6.0 doesn't have the fix as this was added in version 1.6.1 source package.
bugs.impact: This could lead to use of a non-random/predictable session_id which means an adversary could gain access.
bugs.fix: By updating the pam_tacplus source code to 1.7.0 where the vulnerability was fixed in 1.6.1, the new code does not have this issue.

bugs.title: REST API for Docker Restart command fails
bugs.symptoms: The endpoint restconf/data/openconfig-system:system/f5-system-diagnostics-qkview:diagnostics/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:os-utils/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:docker/f5-system-diagnostics-docker:restart can be used (with POST) to restart some Docker containers. However it will fail with the message "restart aborted", e.g.: { "f5-system-diagnostics-docker:output": { "result": "snmpd restart aborted" } }
bugs.conditions: Attempting to restart a Docker container using the REST API.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the REST API to restart a Docker container.
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI instead: config system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node <node> service <service>

bugs.title: BIOS boot may be much slower than normal, if Full Disk Encryption (FDE) is enabled and the BIOS cannot communicate with the configured KMIP servers
bugs.symptoms: It may take up to 50 minutes for the BIOS to finish booting and display the BIOS banner. The BIOS will still display the normal sequence of POST codes on the serial console, but it may pause at POST code 92 for much longer than normal. (Note that when all KMIP servers are unreachable, by design the drives will remain locked and the system will not boot to F5OS. This is intended behavior and ensures the security of data stored on the drives.)
bugs.conditions: -- Devices with Full Disk Encryption (FDE) enabled. -- Booting the system. This issue may occur if FDE is enabled and the local management IP, subnet mask, or gateway is misconfigured (for example, if the gateway is outside of the subnet). It may also occur if FDE is enabled and the configured KMIP servers repeatedly do not respond to connection attempts (for example, if a network partition causes the KMIP servers to be unreachable).
bugs.impact: BIOS boot may be much slower than normal.

bugs.title: L2 Port motion events are not generated for certain port combinations on r10k.
bugs.symptoms: Missing port-motion events between interfaces on r10k platform can result in missing L2 entries.
bugs.impact: Missing port-motion causes missing L2 entries, resulting in excessive DLFs.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that ports used in redundancy configurations are not in the same set of affected ports listed above.
bugs.fix: Configure the L2 FDB table so port-motion is detected between the affected sets of ports.

bugs.title: High memory utilization by NetworkManager
bugs.symptoms: After a VELOS system controller, blade, or rSeries appliance has been running for several hundred days, the NetworkManager service may start leaking memory. This will eventually result in system instability including a failover between system controllers, or instability to tenants. Log messages similar to the following occurring in /var/log/messages or the systemd journal: controller-2.chassis.local NetworkManager[180091]: gsignal.c:2642: instance '0x564069a2be40' has no handler with id '34120' Prior to these log messages being generated, there is no way to tell if the issue is close to occurring.
bugs.conditions: The NetworkManager service has been running for a substantial period of time (i.e. more than 500 days).
bugs.impact: NetworkManager service utilizes high memory in the system, which leads to controller failover.
bugs.workaround: Restart NetworkManager by logging in to the appropriate device as root (system controller, blade, or appliance) and running the command "systemctl restart NetworkManager".

bugs.title: Egress traffic is being dropped by upstream switch following a reboot of rSeries.
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently observed egress packets sent from the rSeries device through a specific port are discarded by the adjacent device.
bugs.conditions: - r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance - Intermittently occurs when a link is brought up during boot, for instance after multiple reboot attempts.
bugs.impact: Traffic on the affected port is completely dropped when the system comes up after a reboot. This includes the failure of all Layer 2 (L2) protocols, such as LACP, STP, and LLDP, along with tenant traffic.
bugs.workaround: An additional reboot helps to recover the system.

bugs.title: "Failed to write to cdb" and "Unable to set STP VLAN state" error logs are seen with MSTP configuration deletion via CLI
bugs.symptoms: Stpd and FPGA error logs are observed while doing MSTP configuration. In platform.log: stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="MST Instance mst-id" ERRNO=8 ERRNOSTR="badly formatted or nonexistent path". stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="MST Instance designated-root-address" ERRNO=8 ERRNOSTR="badly formatted or nonexistent path". stpd[1]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6102000000000018 msg="Failed to write to cdb" FIELD="WriteTenantOperMSTInstance failed" ERRNO=0 ERRNOSTR="Unknown error".
bugs.conditions: 1. Create VLANs. 2. Attach VLANs to the interfaces. 3. Enable MSTP using webUI. Select Network Settings > STP configuration and select MSTP. 4. Create an instance(1) and attach a VLAN to it (created VLANs). 5. Add the interfaces to instance 1. 6. Delete mstp instance. 7. You will observe errors under platform.log.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on MSTP behavior and convergence.

bugs.title: GUI immediately logs user off with "User Session Terminated" error and "validator" process cores
bugs.symptoms: After logging into the device, the GUI immediately reports "User Session Terminated. You will be logged out of the application." Core files generated from the "validator" process in the confd container (system_manager, vcc-confd, or partition<X>_manager).
bugs.conditions: Trying to login to the GUI, and the "limited" group is missing from /etc/group. The "limited" group is an internal role that should always be defined and cannot be deleted by a user. The most likely reason for it to be missing is https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.impact: Users are not able to access the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Apply a workaround for https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1858617.html
bugs.fix: Even if the "limited" group goes missing, users should still be able to access the GUI.

bugs.title: Infrequent and uneven traffic to front panel LAGs can lead to premature aging of L2 events
bugs.symptoms: For front panel LAGs on rSeries which span FPGAs (1.0/11.0, 2.0/12.0, etc) infrequent traffic which is not evenly distributed across the LAG members can lead to premature aging of L2 entries.
bugs.conditions: - r10000 or r12000-series appliance - LAG members spanning FPGAs and minimal incoming traffic on the LAG can cause premature aging of L2 entries when the traffic isn't evenly distributed among LAG members.
bugs.impact: Missing L2 entries can cause excessive DLFs until the MAC address is re-learned.
bugs.workaround: Re-configure the LAG members such that they connect to the same FPGA (1.0/2.0, 11.0/12.0). Interfaces 1.0 through 10.0 are on one FPGA, and interfaces 11.0 through 20.0 are on the other FPGA.
bugs.fix: Ensure L2 age events are handled for all LAG members.

bugs.title: Qkview-collect crashes while collecting a QKView
bugs.symptoms: Qkview-collect may crash when collecting a QKView.
bugs.conditions: This happens intermittently when collecting a QKView.
bugs.impact: Unable to collect a QKView.

bugs.title: L2 Port motion events are not generated between ports hosted by the same FPGA
bugs.symptoms: Missing port-motion events between interfaces on r15k/r10k platform can result in missing L2 entries.
bugs.conditions: Port-motion between the following sets of ports on the r5k appliance: 1.0 - 2.0 3.0 - 7.0 4.0 - 8.0 5.0 - 9.0 6.0 - 10.0 In addition, the following ports on the r10k are affected: 11.0 - 12.0 13.0 - 17.0 14.0 - 18.0 15.0 - 19.0 16.0 - 20.0
bugs.impact: Missing port-motion causes missing L2 entries, resulting in excessive DLFs.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that ports used in redundancy configurations are not in the same set of affected ports listed above.

bugs.title: Confd.smp memory consumption spikes high with snmpEnableAuthenTraps enabled
bugs.symptoms: When config-restore is performed on a RMA system, with the configuration of SNMPv3 users and targets and snmpEnableAuthenTraps enabled, observed confd.smp process memory spikes increase and causes OOM after system reboot.
bugs.conditions: Restoring the configuration onto an RMA replacement system.
bugs.impact: Confd's RSS memory begins to grow rapidly and causes restart of ConfD process.
bugs.workaround: The available workarounds, 1. After performing config-restore on a RMA system, disable snmpEnableAuthenTraps 2. Reset all SNMPv3 users and passwords right after performing config-restore.
bugs.fix: Disabling snmpEnableAuthenTraps when the engine-id of the database backup and the system engine-id. This will prevent confd.smp process memory hike in case of any sudden reboot of the system. User can reconfigure the snmpEnableAuthenTraps after reseting the SNMPv3 users authentication and privacy password.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Tenant's VM will be patched/relaunched everytime after system reboot/upgrade/failover/TPOB restart
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from F5OS v1.6.1/1.7.0 to v1.8.x, tenant VMs were being unnecessarily patched and recreated, VM patches also not being properly applied.
bugs.conditions: - System upgraded from F5OS-C v1.6.1 or v1.7.0 to v1.8.x. - System reboot, failover, or TPOB restart occurs.
bugs.impact: Tenant VMs were being unnecessarily patched and relaunched after every reboot.
bugs.workaround: None. Recommended to upgrade to F5OS-C v1.8.3 which includes this fix.
bugs.fix: These changes prevent unnecessary VM patching and recreation after system upgrades, reboots, or TPOB restarts while ensuring legitimate patches are properly applied.

bugs.title: In IPv6-only environment, remote authentication using RADIUS server by hostname may not work
bugs.symptoms: F5OS remote authentication does not work. Administrator can observe F5OS performing DNS resolution of the configured RADIUS server, but F5OS never transmits RADIUS Access-Request packets to the server.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS host is configured with only an IPv6 management IP address. - RADIUS remote authentication configured with a RADIUS server specified via hostname. - RADIUS server hostname has both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (i.e. both A and AAAA records in DNS)
bugs.impact: Remote authentication does not work.
bugs.workaround: Create a separate hostname for the RADIUS server that only resolves to an IPv6 address.

bugs.title: RADIUS remote authentication specifying IPv6 server addresses does not work
bugs.symptoms: F5OS does not send RADIUS Access-Request messages to a server specified as an IPv6 address. No messages are transmitted at all. When attempting authentication against SSH, log messages similar to the following are in /var/log/secure: sshd[30736]: pam_radius_auth: Failed looking up IP address for RADIUS server [2001:db8::1] (errcode=9)
bugs.conditions: F5OS remote authentication configured with a server defined by IPv6 address.
bugs.impact: F5OS remote authentication does not work.
bugs.workaround: Reference the RADIUS server by DNS hostname rather than IP address. Important: The DNS hostname should only only resolve to IPv6 addresses, and not also be associated with an IPv4 address; for more information, refer to ID1975245: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1975245.html

bugs.title: Logging from PAM modules only seen for SSH authentication, and not GUI/API authentication
bugs.symptoms: Logging from PAM modules (e.g. pam_unix, pam_radius_auth, or pam_unix) is only captured in system logs when a user attempts to authenticate via SSH; no such logging occurs when authenticating via the F5OS GUI or API.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS system - Attempting to troubleshoot issues related to authentication
bugs.impact: PAM module log messages are not logged anywhere. The system does generate authentication success/failure messages that are captured in the audit.log, e.g.: audit-service[12]: priority="Notice" version=1.0 msgid=0x1f03000000000012 msg="User authentication failed" reason="Invalid login attempt, user-id/password is incorrect" failcount=8 user="otters".
bugs.workaround: When troubleshooting authentication issues, attempt to log in via SSH. PAM modules will generate log messages that are captured in /var/log/secure and the systemd journal.

bugs.title: System primary key is recreated when there is an error reading it from the hardware TPM
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS appliances, if there is an error reading from the hardware TPM at some point, the system primary key is recreated but the ConfD database is not re-encrypted. When the system restarts at some point in the future, F5OS will be unable to decrypt the encrypted parts of the ConfD database, and will be unable to start up properly. When the TPM read error happens, the following message is logged in the platform.log file: "tpm has no data, writing new key" However, the administrator will not notice a problem until the system is restarted. The restart could happen a significant time after the rewrite, and the above message may no longer be in the platform.log file. After the restart, "Key header check failed" errors will be logged by the api-svc-gateway and orchestration-agent components. Note that these messages alone are not a definite indicator that the primary key was rewritten, as other issues can cause them to occur.
bugs.conditions: -- rSeries appliance -- The system has been restarted after F5OS encounters an error when reading from the TPM.
bugs.impact: After the restart, the system is unusable and needs to be recreated.

bugs.title: Config backup and restore is failing after downgrading from 2.0 to lower versions
bugs.symptoms: When restoring a configuration from backup, the restore action fails with an error: Error: response 'Failed.' confd_load: 662: maapi_apply_trans_flags(sock, tid, 0, aflags) failed: external error (19): /oc-sys:system/f5-security-ciphers:security/ services/service{httpd}/config/ssl-ciphersuite: Invalid openssl cipher received: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
bugs.conditions: -- Config backup is taken after downgrading from 2.0. -- The backup file is used to restore the configuration.
bugs.impact: Config restore fails due to unsupported ciphers present.
bugs.workaround: There are three possible workarounds: -- The issue will not be seen if rollback is applied before downgrading from 2.0 -- Issue will not be seen if config-backup is taken before upgrading to 2.0 from lower versions and then config-restore is applied after downgrading to lower versions. -- If config-backup is not taken before upgrading to 2.0, then after downgrading to lower versions, execute "no system security services service httpd" before taking config-backup.

bugs.title: VLAN cannot be deleted after removing all tenant and interface references
bugs.symptoms: If a box experiences hitting Bug ID 1759761, sometimes the workaround for that bug does not always work. The currently published workaround for that bug is: "The [vlan] deletion operation can be retried, or wait a moment after unassigning the VLAN before deleting it." However, in some cases the vlan delete will always fail because the vlan-listener for the tenant is never removed. Which means every attempt to delete the vlan will fail until the vlan-listener is removed, and any lingering fdb entries. You will see one or even a handful of vlan listeners that should not exist anymore.
bugs.conditions: Sometimes it will take several iterations for the vlan-listener to not be deleted in time. It's possible enabling network-manager and api-svc-gw debug logging increases the probability of hitting this bug. 1. Create and deploy a tenant 2. Copy the bash script vlan.tenant.tort.bsh to an external client 3. Modify the script to match rseries or partition mgmt ip, username, password and tenant name: ex. PARTITION_MGMT_IP=172.12.12.12 USERNAME=admin PASSWORD=admin TENANT=rdt1 4. run show vlan-listener | repeat 1 on the rSeries 5. run the script: while :;do date;bash vlan.tenant.tort.bsh 1;echo "sleeping for 10";sleep 10;done 6. As soon as the script reports it's sleeping for 10 seconds, check to see if the vlan-listener still exists from the output of #5. If its still there for 2+ seconds; kill the bash script to leave the device in that state.
bugs.impact: VLAN-listener does not get deleted, and will show disabled.
bugs.workaround: There are two delays needed, which I know is less then ideal. One for Bug ID 1759761 which is before removing the vlan entirely. and A second one for Bug ID 1983061 before removing the vlan from the tenant. And both bugs are resolved by the change for 1759761 which is fixed in F5OS v2.0.0 and is unfortunately not backportable.
bugs.fix: Fixed in version 2.0.0.

bugs.title: Tenant experiences master key decrypt error after F5OS api-svc-gateway restart
bugs.symptoms: After the F5OS API service gateway (api-svc-gateway) restarts, tenants may experience SecureVault errors while attempting to decrypt the master key. The tenant will be inoperative. Logs similar to the following will be present in F5OS: api-svc-gateway[13]: nodename=blade-2(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x5803000000000011 msg="Crypto key installation failed:" ERRNOSTR="Lost connection to ConfD" LASTERR="EOF on socket to ConfD" ERRNO=45 api-svc-gateway[13]: nodename=blade-2(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x5804000000000027 msg="No unit key was found in confd for tenant" TENANT="tenant1" Logs similar to the following in the tenant: err mcpd[5803]: 010713d0:3: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt failure - decrypt failure notice mcpd[5803]: 01071029:5: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt notice mcpd[5803]: 01071027:5: Master key OpenSSL error: 4007094004:error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt:evp_enc.c:664:
bugs.conditions: Issue is observed rarely when there is a recent restart (or power-cycle) of the system (specifically after a restart of the F5OS api-svc-gateway container).
bugs.impact: Unable to access tenants. Tenant restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restart the API service gateway and ensure it does not log errors while retrieving the tenant unit keys. If the problem persists, restart the tenants. If the problem continues to persist after number of tenant restarts, deploy new tenant and load UCS.

bugs.title: F5OS SCP hardening
Privilege Escalation to Admin via SSH Port Forwarding
Tcpdump may crash with "malloc(): corrupted top size" when using complex BPF filters
bugs.symptoms: Running tcpdump with complex or long BPF filter expressions may result in a crash with the error message: malloc(): corrupted top size
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when tcpdump is invoked with a filter expression containing multiple conditions or a long filter string, especially when run via the system diagnostics
bugs.impact: Packet capture operations fails and no data is collected. This may impact troubleshooting or monitoring activities that rely on tcpdump.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump has been updated to reliably support complex and long filter expressions. The utility now validates filter input to prevent errors, ensuring stable and consistent packet capture operations

bugs.title: Confd call "system disk-encryption validate-kmip" fails intermittently with a time out error
bugs.symptoms: The execution of the "system disk-encryption validate-kmip" operation in ConfD experiences intermittent failures due to timeout errors.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs only when Full Disk Encryption feature is configured and connection to kmip server exceeds 5 seconds due to network latency.
bugs.impact: It may not be possible to validate the operational status of KMIP servers.
bugs.workaround: You should evaluate connection latency and configure their KMIP servers so that the appliance can reach them within 5 seconds.
bugs.fix: Increased timeout value from 5 seconds to 10 seconds to improve connectivity with slow or distant KMIP servers. The execution of the "system disk-encryption validate-kmip" operation in ConfD will succeed, if the system is able to connect to KMIP servers with in 10 sec.

bugs.title: Max DNS entries supported are three, if more are configured the extras are ignored, and even after reducing to three, the previously ignored entries are not reapplied.
bugs.symptoms: The system supports a maximum of three DNS entries. When more than three are configured, the additional entries are ignored. However, after removing the extra entries and reducing the list to three, the previously ignored entries are still not added back to the system.
bugs.conditions: Configuring more than 3 DNS entries and removing previously added entries
bugs.impact: DNS resolution failure.
bugs.workaround: Recreate DNS entries

bugs.title: Changing LDAP configuration via the GUI results in an unexpected error
bugs.symptoms: Changing LDAP configuration on GUI errors out with the following error message - "object is not writable: /oc-sys:system/oc-sys:aaa/oc-sys:authentication/f5-aaa-ldap:ldap/f5-aaa-ldap:state"
bugs.conditions: When using a Windows Active Directory (AD) server and LDAP settings are configured with Active Directory authentication enabled (true) and Unix Attributes disabled (false).
bugs.impact: You are unable to make LDAP configuration changes via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Make the configuration change from CLI.
bugs.fix: GUI will not modify the read-only state part of the LDAP configuration and allow user to save the LDAP configuration changes.

bugs.title: On rSeries system, FIPS partition name should use escape sequence for special characters.
bugs.symptoms: Partitions are created with truncated names when the name contains a special character. appliance-1(config)# fips set-partition name T!est keys 1000 accel-devs 2 Value for 'so-password' (<string, min: 7 chars, max: 30 chars>): ******** result fips partition T has been created appliance-1(config)# exit appliance-1# show fips partitions OCCUPIED ACCEL FIPS SESSION SESSION PCI NAME KEYS DEVS BACKUP STATE KEYS COUNT ADDRESS ---------------------------------------------------------------- T 3100 2 disabled -1 0 0 c3:10.4 appliance-1#
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a partition -- Special characters like ; and ! are used in partition name.
bugs.impact: The partitions are not created with expected name.

bugs.title: PlatformStatsBridge process crash
bugs.symptoms: The PlatformStatsBridge process crashes on SIGSEGV, creates a core file. The associated Docker container goes into "Exited" state. SNMP failures and webUI errors occur, indicating the server or underlying service is unreachable.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs occasionally, when an snmp request tries fetching diskUsagePercentage on platform stats.
bugs.impact: The Docker container does not restart automatically as expected.
bugs.fix: The support for diskUsagePercentage MIB has been reverted.

bugs.title: Platform tcpdump omits egress traffic on a specified interface
bugs.symptoms: On F5OS-A, a platform tcpdump capture on a specified physical interface captures ingress traffic but omits egress traffic for the same flow.
bugs.conditions: - r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance - Platform-level tcpdump run against a specific physical interface, e.g. "system diagnostics tcpdump -i 3.0"
bugs.impact: Interface-specific platform packet captures are incomplete and cannot reliably confirm whether egress traffic reaches the F5OS dataplane, delaying network troubleshooting.
bugs.workaround: Capture on all interfaces (-i 0.0 / -i any) with a sufficiently narrow BPF filter. This captures both traffic directions but does not preserve interface-specific capture filtering.

bugs.title: Upon reaching maximum memory capacity, BIG-IP tenant pods intermittently regenerated after a host reboot
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Tenant Pods will keep restarting forever. On host(root access)# kubectl get pods Ex: # kubectl get pods NAMESPACE NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE default f5-resource-manager-jlv5q 1/1 Running 0 7h9m default virt-launcher-v171x-1-xnk5s 1/1 Running 0 2m15s ==========> default virt-launcher-v175x-1-24d9w 1/1 Running 0 2m4s ==========> default virt-launcher-new-183-tenant-1-2nz9q 0/1 Running 0 15s ===========> default virt-launcher-v151x-1-bqqr5 0/1 Init:0/1 0 2s The status of the BIG-IP tenants on F5OS user CLI might show as "Started Tenant Instance" but the tenants will not be accessible.
bugs.conditions: One or more tenants are configured to utilize all available memory and the host undergoes a reboot.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP tenants will not reachable. No impact to BIG-IP's data.
bugs.workaround: With root access to the F5OS host, run the below command on bash shell: # docker restart system_fpga after few(~5) min the BIG-IP tenants will be reachable.
bugs.fix: A command should be executed on F5OS with root privileges to recover the tenants from inaccessible state.

bugs.title: Dagd may crash if a malicious message is sent from the tenant
The anaconda-ssh service fails to start during installation phase, preventing remote SSH access
bugs.symptoms: SSH access is unavailable when using the inst.sshd boot parameter to enable remote debugging or Kickstart monitoring.
bugs.conditions: To enable SSH access and troubleshoot boot issues during the bare metal installation process.
bugs.impact: Blocks remote debugging over SSH during the bare metal installation process.
bugs.workaround: Need to trobleshoot through console only.
bugs.fix: Enabled the eno1 physical port and resolved the OpenSSL and OpenSSH compatibility.

bugs.title: The kdump service does not run at the anaconda installer phase
bugs.symptoms: The kdump service does not run in the installer phase.
bugs.conditions: The kdump service does not run in the installer phase.
bugs.impact: The kdump service does not run in the installer phase. The kernel crash cannot be troubleshot if it happens during baremetal installation.
bugs.workaround: If the kernel crashes during baremetal installation, Baremetal installation can be retriggered.

bugs.title: Older BIG-IP image import fails with signature verification
bugs.symptoms: The TMOS tenant images prior to certificate rotation fail to verify the signature. An error is logged: appliance-1.chassis.local image-agent[14]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x2002000000000010 msg="Failed to verify image signature. Removed." IMAGE="<image>.tar.bundle" FAILURE="signature".
bugs.conditions: Importing a BIG-IP tenant image that was released prior to certificates being rotated.
bugs.impact: You can't import the image. But images that were imported before the F5OS-A upgrade continue to work.
bugs.workaround: Import a BIG-IP tenant image which has had its certificates rotated.
bugs.fix: Updated the F5OS-A image verification to successfully verifies the TMOS tenant images contain certificate rotation.

bugs.title: init_etile: Cable check failed
bugs.symptoms: F5 rSeries Appliances may experience issues with port bringup when using an OPT-0036 in 4x10G bifurcated (breakout) mode. The system log will show an “init_etile: Cable check failed” message for one or more of the bifurcated ports. The system will not be able to establish a link on the port and the port status will remain down.
bugs.conditions: rSeries Appliance using an OPT-0036 in 4x10G breakout mode running F5OS-A-1.8.3 or earlier.
bugs.impact: Port remains down.
bugs.workaround: None. Requires F5OS update.
bugs.fix: Fixed in F5OS-A-1.8.3-25023-EHF-6 and later.

bugs.title: PSU inventory data shows "Not Available" on F5OS-A
bugs.symptoms: After PSU power test, F5OS reports PSU serial/part number as "Not Available" and shows empty state. Platform-hal logs "wrong common header format version: 0" and "wrong zero checksum 255 != 254" errors. PSU functions normally but inventory data unavailable.
bugs.conditions: Occurs after PSU power test/reseat PSU FRU EEPROM corrupted Failed to read the Seriel number.
bugs.impact: Incorrect PSU inventory display.

bugs.title: Packets destined to the Kubernetes API server may leave the rSeries appliance's management port on platform services shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Some packets destined to the internal Kubernetes API server may leave the system's management port towards the configured management gateway for up to 10 seconds during platform services shutdown or reboot. These packets will be destined to an IP address in the internal network range on TCP port 6443, by default 100.64.0.0/12 (RFC6598).
bugs.conditions: Platform services are shutting down, typically during a system reboot.
bugs.impact: There is no known impact to system operation. Packets will no longer leave the management port once platform services start up again, which happens automatically on system startup. The small number of "leaked" packets may occasionally be observed in monitoring or logs from external systems such as firewalls.
bugs.workaround: The following workaround will stop the packets into management interface. As a root user need to add following dummy route. e.g. ip route add unreachable 100.64.0.0/12 metric 1000 table main Based on network prefix, the IP Address 100.64.0.0/12 need to be adjusted to relevant prefix.

bugs.title: Error message IDs for image-agent do not match those documented in the error catalog
bugs.symptoms: Some of the message ids logged by the image-agent service in platform log do not match the error message id in the catalog.
bugs.conditions: Looking up image-agent logs by ID in the error message catalog.
bugs.impact: This discrepancy makes it difficult to correlate system logs with documentation for troubleshooting and support.
bugs.fix: Updated the error catalog message IDs correctly.

bugs.title: Interface 8.0 on r2000 and r4000-series F5OS appliances does not join LACP LAG or transmit LLDP BPDUs after upgrade to F5OS-A 1.8.3
bugs.symptoms: - Interface 8.0 has an operational status of UP - Interface 8.0 does not join a LACP LAG. - Interface 8.0 does not transmit any LLDP packets. - Log messages similar to the following in the platform.log: nic-manager[8]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x720c000000000003 msg="Error NULL interface descriptor".
bugs.conditions: - Running an affected version of F5OS-A. - An r2000-series or r4000-series appliance. This issue does not affect r5000-, r10000-, or r12000-series appliances. - Interface 8.0 is in a LACP LAG.
bugs.impact: Interface 8.0 is not able to negotiate and join a LACP LAG
bugs.workaround: This issue is fixed in F5OS-A 1.8.3 EHF-1, which is available for download on MyF5: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/downloads?productFamily=F5OS&productLine=F5OS+Appliance+Software&version=1.8.3&container=1.8.3-EHF

bugs.title: After upgrading, system health shows "disk encryption" as unhealthy even when UEFI communication is successful
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from a version before 1.8.2 to version 1.8.2 or later, the system may incorrectly show "Disk Encryption" as unhealthy.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when upgrading from a version earlier than 1.8.2 to version 1.8.2 or later.
bugs.impact: System hardware health is incorrectly shown as unhealthy.
bugs.workaround: Reset the component attributes by calling below API as below: docker exec -it diag-agent psf run POST:components/reset component=appliance/hardware/drives/disk-encryption
bugs.fix: Component attributes have been updated to correctly reflect the actual system state.

bugs.title: Serial console access behavior
bugs.symptoms: Console access may be temporarily unavailable.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: Could affect maintenance operations.
bugs.workaround: Follow standard recovery procedures.
bugs.fix: Fixed

bugs.title: Multicast traffic can be dropped by Host DLF rate-limiter
bugs.symptoms: Multicast traffic from a tenant can be dropped by the host DLF rate-limiter, causing traffic loss.
bugs.conditions: Egress multicast traffic exceeding 2500 packets per second.
bugs.impact: Loss of multicast traffic.
bugs.workaround: Create a static FDB entry for the multicast MAC address.
bugs.fix: We changed the behavior of the FPGA code to remove multicast packets that miss the L2 table from being classified as DLF.

bugs.title: Prompt-statusd process occasionally cores
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the prompt-statusd daemon will core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur in prompt-statusd during normal operation.
bugs.impact: After core, service will restart the operation

bugs.title: TACACS External Authentication Failure after a software upgrade
bugs.symptoms: TACACS users are not able to login to the device.
bugs.conditions: TACACS+ server sends back an authorization reply with an auth status of 'PASS_REPL' (pass + *replace all attributes*) instead of 'PASS_ADD' (pass + *add* to attributes)
bugs.impact: TACACS users will be unable to log in when the server is configured under the specified conditions.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using PASS_REPL on Tacacs server.
bugs.fix: After upgrading device to latest EHF build, the issue is not reproduced.

bugs.title: The "system aaa tls config passphrase" command does not validate whether or not the new passphrase correctly decrypts the current key file
bugs.symptoms: If the GUI is configured to use a custom key and certificate ("system aaa tls config certificate" and "system aaa tls config key") and use an encrypted key file protected by a passphrase ("system aaa tls config passphrase"), the system fails to perform validation for subsequent changes to the passphrase (and the system is not decrypting and re-encrypting the key file).
bugs.conditions: -- System is configured to use a custom key and certificate for GUI access. -- They key is encrypted with a passphrase, and "system aaa tls config passphrase" is used to set this passphrase in F5OS. -- "system aaa tls config passphrase" is later used to change the passphrase, but the underlying key is not changed.
bugs.impact: -- Key migration fails -- HTTP GUI and API are rendered unusable
bugs.workaround: Using the CLI: -- Manually re-encrypt the key to use the new passphrase. OR -- Change the passphrase ("system aaa tls config passphrase") back to the one that matches they key.

bugs.title: Disabled ports or port mode mismatchs can cause bad register reads.
bugs.symptoms: When a Front panel port is disabled or the port mode is mismatched, it can cause incorrect register reads. This may manifest as port interface flapping on other unrelated ports.
bugs.conditions: Front Panel Port is disabled or a port mode mismatch, such as a 100GE optic installed when the port is configured for 40GE operating mode.
bugs.impact: The status on other interfaces may incorrectly show ‘down’ when the interface is ‘up’ or other unexpected behavior.
bugs.workaround: Enable all Front Panel ports, even those not in use, and ensure there are no port mode mismatches.
bugs.fix: Updated FPGA firmware is required for the fix.

bugs.title: Application level DOS via improper configuration of the look aside memory allocator.
Tenant outage caused by deletion of VLAN in the tenant and unassignment of the VLAN from F5OS
bugs.symptoms: When a VLAN inside the tenant is deleted and the VLAN is un-assigned from F5OS, a service for the tenant could be deleted. Deletion of service will cause an outage on the tenant. Here are the two log messages on F5OS datapath-cp-proxy[11]: priority="Info" msgid=0x5901000000000045 msg="Confd Event Update:" EVENT="DELETE_SERVICE_ID" FROM="CONFD" TENANTNAME="" ATSE=0 SUBMODULE=0. datapath-cp-proxy[11]: priority="Info" msgid=0x5901000000000034 msg="Service Instance Update Success." TENANTNAME="tenant-1" DOSGRP="[2]" SVCGRP="[7]" SVCID=22.
bugs.conditions: -- Deletion of the VLAN inside the tenant. -- Un-assignment of the same VLAN from the F5OS.
bugs.impact: Because the service is removed, all VLANs on that service will be inaccessible for the tenant and cause an outage in the tenant.
bugs.workaround: If a VLAN is going to be deleted from the tenant, first un-assign the VLAN inside the tenant from F5OS. Then after a 2 second delay, delete the VLAN inside the tenant.

bugs.title: K3s install fails if a weak SSH MAC algorithm is configured
bugs.symptoms: If a weak SSH MAC algorithm is configured (via "system security services service sshd"), K3s will fail to install.
bugs.conditions: -- Appliance. -- Weak SSH MAC algorithm configured.
bugs.impact: This can prevent upgrades or K3s reinstallations.
bugs.workaround: Configure a strong SSH MAC algorithm, e.g. hmac-sha2-256. In the CLI: config system security services service sshd config macs [ hmac-sha2-256 ] commit It is possible to configure multiple MAC algorithms, in which case the administrator should keep the stronger algorithms enabled as well.

bugs.title: DmaTenantTcpCopOperHdlr, couldn't find stats for tenant
bugs.symptoms: An error is found in platform.log platform-stats-bridge[10]: nodename=controller-1(p3) priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x4305000000000008 msg="" msg="DmaTenantTcpCopOperHdlr, couldn't find stats for tenant".
bugs.conditions: -- Tenant is in configured or not deployed completely -- tcp-cop stats are queried when there are not yet any stats. (show tenants tenant tcp-cop tcp-cop)
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The log message is logged at the error level and should be logged at the warning level.

bugs.title: The Virtual Server is not receiving traffic due to an incorrect VLAN update from F5OS platform
bugs.symptoms: When a specific native VLAN is configured for a port in virtual-wire, the incoming packets still arrive with VLAN ID 4094, while the Virtual Server expects traffic with the configured VLAN ID.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a specific native vlan on a port and then configuring it in virtual-wire.
bugs.impact: When enabling/disabling virtual-wire mode on a port with a configured native VLAN, the port default VLAN was being set with values (4094 for vwire enable, 4095 for vwire disable), ignoring any existing native VLAN configuration.
bugs.workaround: Once the virtual-wire is configured on the port, if the remove and re-add the native vlans to the interfaces, the hardware should get programmed correctly.
bugs.fix: Added a fix such that ensure native VLAN configuration is respected and preserved throughout the virtual-wire lifecycle.

bugs.title: FDB entries may expire when multiple entries hash to the same FPGA table index and traffic is intermittent
bugs.symptoms: L2/FDB entries may expire even when traffic is arriving at the FPGA of the Appliance or VELOS Blade.
bugs.conditions: L2 entries which internally hash to the same table index inside the FPGA can lead to the expiration of the entry when traffic is arriving on intervals of more than 30 seconds from that MAC address. On each interval, an age refresh message might be lost, leading to decrement the age of the entry on 30 seconds. When the entry reaches the last period it will expire, and then it will be re-learnt again.
bugs.impact: The expiration of the FDB entry can lead to Destination Lookup Failures that are rate-limited, i.e. traffic loss. Depending on the scenario this could lead to intermittent potential outages between the entry expires, and it is learnt again.
bugs.workaround: Create a static FDB entry for the MAC address that suffers expiration issues. See K000152328. Ensure that traffic from the MAC address expiring arrives continuously under 30 seconds intervals. Open a Support case and request an EHF.

bugs.title: Tenant Stuck in "INOPERATIVE" State with "Key Header Check Failures" in API Service Gateway Logs
bugs.symptoms: In rare instances, tenant deployment results in the tenant being stuck in "INOPERATIVE" state, with MCPD connection failures and "Key header check failed" error messages in logs.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs after performing a live installation and deploying a tenant
bugs.impact: Tenant functionality is disrupted, rendering key features and services inaccessible due to MCPD failure in the "INOPERATIVE" state.
bugs.workaround: Restart the API service gateway and ensure it does not log errors while retrieving the tenant unit keys. If the problem persists, restart the tenants. If the problem continues to persist after number of tenant restarts, deploy new tenant and load UCS.
bugs.fix: Resolved issues causing key header check failures during tenant deployment.

bugs.title: Tenant image upload failure when there is still sufficient space available
bugs.symptoms: Tenant image upload failure when there is still sufficient space available. You may see below error from logs "Disk usage exceeded threshold."
bugs.conditions: When there is sufficient space available, tenant image upload fails.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload tenant image
bugs.fix: Fixed in 2.0

bugs.title: RADIUS/TACACS+ Remote users other than 9000 GID login fails Intermittently
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently, RADIUS and TACACS+ remote users are unable to login with "No valid role group found in user groups."
bugs.conditions: 1. RADIUS or TACACS+ Authentication is enabled. 2. Users with GID 9000 (who are admins) are able to login 3. Users with other than 9000 are unable to login 4. File "/etc/libnss-udr/group" is not getting updated with other than admin roles.
bugs.impact: RADIUS and TACACS+ remote users other than 9000 GID login fails Intermittently

bugs.title: F5OS web UI fails to load upon refreshing the page
bugs.symptoms: After performing a live upgrade of F5OS, refreshing the browser while on the appliance/partition/controller web UI returns a "404 Not Found — The requested URL was not found on this server" error. The web UI does not recover until the browser navigates back to the root URL manually.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on F5OS-based platforms (chassis and appliances) when a user refreshes the browser page.
bugs.impact: Access to the webUI may be lost when the browser is refreshed.
bugs.fix: Added a client-side fallback in the F5OS http-server to redirect stale deep-link requests back to the application root on page reload.

bugs.title: WebUI Connection may be refused After Upgrading to version F5OS-A 1.8.3
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from version 1.5.3 to 1.8.3, access to the WebUI is no longer available. All connection attempts result in a "connection refused" error.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when upgrading from v1.5.3 to v1.8.3
bugs.impact: WebUI becomes inaccessible.

bugs.title: Intermittent webUI startup failure after F5OS v1.8.x upgrade caused by SSL certificate generation issue
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases after upgrading to F5OS v1.8.x, the Web GUI (httpd) may fail to start. System logs may show a missing ServerName directive, and the /etc/auth-config/default/f5os.cert file may be missing or zero bytes.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur in certain scenarios where the upgrade process fails to properly generate or retain the f5os.cert certificate file, and the authentication-manager does not recover from the missing or empty certificate, resulting in an invalid httpd configuration.
bugs.impact: The webUI is completely unavailable. CLI and API access remain functional.
bugs.workaround: Restart the authentication-mgr and http-server services using the following CLI command: system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service authentication-mgr system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service http-server

bugs.title: LACP LAG interface stops forwarding packets when interface is disabled and re-enabled
bugs.symptoms: When an interface that is part of a LACP LAG is disabled and then re-enabled, the interface stops forwarding packets.
bugs.conditions: LACP LAG interface disabled and re-enabled.
bugs.impact: LACP LAG down since BPDU packets are not being captured.
bugs.workaround: A reboot re-enables packet forwarding on the interface.
bugs.fix: Restarting the appliance allows BPDU packet capture which fixes LACP.

bugs.title: Snmpwalk misses LAG interface stats intermittently
bugs.symptoms: Though the LAG interface is configured in system, some stats for the LAG interface will be missed in snmpwalk output intermittently.
bugs.conditions: Issue is rarely observed when running snmpwalk in a loop continuously.
bugs.impact: Snmpwalk may not display all statistics for the LAG interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Run snmpwalk after a 20 second delay.
bugs.fix: Ensured all LAG interface statistics are properly reported in SNMP walk output.

bugs.title: Long BIG-IP tenant names will prevent virtual console access
bugs.symptoms: Creating a BIG-IP tenant in the GUI with a name longer than 32 characters will prevent virtual console access to the tenant.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant name is longer than 32 characters.
bugs.impact: The creation of the tenant-console user fails, preventing access to the virtual console for that tenant.
bugs.workaround: Use tenant names that don't exceed 32 characters in length.

bugs.title: TLS client authentication for LDAP servers not working
bugs.symptoms: F5OS does not authenticate to LDAP servers.
bugs.conditions: - LDAP authentication in F5OS configured to use a client certificate and key ("system aaa authentication ldap tls_cert" and "system aaa authentication ldap tls_key"). - Either or both of the following: -- An LDAP group mapping is configured (ldap-group specified for a role) -- Active Directory enabled and Unix Attributes disabled
bugs.impact: F5OS is unable to connect to the LDAP server

bugs.title: Enable login-attribute to work with UPN based authentication in F5OS
bugs.symptoms: Authentication using userPrincipalName is not enabled by default in F5OS.
bugs.conditions: In F5OS, When configured active_directory to true and trying to authenticate the user with userPrincipalName instead of sAMAccountName will fail.
bugs.impact: Authentication using userPrincipalName will fail in F5OS for active directory based remote authentications.
bugs.workaround: 1. Configure login-attrribute to userPrincipalName from ConfD CLI as below: system aaa authentication ldap login-attrribute userPrincipalName 2. For client based UPN authentication - a. Client Certificates should have been generated using UPN name b. Configure in which field we need to fetch username in confd via "system aaa authentication clientcert config client-cert-name-field" c. Configure login-attribute as userPrincipalName in confd via "system aaa authentication ldap login-attrribute userPrincipalName" Note: We can configure login-attribute via confd cli or restconf api. In this release there is no support to configure login-attribute from GUI.
bugs.fix: Added configurable parameter in confd to enable "userPrincipalName" based authentication.

bugs.title: Empty File path in upload api leads to core
bugs.symptoms: The utils-agent service crashes
bugs.conditions: Provide an empty file path to the upload api
bugs.impact: Utils-agent crashes and generates a core.
bugs.fix: Empty/Null check added for file path field in upload api to make sure no crash in utils-agent service.

bugs.title: F5OS image import fails with 'Signature verification failed' error
bugs.symptoms: When F5OS ISO certificates were rotated for the first time in October 2025, certificate validity was set to 6 months. Consequently, importing affected images fails after expiration. This issue is limited to image import.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when attempting to import an F5OS ISO image published on or before October 2025.
bugs.impact: F5OS ISO images published on or before October 2025 cannot be imported.
bugs.workaround: Use F5OS ISO images published after October 2025 for import.
bugs.fix: F5OS ISO certificate expiration period has been extended to 39 months.

bugs.title: Corrected Typo "tenanat" to "tenant" in Logging
bugs.symptoms: When searching log archives or examining journalctl outputs, the word "tenant" is misspelled as "tenanat" in log messages generated. This prevents support engineers and diagnostic tools from finding relevant log entries when searching or grepping logs for the keyword "tenant".
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on all supported platforms (including version A-1.8.3) when log entries are written by network-manager or appliance-network-manager.
bugs.impact: Although the spelling error is minor, it directly hinders supportability. Standard diagnostic tools, automated scripts, search queries, or grep commands targeting the word "tenant" will fail to locate these logging records. This can lead to frustration and extended troubleshooting times for support teams.
bugs.workaround: To locate these logs prior to applying the fix, search or grep for the misspelled term tenanat instead of tenant.

bugs.title: AOM and fan alarms persist on rSeries appliance persist after hardware replacement and cannot be cleared
bugs.symptoms: After replacing a faulty fan tray via RMA, critical fan and AOM fault alarms remain visible in show system alarms even though replacement hardware is operating normally and show system health reports all components as healthy. Standard docker alert-service clear commands fail to remove the stale alarms.
bugs.conditions: Fan tray hardware replaced via RMA Replacement fans operating correctly (>15K RPM, health status: ok)
bugs.impact: Persistent false-positive critical alarms create operational confusion and monitoring noise.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as root and run: docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert -n "<message>" -s <Resource> -r clear -se error -i <ID> -d "<Text>" If above does not clear it. 1. docker restart alert-service 2.docker exec alert-service /confd/test/sendAlert -n "<message>" -s <Resource> -r clear -se error -i <ID> -d "<Text>"

bugs.title: F5OS tpm-integrity-status is Unavailable on certain versions released since October 2025
bugs.symptoms: When you run show components component state tpm-integrity-status, the TPM integrity status reports "Unavailable" # show components component state tpm-integrity-status TPM INTEGRITY NAME STATUS ----------------------- platform Unavailable
bugs.conditions: -- Running the tpm-integrity-status command from F5OS-A or F5OS-C on rSeries or VELOS: - VELOS systems running F5OS-C versions 1.8.2, 1.8.2-EHF, or 1.6.4 - rSeries systems running F5OS-A versions 1.8.3, 1.8.3-EHF, or 1.5.4 - EHFs built after October 15, 2025, including EHFs posted to MyF5 downloads in October such as: - F5OS-A-1.8.3-23493.R5R10.EHF-1 - F5OS-C-1.8.2-28324.CONTROLLER.EHF-1 - F5OS-C-1.8.2-28324.PARTITION.EHF-1 -- The calendar date is on or after April 4, 2026
bugs.impact: The tpm-integrity-status output reads Unavailable after April 4th, 2026.
bugs.workaround: If it is before April 4, 2026, you can run 'show components component state tpm-integrity-status' to get the TPM status.

bugs.title: Tenant image upload silently fails
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios extra disk space is required for a tenant image. If there is enough space to upload the image, but not enough extra space, the operation will silently fail.
bugs.conditions: Enough disk space available to upload a tenant image, but not enough to copy it.
bugs.impact: Silent failure when uploading a tenant image.
bugs.workaround: Clear disk space by removing old tenant images, or resize the images volume.

bugs.title: Creating a new tenant shortly after deleting one with the same name fails intermittently
bugs.symptoms: Tenant creation will occasionally fail when creating a tenant with the same name as one that was recently deleted.
bugs.conditions: Deleting and then quickly recreating a tenant with the same time.
bugs.impact: Stale pod get left behind, consuming resources on the system and potentially blocking creation of additional tenants.
bugs.workaround: Allow more time between deleting and recreating a tenant with the same name.

bugs.title: [Windows AD] Secure LDAP / Basic LDAP is not working post toggling the active_directory flag True/False
bugs.symptoms: With Basic LDAP or Secure LDAP (LDAPS) integrated with Windows Active Directory, toggling the active_directory and unix_attributes flags causes LDAP authentication to stop working. Specifically: 1. The Windows AD Domain SID is not recreated after the toggle. 2. LDAP-authenticated users receive a 403 Forbidden error when accessing the REST API.
bugs.conditions: 1. F5OS-A/C is configured with Windows AD LDAP or Secure LDAP (LDAPS) authentication. 2. LDAP roles are mapped to AD groups using system aaa authentication roles. The active_directory flag is toggled from true -> false (and unix_attributes from false -> true), then toggled back.
bugs.impact: All remote LDAP users cannot authenticate via LDAP, and LDAP-authenticated users lose access to the management CLI and REST API.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed on F5OS-2.0.0 and F5OS-A-1.8.4

bugs.title: Packet loss on a F5OS tenant when vlan-groups are in use
bugs.symptoms: On an F5OS tenant, there may be packet loss when vlan-groups are in use. This occurs due to high churn inside the FDB table due to MAC addresses being learned between different host ports resulting in temporary DLF drops while the MAC is learned on the new port.
bugs.conditions: - BX520 blade - VLAN groups - A large amount of unique MAC addresses in the FDB table
bugs.impact: Packet loss. Failing monitor probes.
bugs.workaround: Monitor probe issues may be alleviated by creating a static FDB entry for the local admin bit flipped MAC address that TMM is egressing packets from.

bugs.title: LDAPS: DomainSID fails to populate intermittently when toggling Active Directory configuration with TLS client certificate and key
bugs.symptoms: After configuring LDAPs with a root certificate, TLS client certificate, and key, toggling the Active Directory or Unix attributes settings may cause the DomainSID to fail to populate for LDAP group accounts, resulting in authentication failures.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following CLI commands are executed to toggle LDAP Active Directory and Unix attributes settings: system aaa authentication ldap active_directory false system aaa authentication ldap unix_attributes true system aaa authentication ldap active_directory true system aaa authentication ldap unix_attributes false
bugs.impact: Users in LDAP groups mapped to F5OS roles will experience authentication failures.
