bugs.workaround: Restart the authentication-mgr service using the following CLI command: system diagnostics os-utils docker restart node platform service authentication-mgr

bugs.title: Platform-diag-agent process consuming more memory
bugs.symptoms: The diag-agent service running on the service seems to consuming more memory over the time due to runtime memory leaks leading OOM on system.
bugs.conditions: The diag-agent services receiving a burst of events at a time, leading to its queues being filled up with too many entries and raising the memory.
bugs.impact: Over the long time, if diag-agent receives event bursts again and again the service would end up consuming more memory from DUT.
bugs.workaround: If diag-agent service memory raised too much, restarting the diag-agent service before any OOM would free up the memory of device.

bugs.title: Superuser-bash users cannot execute virtctl or access tenant console after upgrade to F5OS-A 1.8.4
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to F5OS-A 1.8.4, superuser-bash users receive "Permission denied" when running virtctl to connect to tenant consoles. The error occurs both when running as the superuser directly and after running sudo su to root. SELinux audit logs show AVC denials for execute on /usr/local/bin/virtctl with source context staff_u:sysadm_r:sysadm_t and target context var_t.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure an rSeries appliance with F5OS-A-1.8.x-EHF. 2. Enable superuser-bash-access: system aaa authentication config superuser-bash-access true 3. Create a local user in the superuser role: $ system aaa authentication users user <name> config role admin ; top $ system aaa authentication roles role superuser config users <name> $ commit $ system aaa authentication users user <name> config set-password $ system aaa authentication users user <name> config last-change 2026-05-20 $ commit and-quit 4. Log in to the device with the above-created super user, then run the commands below, and observe the failure patterns ex: ssh <super-user>@<mgmt-ip> $ sudo su $ virtctl console <tenant-VMI-Name>
bugs.impact: Operators who previously used superuser-bash access to manage tenant consoles via virtctl can no longer do so. It breaks the primary workflow for superuser-bash users to access the tenant console.
bugs.workaround: Log into the system as root and change the SELinux context for /usr/local/bin/virtctl: semanage fcontext -a -f f -t bin_t '/var/usrlocal/bin/virtctl' restorecon -F /var/usrlocal/bin/virtctl
bugs.fix: Registered a persistent SELinux file context rule (bin_t) for /var/usrlocal/bin/virtctl using the actual filesystem path. This rule is seeded at ISO build time and refreshed during upgrades and reboots via platform-deployment.

bugs.conditions: The likelihood of an interface failing to come up increases as more interfaces are repeatedly enabled and disabled.
bugs.impact: Enabling an interface fails to bring the interface up.
bugs.workaround: 1. Stop the nic-manager container as well as the l2-agent docker stop system_L2 docker stop nic-manager 2. Ensure they are both stopped docker ps -a --filter "name=system_L2" docker ps -a --filter "name=nic-manager" ex. for l2-agent showing it as exited # docker ps -a --filter "name=system_L2" CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES d3c670d3dd12 localhost:2504/l2_agent:9.7.0-f5os-a-1-8-5-candidate.2026-05-12-09-14-19.S9547e872 "/confd/scripts/agent" 4 days ago Exited (1) 6 seconds ago 3. Then (re)start them docker start nic-manager docker start system_L2 4. And finally check that they are running. docker ps -a --filter "name=system_L2" docker ps -a --filter "name=nic-manager" ex. for system_L2 # docker ps -a --filter "name=system_L2" CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES d3c670d3dd12 localhost:2504/l2_agent:9.7.0-f5os-a-1-8-5-candidate.2026-05-12-09-14-19.S9547e872 "/confd/scripts/agent" 4 days ago Up 7 seconds system_L2

bugs.title: The superuser-bash users cannot perform ls and cat operations files from log/host/ paths
bugs.symptoms: Super users operating under the default SELinux staff_u:staff_r:staff_t context are unable to perform ls, cat, or similar file access operations on certain log and host paths due to SELinux policy restrictions
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when a user attempts to access restricted log or host files while executing under the standard staff_u:staff_r:staff_t SELinux context. The restriction is present regardless of whether the user has a superuser role.
bugs.impact: Super users cannot list directories or view files within protected log and host locations, resulting in permission denied errors.
bugs.fix: Updated the SELinux policy to allow users running under the staff_u:staff_r:staff_t context to access approved log and host paths.

bugs.title: F5 r5K/10K device second PSU reports phantom/stale without PSU connected
bugs.symptoms: F5 r5K/10K device shows phantom/stale PSU data in confD CLI when a PSU is removed from a device.
bugs.conditions: - PSU device is removed from the F5 r5K/10K device.
bugs.impact: Misleading PSU info is showed in confD CLI for the unavailable/removed PSU device.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fixed

bugs.title: AOM fault alarm is not raised, when LOP health checks failed
bugs.symptoms: The system does not raise an AOM fault alarm when Loss of Power (LOP) health checks fail. No alarm appears in the show system alarms output, even when LOP health check failures are detected.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under all conditions when LOP health checks fail. No specific configuration or trigger is required to reproduce the issue.
bugs.impact: LOP health check failures go undetected through the alarm system. Without an alarm, you may not be aware of potential power-related issues affecting the Always-On Management subsystem.
bugs.fix: The 'aom-fault' alarm now triggers when LOP health checks fail.

bugs.title: Cron entries after the first one in file do not run
bugs.symptoms: A scheduled cron job that previously worked stops running after upgrading to a version containing the fix for ID1185573 and ID1994869. The job is still listed by "crontab -l" and works when run by hand, but never executes on schedule, with nothing logged.
bugs.conditions: -- A user-defined crontab (e.g., root's crontab) or an /etc/cron.d file containing more than one schedulable entry. -- The entry that fails to run is any entry after the first in that file.
bugs.impact: User-defined scheduled jobs silently fail to run after upgrade unless they're the first entry in the crontab file. Failure is silent: the job is present in "crontab -l", runs correctly when invoked manually, and produces no errors or SELinux denials. System-managed (F5-owned) crontabs are NOT affected.
bugs.workaround: Place the required job as the FIRST entry in the crontab (or in its own single-entry /etc/cron.d file). This is a positional workaround only and is fragile - adding further entries, or any reordering, will cause later entries to silently stop running again.

bugs.title: DMA-Agent crashes while trying to disable a Service Endpoint (SEP) that is already disabled
bugs.symptoms: The DMA-Agent process crashes with an assertion failure ("Assertion Failed: FALSE"), causing ATSE data movers to stop unexpectedly. Affected tenants may become unresponsive or experience a service interruption. The crash occurs after an SEP (Service Endpoint) has been successfully enabled and a subsequent disable operation is issued against a SEP that is already in a disabled state.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on F5OS v2.1.0 across all supported platforms. The condition is triggered when the DMA-Agent receives a request to disable an SEP that has already been disabled. For example, during tenant lifecycle operations or automated service recovery sequences where redundant disable commands may be issued against the same SEP.
bugs.impact: When this issue is triggered, the DMA-Agent crashes and all associated ATSE data movers are stopped, resulting in a loss of tenant data-plane traffic processing. This is a critical-severity issue that can cause an unplanned tenant outage requiring manual intervention or a service restart to restore normal operation.
bugs.workaround: No workaround available. If the crash occurs, restart the DMA-Agent and affected tenants to restore service. Avoid initiating rapid or repeated tenant disable operations in close succession to reduce the likelihood of encountering this issue.

bugs.title: F5OS does not send LAG information to tenant when LAG is configured with virtual wire
bugs.symptoms: No LAG objects available in tenant.
bugs.conditions: LAG configured with virtual wire, and virtual wire is configured on a tenant.
bugs.impact: No LAG objects available in tenant.

bugs.title: Intermittent traffic failures when tenant is running BIG-IP v17.5.1.6 or above and host is on version prior to F5OS-A 1.8.0 or F5OS-C 1.8.0
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent traffic failures for a tenant running BIG-IP v17.5.1.6 or above This often manifests as ICMP monitors failing
bugs.conditions: - Tenant running BIG-IP v17.5.1.6 or above - Host is one of the following platforms: - r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance - VELOS - Host is running a version prior to F5OS-A 1.8.0 (rSeries appliance) or F5OS-C 1.8.0 (VELOS chassis)
bugs.impact: Intermittent traffic disruption. This often manifests as ICMP monitors intermittently failing, but it will also impact virtual server traffic and other protocols (e.g., UDP and TCP)
bugs.workaround: Upgrade F5OS to version 1.8.0 or higher

bugs.title: SNMP GET-NEXT/BULK on F5-PLATFORM-STATS-MIB cpu tables may cause daemon stall or genErr.
bugs.symptoms: Under SNMP polling of cpuUtilizationStatsTable or cpuCoreStatsTable OIDs, the platform-stats-bridge daemon may stall on a GET-NEXT operation. The SNMP session hangs until the UDP socket times out (~2 minutes), returning genErr. The daemon does not crash but the SNMP walk does not progress past the stalled OID.
bugs.conditions: High system load or slow internal agent responses can cause SNMP walk requests to time out prematurely, resulting in incomplete SNMP monitoring data and genErr errors.
bugs.impact: The SNMP polling will not be successful and returns genErr on SNMP Manager
bugs.workaround: Reduce the frequency or polling rate of SNMP GET-NEXT walks on the system. Lowering the poll rate decreases load on the internal monitoring service, significantly reducing the likelihood of hitting timeout errors. Also, use snmp polling command with extended timeout option
bugs.fix: Improved SNMP CPU statistics handling to prevent duplicate transaction responses and index corruption during timeouts. The system now runs SNMP walks, ignores late responses, and includes additional safeguard checks to ensure consecutive OIDs complete successfully.

bugs.title: Tenant image or F5OS ISO upload fails with "Copy failed" error in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When uploading a tenant image or F5OS ISO via the GUI file utility, the upload fails with a "Copy Failed" error message. Logs for utils-agent show: msg="file upload error" error="Failed to move file to destination path" msg="File change path failed, so deleting the uploaded file."
bugs.conditions: User attempts to upload tenant image or F5OS ISO using the GUI file utility feature
bugs.impact: Admin cannot upload tenant images or F5OS ISO files via the GUI. Uploaded file is automatically deleted by the system after the failed move operation.
bugs.workaround: You may select one of the following options below: 1. Use GUI Import instead of Upload — In the F5OS GUI, use the Import function (import via URL from an accessible repository) rather than Upload. 2. Use SCP to push the file directly to the F5OS system.
bugs.fix: Tenant or F5OS ISO images successfully upload.

bugs.title: Force recognition of select optic modules.
bugs.symptoms: F5 software uses the Ethernet Compliance Code in the optic modules eeprom to initialize the optic module. Some unsupported optics do not include the proper compliance code. This leads to in-complete initialization.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when using unsupported optics which do not include the Ethernet Compliance Code in the optic modules eeprom.
bugs.impact: Optics that do not include the Ethernet Compliance Code in the optic modules eeprom do not initialize correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use an F5 supported optic or an unsupported optic that includes the Ethernet Compliance Code.
bugs.fix: A change was added to F5 software to recognize and initialize select optics that don't include the Ethernet Compliance Code in the module eeprom.

bugs.title: SELinux denials for SSH faillock access after version downgrade from 2.1.0 to 1.8.4 HR-2
bugs.symptoms: After downgrading from F5OS 2.1.0 to F5OS-A-1.8.4 HR-2, SELinux audit logs may report that sshd was denied permission to open /var/log/faillock/root. SSH authentication attempts made during system startup may fail while authentication configuration is being regenerated.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur after a live downgrade from 2.1.0 to 1.8.4 HR-2, when SSH connections are attempted shortly after boot before the authentication-manager startup has completed regenerating the PAM configuration.
bugs.impact: SSH authentication attempts during the startup window may fail. SELinux AVC denials may be recorded for sshd accessing /var/log/faillock/root. The issue is transient and related to startup timing.
bugs.workaround: Wait for authentication-manager startup to complete, then retry SSH authentication.
